optional.text: Brief the media on a successful cutover, with pre-prepared executive remarks
Issue an announcement on the stock exchange regarding the successful cutover

nuances.text: Cutover of employees including data and official employment status may also have to take place, with onboarding onto Absa systems

artefacts.text: Approved cutover runbook, including a time-sequenced plan: activities, owners, dependencies, control gates, and completion criteria (Absa transaction specific)

stages.title: Hypercare
stages.purpose: Stabilise the transferred assets and liabilities and ensure everything in-scope has been transferred completely and accurately.

role.text: Monitor a consolidated view of incidents post cutover, and monitor the Hypercare team's triage and remediation efforts
Support the Hypercare team in escalating issues through agreed governance in order to prevent any financial, regulatory or client harm
Assess readiness to exit Hypercare using an agreed checklist and criteria, coordinating a formal handover to BAU
Lead regular updates to executives on tracking of strategic and financial outcomes

timelineDrivers.text: Number of clients transferring (additional clients means Additional time required to triage and resolve issues)
Capacity within Hypercare team (smaller team takes longer to resolve issues)
Complexity of transfer (a transfer of complex clients with complex products likely requires more dedicated service time)
Success of cutover (issues on cutover mean an extended Hypercare period will likely be needed to stabilise clients and resolve issues)

necessary.text: Set up a dedicated team to monitor client queries, feedback, and complaints from only the transferred population
Triage issues for remediation, add them to a backlog, and flag with technology / BAU teams as required
Escalate persistent or P1 issues immediately, through a dedicated escalation pathway
Stand up and coordinate war-rooms as necessary to remediate P1 issues quickly and avoid disruption
Set up dedicated client communications teams to ensure clients remain in the loop post LD1
Set up dedicated documentation remediation teams to quickly source outstanding documentation which could not be received pre-LD1
Gradually hand off servicing to BAU teams by transitioning issue resolution and triage into the BAU process, prioritising only the most serious issues for Hypercare as time passes
Track deal objectives such as revenue, asset/liability transfer, volumes, etc. as soon as LD1, and provide updates to executives on progress against objectives
Hold daily touchpoints with AEs to flag the most important issues and discuss remediation plans
Hold regular touchpoints with client-facing teams to discuss client sentiment and assess action plans

conditional.text: Set up a Hypercare centre for transferred employees, as a dedicated channel for any procedural, technical, or facilities-based issues
Leverage seller capacity and knowledge to support Hypercare for systems which have transitioned from seller to buyer

optional.text: Reach out to clients directly to assess sentiment

nuances.text: Hypercare systems may also be set up to support employees
Seller knowledge may be required to support Hypercare for transferred systems/technologies

artefacts.text: Transferred portfolio of clients (Absa transaction specific)

lifecycles.variantLabel: Variant A · Buyer integrates the business
lifecycles.sourceTitle: Full Business Acquisition A (Buyer integrates the business)

stages.title: Due Diligence
stages.purpose: Determine whether the acquisition creates value, what you are actually buying, and what needs to be protected contractually. Legal & CorpDev lead; other areas input where required. Activities below relate to key items for the integration team to consider during this process, they do not override current DD processes

role.text: Extract information from the DD process necessary to properly plan and run the implementation
Act as M&A SMEs to provide oversight, bringing a practical, Absa oriented lens which goes beyond financials and ensures nuances are identified and caught based on previous experience

timelineDrivers.text: Acquired firm's product set (broader product set requires more detailed review, e.g., inclusion of intellectual property, branding, technology systems, etc)
Maturity of DD teams (experienced teams can work through a DD checklist in a very short period)
Seller availability (heavily reliant on seller supporting in providing materials)

necessary.text: Ensure virtual data room set up to access confidential documentation and ensure it persists after deal signature
Ensure an NDA process to wall-cross those who need access to confidential information is set up
Understanding what the hurdle rates are: what EBITDA, NII, NIM, revenue, operating leverage, ROC, ROE, MOIC, will create a go-decision for deal signing?
Understanding the factors which influenced these hurdle rates, as well as what other non-financial factors may influence decision making (new capabilities, strong brand loyalty, etc)
Build an initial view of project implementation costs, leveraging comparable deals. All assumptions in planning costs must be defensible and informed by functional experts
Build or oversee build of a detailed business case comparing forecasted benefits to project costs and continued running costs
Ensure DD has accounted for and documented all legal entities, subsidiaries, branches, and ownership structures to inform execution operating model
Ensure DD has documented the effectiveness of governance, risk management, and internal controls
Ensure DD includes assessment of management capability, organisational health and cultural compatibility to inform change management activities required
Ensure subject matter experts are engaged to conduct cyber, technology, security, compliance DD to ensure that a deep understanding of these elements is gained during DD, to inform accurate planning
Ensure subject matter experts are engaged to conduct DD on the overall operational health of the business in areas such as brand value, intellectual property value, goodwill, client sentiment, etc.
Support the DD team to develop the integration thesis, synergy case and target operating model options
Ensure tax implications have been assessed and remediation planned
Financial-crime review: assess KYC and AML requirements against regulatory requirements, and Absa standards
Coordinate a Day 1 readiness test, to see how the acquired capabilities will operate
Ensure that cost implication of the people movement has been assessed, and agree which will be protected from redundancy, leveraging capability mapping
Ensure total cost of ownership of transferring technology has been understood by leveraging seller provided information, and identify potential cost synergies
Ensure existing obligations of the selling legal entity are assessed, to inform execution
Ensure that the value of intangible assets is also considered and assessed
Ensure the integration thesis and synergy case is developed and drivers understood
Ensure Target Operating Model options are initially defined
Ensure product overlap and rationalisation opportunities are assessed
Ensure cultural compatibility and change requirements are assessed

conditional.text: Assess the requirement for TSAs from the seller, and the cost of these
Access to this early stage of the lifecycle may not always be possible given the broader business context, but it should be requested given its importance to execution

optional.text: Benchmark estimated performance against previous deals
Review lessons learnt from previous deals
Engage a subset of seller clients to assess current pain points and identify any potential deal red flags (e.g. compliance issues, pricing mismatches, in-scope technology issues)
Engage previous buyers of seller business to understand key seller-specific pain points to avoid (e.g., data sharing issues, client communication issues)

nuances.text: DD must account for shift of new business into Absa cost environment, including accounting for different fixed cost base, funding rates, etc
DD must account for business line synergies inherent in taking all of the business, and assess pricing elasticity (e.g., can acquired clients be easily repriced if Absa prices are higher)
DD must account for the acquisition of a full legal entity and its subsidiaries, assessing any outstanding obligations the entity has

artefacts.text: Previous transaction materials and lessons learnt (Absa transaction specific)

stages.title: Legal Drafting & Signature
stages.purpose: Ensure the Sale and Purchase Agreement (SPA) reflects reality of programme delivery, and enables execution. Legal & CorpDev lead, other areas input where required. Activities below relate to key integration considerations, they do not overwrite the current processes.

role.text: Ensure legals reflect execution reality, and timelines are realistic
Ensure legals include provisions which will support execution, such as data sharing
Ensure any go-live dates are based on realistic assumptions around regulatory approval and client onboarding timelines
Leverage lessons learned from previous deals to ensure legals address any historic pain points

timelineDrivers.text: Deal complexity (complex deals require additional protections and conditions)
Scale of employee transfer (significant employee transfer requires additional legals and schedule negotiation)
Technology ownership (addenda will be required to stipulate technology requirements)
Pre-signing alignment (pre-agree valuations and completion mechanisms will speed up drafting)
DD quality (high quality DD will allow defensible assumptions to be made in the legals, otherwise these will have to be assessed during this phase)
Regulatory complexity (multiple regulators across multiple jurisdictions increases complexity in drafting legals)
Branding and intangibles (transfer of ownership of branding and intangible assets requires addenda to be negotiated)

necessary.text: Engage external lawyers to lead SPA drafting and negotiation, informed by internal legal opinion
Convert DD findings into agreed transaction terms including valuation, adjustment principles, completion mechanisms, and payment terms
Ensure price, adjustments and effective transfer date are agreed
Coordinate and confirm the signing sequence between Absa, the seller and other parties
Document employee transfer, retention and knowledge-transfer obligations
Assess which items transfer from the seller to Absa automatically under agreed regulatory processes (e.g., Section 54), and which will have to be manually transferred
Detail novation processes for items not automatically transferring, whether independent legal opinions on contracts are required, and where liability sits during transfer
Set out the joint governance mechanisms across buyer and seller at a high level (e.g., the scheduling of joint Steering Committees, appointment of Transaction Directors from each party)
Set out joint escalation mechanisms for programme-level issues, as well as dispute resolution mechanisms
Set out stipulations and timings for the sharing of client data, including whether business cases are required, and what can and can't be shared ahead of regulatory approval
Set out conditions precedent for completion, including funds transfer, assets/liabilities transfer, regulatory approval, and board approval
Agree signatures required on each side
Set out completion date precedent on regulatory approval date(s), rather than a pre-agreed specific date
Set out a joint communications plan to clients from both buyer and seller, including timelines for when buyer can engage the clients
Define ownership and licensing of shared Intellectual Property
Detail technology maintenance requirements of the seller, and stipulations on major changes
Ensure that the SPA sets out the required regulatory change of controls approval
Ensure that SPA sets out provisions for employee transfer and consultations
Ensure that the SPA sets out brand transfer, consolidation or retirement stipulations

conditional.text: Detail seller hiring/redundancy stipulations whilst completion is in progress (e.g. maximum salary to be hired, redundancy processes)
Detail FX payment mechanisms, including adjustments for FX risk and longer settlement times
Ensure that the SPA details management retention requirements of the seller
Ensure that the SPA sets out any seller-group services which require TSAs after completion
Access to this early stage of the lifecycle may not always be possible given the broader business context, but it should be requested given its importance to execution

optional.text: Set SPA change control mechanisms
Set up SPA access mechanisms for project team members
Socialise with functional leads ahead of signature

nuances.text: SPA should account for any intellectual property or goodwill transfer
Any joint technology agreements should be attached as addenda
Data migration and client data provisions must be included, as the business will be integrated and migration will need to occur

artefacts.text: DD summary and agreed deal decisions (Absa deal specific)

stages.title: Mobilisation & Planning
stages.purpose: Define the key activities which must take place to enable LD1 to take place on the agreed date, and surface dependencies

role.text: Inorganic Change team should lead the mobilisation effort across Absa: briefing functional leads / AEs, onboarding teams, executing the NDA process, creating onboarding materials, briefing teams on detailed plan creation, leading joint planning workshops, translating workshop outputs into a programme plan

timelineDrivers.text: Deal complexity (complex deals need more workstreams to execute)
Geographical scope (multiple geographies require more coordination)
Existing knowledge (teams familiar with these deals can draft a detailed plan much faster, and understand dependencies)
Available resource (resource constraints mean activities take longer)

necessary.text: Set up mobilisation hierarchy:
subs: Board appoints executive sponsor for the deal
Transaction Director and Executive Sponsor agree Accountable Executives for each function / workstream
AE selection should be informed by their expected responsibilities, detailed in the Hub and Spoke Operating Model
AEs appoint functional workstream leads, who appoint in-country leads
Transaction Director mobilises central Inorganic Change team and in-country coordinators
Buyer and Seller Inorganic Change teams share lists of functional leads to enable joint planning
Joint and individual governance established based on Mobilisation Toolkit

necessary.text: Define which items across the acquired party will be :
Define key workstreams required based on the deal-archetype and SPA specifics, including rough size of each workstream
Define workstream charters per workstream, setting out objective, purpose, success metrics, key personnel, skills, and ownership

Jointly carry out workstream blueprints across buyer and seller, laying out each business process related to the workstream, which the seller will stop, which the buyer will start, and which will carry on as is
Define key milestones required to enable these process and achieve a seamless cutover at Legal Day 1 (LD1)
Support each workstream to define a detailed, L2 plan below this to enable the meeting of these milestones
Hold joint workshops across buyer and seller to discuss and agree on these milestones
Identify milestones with key dependencies across workstreams, and document these dependencies in detail

Identify the critical path, and dates/factors will have a material impact on completion, and which of these can be controlled (e.g., regulatory approval or bank-wide change freezes cannot be controlled, client onboarding must take place ahead of LD1 but non-BAU processes can speed up timelines, data migration solution build and test is critical to LD1 success, etc)
Translate the milestones into an overarching project plan to be tracked weekly
Agree initial LD1 readiness criteria per workstream (key performance indicators which will enable cutover, e.g., for HR, 100% of consultations complete)
Agree on internal governance cadence which will sync with joint governance laid out in the SPA, including:
subs: Internal and joint Inorganic Change meetings weekly / bi-weekly to align on priorities and joint risks/issues
Working group / workstream led sessions to discuss key risks, issues, and progress
Internal Steering Committee sessions to escalate Absa-specific risks and issues, and receive guidance on key decisions
Joint Steering Committee sessions to discuss joint risks and issues, and coordinate cross-party solutions

necessary.text: Translate DD findings and governance structures into onboarding materials which clearly articulate the purpose and objectives of the deal, how execution will run day to day, roles and responsibilities, and escalation pathways
Define Day 1 control and ownership plan
Define plan for executive and board transition, as well as a joint management retention plan
Create a detailed workstream plan for employee and technology transfers

conditional.text: Define target operating model activities to take place ahead of LD1, informed by the level of integration agreed
Define a cultural integration and change management plan to properly integrate new business as required
Define a plan for Absa policy and control adoption
Agree a financial and regulatory consolidation plan
Create a brand transition plan
Submit a version of the programme plan to the regulator alongside the request for approval
Set up TSA exit team and define timeline for complete TSA exit

optional.text: Translate the project plan into project management software (e.g., Jira, MSP)
Link governance into bank-level governance such as Board meetings, StratCos, etc

nuances.text: Planning for this archetype will be the most complex, given that full scale integration must take place across seller and Absa

artefacts.text: Regulatory commitments and approval timelines (Absa transaction specific)
Previous transaction playbooks with lessons learned (Absa transaction specific)

stages.title: Programme Execution
stages.purpose: Execute on agreed milestones, run governance cadence, and build required technical/data solutions

role.text: Inorganic Change Team acts as the central hub in the execution phase, driving workstream level execution, tracking RAID items, defining SteerCo material, and holding those responsible for execution accountable

timelineDrivers.text: Regulatory change of control approval timelines
Deal scope complexity (if the target has complex products, legal entity structures, technology assets, people transfer, intellectual property transfer, etc. timelines may be extended)
Seller cooperation (early sharing of data, and daily cooperation speeds up timelines)

necessary.text: Conduct programme management activities: run governance processes including workstream sessions, Exec SteerCos, and Joint Buyer/Seller SteerCos; set up and track risks and issues in a central RAID log, and escalate to SteerCo as appropriate
Align risk appetite, policies, controls, and assurance of the acquired firm
Integrate and rationalise product sets aligned to the programme plan
Provide regular updates to the Board and Bank Leadership Forums on progress against plan, key risks and issues, and LD1 viability
Engage the regulator regularly to update progress and assess approval timelines
Conduct contingency and scenario planning for if approvals arrive later than anticipated, and define final possible date for receipt before LD1 must move
Build out detailed client communication plan across buyer and seller, and keep clients updated on the progress of the programme, and when they can expect to be onboarded
Request that the seller shares a data dictionary detailing data structures across source systems
Define success criteria across all workstreams, and continually measure progress against these
Work with the seller to receive regularly updated financials, update the business case, and track that the deal remains aligned to strategic objectives
Define a target operating model for once new employees land – define design principles, key roles and responsibilities, skills assessment, and target state structure
Ensure joint technology specifications with the seller defined (e.g., Joint Application Development (JAD) documentation, API documentation, technical requirements, business requirements)
Agree and execute a joint technology build governance structure to drive joint progress
Ensure transferring employee packages defined and socialised through consultations
Consolidate financial and management reporting
Implement culture and change activity plan
Decommission duplicated systems and processes
Ensure source-to-target mapping across all systems is conducted to enable build of core data migration solution
Drive the build of the data migration solution to Extract, Transform, and Load (ETL) solution across all source systems into target systems
Ensure the data migration solution is tested using dummy data aligned to the data dictionary, or where possible, real client data

conditional.text: Agree with the seller what data can be transferred ahead of LD1, and load it into Absa systems early to avoid cutover complications
Ensure provisions are made for capital, liquidity, treasury, and funding requirements should these be integrated into Absa
If TSAs are in place, monitor service delivery and exit planning
Define a plan to rationalise supplier, premises, and shared services
Manage the brand transition should the brand be transferring into Absa, or branding be wound down

optional.text: Engage friendly clients during the process to assess key value proposition and ensure project execution remains aligned
Conduct change management activities for project execution teams to drive continued buy-in and morale (e.g., team socials, rewards, etc)

nuances.text: Execution focus in an integrated archetype such as this is on data migration, product build, target operating model design, etc. Execution of this deal type can be expected to be the most complex and largest scale across archetypes
Suppliers, services, premises must be rationalised

artefacts.text: Detail project plan built out from mobilisation and planning stage (Absa transaction specific)
Previous project playbooks with lessons learnt (Absa transaction specific)

templates.text: Joint buyer and seller status report template
Programme RAID log template with added SteerCo escalation if necessary

stages.title: Business Testing
stages.purpose: Confirm that clients, products, data, technology and processes will operate correctly within Absa and that required controls remain effective

role.text: Inorganic Change Team role is to coordinate and govern testing across business and technology teams, not to perform testing itself.

timelineDrivers.text: Scale of business process change
Level of integration
Testing expertise in-house (testing SMEs within each team means scripts require less review and testing can happen faster)
Capacity within teams to accommodate testing (needs to be balanced with BAU, build, other deal-related work)
Complexity of process change (complex new systems or products require significant testing)
Downstream systems (impact of changes on multiple downstream systems requires more extensive end-to-end testing)

necessary.text: Work with BAU teams and functional / product SMEs to detail every business process impacted by changes the programme has made
Work with technology teams to understand the requirements for testing environments, including end-to-end environments
Testing should focus on:
Book these environments well in advance, or flag if suitable environments do not yet exist and must be built
Set up an independent testing team to liaise with business and technology to drive test script creation and sign off
Designate a testing lead within each workstream responsible for coordinating and executing tests assigned to them
Drive execution of test scripts by the business, with oversight from the testing team
Conduct negative testing to ensure controls are functioning as expected
Once individual processes are validated, test every process end-to-end, including the feed into downstream systems like AML, finance, and HR systems
Set up a testing-specific defect log to track issues to closure
Re-test issues post closure end-to-end, to ensure the fix has not created additional issues
Conduct Production Validation Testing to check that new functionality works in production as well as in test environments
Set up testing-specific governance, and feed into programme governance
Secure executive and business sign off on testing closure, with any open items clearly detailed
Test the flow of data into HR systems such as Workday
Conduct testing to ensure decommissioning efforts have been successful

conditional.text: Business process change related to additional products, assets, liabilities, and data being integrated will need to be tested

optional.text: Conduct friendly client testing to ensure that end-to-end flows work in a real world scenario

nuances.text: Full end-to-end migration testing is needed where systems, products or clients move at LD1. Later migrations should have their own testing and rehearsal cycles
Testing is especially critical when full-scale integration is taking place, as in this archetype, as the scale of business process change is likely to be significant

artefacts.text: Previous business testing programmes with lessons learnt, including a scenario-based risk mitigation plan (Absa transaction specific)
Business testing process flows and customer journeys (Absa transaction specific)

stages.title: Client Onboarding & LD1 Readiness
stages.purpose: Onboard and migrate clients to the agreed Absa products, platforms, channels and service model while maintaining continuity

role.text: Oversee the standing up of an LD1 Readiness stream, and tracking its progress and risks as part of programme management to assess critical risks to LD1

timelineDrivers.text: Scale of client transfer (more clients require communication and training)
Complexity of client product mix (complex products and multi-product portfolios increase time to onboard)
Availability of client data (high-quality client contact data removes time spent on remediation)
Client responsiveness (heavily reliant on clients responding to outreach and providing documentation)

necessary.text: Ensure client contact details are shared by seller as early as possible, and track client outreach, and monitor potential client attrition.
Conduct risk assessment to understand which clients are high risk, and which some documentation can be obtained post-LD1
Confirm required KYC / AML documentation in place across transferring clients
Define and test the updated service model
Define the Hypercare model for post go-live, including detailed roles and responsibilities
Identify client contracts containing change-of-control provisions, and determine notification and consent requirements
Confirm that accounts, products, mandates and channels continue functioning
Assess whether branding or legal disclosures must change
Confirm continuity of complaints, conduct and servicing arrangements
Prepare future product migration and cross-sell plans
Assess in detail the client onboarding process, understand timelines, and define a 'drop-dead date' for when onboarding must begin
Assess which onboarding processes must be done BAU, and which can be adapted to suit deal context and timelines
Detail all client documentation required to enable onboarding
Perform gap analysis to understand which information can be sourced from the seller, and which clients must provide directly
Conduct employee training as required
Train existing clients on new systems being built as part of the deal
Build training materials, working closely with business SMEs
Build out materials outlining the value proposition of Absa to new clients, including for products which they do not yet have to drive cross-sell opportunities
Set up sessions to train clients on bank systems and channels
Set up client accounts, profiles, products, permissions, and mandates ahead of time to enable Dress Rehearsals and testing
Begin the implementation of the Target Operating Model within Absa

optional.text: Onboard some clients early to conduct friendly-client testing with new to bank clients

nuances.text: The importance of this phase increases in this archetype, as all clients will need to be onboarded onto Absa systems which requires significant operational, organisational, logistical, and technological effort

stages.title: Dress Rehearsals
stages.purpose: Testing end-to-end approach to cutover in order to raise and resolve any issues which would prevent a successful transfer

role.text: Coordinate the logistical preparation of the DRs, support the Data Migration team in defining the runbook, support the execution of the DRs either as logistical support or by acting as Data Migration Coordinators (DMCs).

timelineDrivers.text: Time remaining post build and test (if build and test finishes well ahead of LD1, more DRs can take place)
Number of Dress Rehearsals (DRs) (more DRs require a longer timeframe)
Down-time between DRs (minimum 2 weeks between DRs is recommended)

necessary.text: Work with the Data Migration and Technology teams to define cutover plan which details every activity down to the minute required to wind down the seller and stand up the business within Absa
Hold runbook run-through sessions with all activity owners and back-ups to ensure everyone is clear on expectations
Define success metrics for DRs, with a clear understanding of what is acceptable in the first DR vs the final DR
Agree which data sets will be dummy / anonymised, and which will be real client data
Define roles and responsibilities across DRs and Cutover, including Data Migration Controllers running the runbook
Execute logistical support required to enable 24/7 DRs to take place such as building access, food requirements, accommodation, travel, Wi-Fi, security, facilities, and back-up plans

Define the governance processes to take place during DRs including the command centre, regular executive updates, escalation pathways, war room protocols, issue resolution processes, and continency decision making
Collate a DR playbook summarising success criteria, logistical information, key contacts, governance processes, and timelines
Run a minimum of 4 DRs across weekends, with at least 2 weeks in between each
Each DR should execute the runbook end-to-end, and track issues which arise for remediation
Hold DR retros to note lessons learnt and iterate into subsequent DRs
Track the remediation of issues ahead of subsequent DRs
Ensure DRs test the data migration process end to end, as well as all downstream activities such as reconciliations, operations processes, financial reporting, AML, etc

conditional.text: Ensure DRs test the interactions and flows between multiple acquired products and services

optional.text: Hold a 'Technical DR' before the true DRs take place, to test only the migration solution, and ensure this is not a blocker to future DRs

nuances.text: Full DRs must take place, and should be prioritised due to the scale of data transferring in this archetype
Any migrations planned post-completion should hold separate DRs

artefacts.text: Approved DR strategy: this will cover DR scope, sequencing, success measures and rehearsal cadence (Absa transaction specific)
Previous DR completion records with timestamps, success measure results and lessons learnt (Absa transaction specific)

stages.title: Go/No-Go
stages.purpose: Formally discuss and approve/disapprove whether all workstreams and parties are sufficiently ready to proceed with transfer and integration

role.text: Drive the collation of evidence across execution, testing, and DRs to present a case for a Go/No-Go decision to the Steering Committee. Liaise with functional leads and AEs to ensure they can clearly state the recommendation of their area.

timelineDrivers.text: Likelihood for a no-go (no-go decisions require additional justification and discussion)
Existing evidence (if evidence has to be specially sourced and collated, timelines may increase)
SPA stipulations (some SPAs stipulate when Go/No-Go decisions must take place, and how long discussions may last)

necessary.text: Assess the success of DRs, and confirm that all issues from the final DR have been remediated or have clear timelines for remediation
Ensure that at least one successful end to end DR has taken place
Discuss residual risks and mitigation plans across each workstream, with each AE laying out in turn testing results, DR success, and residual risks related to their area
For each residual risk, lay out the potential risk to go-live, likelihood, and mitigation plans
Gather evidence that key conditions have been met such as:
subs: Data extraction and reconciliation in DRs
Absa and seller obligations as stipulated in the SPA

necessary.text: Gather all AEs / SteerCo members to formally make and document the Go/No-Go decision internally, allowing any reservations to be noted and addressed
Gather buyer and seller AEs to formally make the joint Go/No-Go decision
Formally document go/no position with the Seller and communicate to clients, employees, and regulators

conditional.text: TSA readiness may also be a decision factor should these be in place

optional.text: Announce the decision on the local stock exchange to ensure clients / market is aware (e.g., SENS announcement)
Brief the media on the decision, with a series of prepared remarks

nuances.text: As the business will be integrated, the Go/No-Go decision criteria will be especially numerous and thorough, given the scale of integration taking place

artefacts.text: Go/No-Go criteria (owned by Inorganic Change Team to use throughout this decision making process)
M&A Learning Academy materials on governance and decision rights

stages.title: Cutover
stages.purpose: Execute a controlled and approved change of control event and integration of the entire acquired entity into Absa

role.text: Coordinate the logistical preparation of the cutover, based upon successful DR. Support the execution of the cutover
Run the central control function, coordinating buyer, seller and overseeing workstream execution, against approved runbook.
Coordinate cross-workstream dependencies and stakeholder communications through the cutover timeline.

timelineDrivers.text: Scale of activity required over cutover
Length of individual activities (some activities may last 24 hours + depending on their nature)
Length of time the bank can shut down without impacting service (some jurisdictions have payments flowing over the weekend, others do not)

necessary.text: Work with Data Migration and Technology to define the final cutover plan, iterated during DRs
Walk through the plan again with teams to confirm understanding, roles, and responsibilities
Sign off final cutover plan with all AEs
Coordinate contingency planning across all workstreams, gathering scenarios and planning for potential issues which may arise over the cutover
Define any additional governance to be in place during cutover vs DRs (e.g., additional executive updates, final decision gates, etc)
Execute on cutover plan, including agreed-upon governance gates
Execute on testing activities planned in the runbook to ensure all systems are working as planned
Hold final checkpoint to assess success of the cutover, and define required mitigation plans for issues
Open the bank after cutover activities completed and monitor core systems
Execute share transfer and financial settlement and transfer legal control
Consolidate the acquired firm into Absa financial reporting
Communicate with clients on the success of the cutover, and remind them of new channels into the buyer
Hold regular check-ins to ensure smooth transition to Hypercare
Execute on the employee onboarding cutover plan, ensuring new employees have necessary system and building access on LD1
Ensure data reconciles once loaded onto Absa systems, and flag any mismatches with the seller immediately

conditional.text: Communicate any residual issues to clients which remain post-cutover, and detail timelines for remediation
Activate TSAs where necessary

optional.text: Brief the media on a successful cutover, with pre-prepared executive remarks
Issue an announcement on the stock exchange regarding the successful cutover

nuances.text: As this archetype involves integration of the full business, cutover will be the most complex and highest risk, and should therefore have the most comprehensive runbook, governance, and contingency plans in place

artefacts.text: Approved cutover runbook, including a time-sequenced plan: activities, owners, dependencies, control gates, and completion criteria (Absa transaction specific)

stages.title: Hypercare
stages.purpose: Stabilise the migrated business, resolve integration issues and transition ongoing integration and synergy delivery into BAU ownership.

role.text: Monitor a consolidated view of incidents post cutover, and monitor the Hypercare team's triage and remediation efforts
Support the Hypercare team in escalating issues through agreed governance in order to prevent any financial, regulatory or client harm
Assess readiness to exit Hypercare using an agreed checklist and criteria, coordinating a formal handover to BAU
Lead regular updates to executives on tracking of strategic and financial outcomes

timelineDrivers.text: Number of clients transferring (additional clients means Additional time required to triage and resolve issues)
Capacity within Hypercare team (smaller team takes longer to resolve issues)
Complexity of transfer (a transfer of complex clients with complex products likely requires more dedicated service time)
Success of cutover (issues on cutover mean an extended Hypercare period will likely be needed to stabilise clients and resolve issues)

necessary.text: Set up a dedicated team to monitor client queries, feedback, and complaints from only the transferred population
Triage issues for remediation, add them to a backlog, and flag with technology / BAU teams as required
Monitor migration issues, product and platform stability, and onboarding issues
Drive target operating model adoption amongst servicing teams in the first instance, and embed new employees into front-line teams
Escalate persistent or P1 issues immediately, through a dedicated escalation pathway
Stand up and coordinate war-rooms as necessary to remediate P1 issues quickly and avoid disruption
Set up dedicated client communications teams to ensure clients remain in the loop post LD1
Set up dedicated documentation remediation teams to quickly source outstanding documentation which could not be received pre-LD1

stages.title: Mobilisation & Planning

Geographical scope (multiple geographies require more coordination)
Existing knowledge (teams familiar with these deals can draft a detailed plan much faster, and understand dependencies)
Available resource (resource constraints mean activities take longer)

subs: Board appoints executive sponsor for the deal

AEs appoint functional workstream leads, who appoint in-country leads
Transaction Director mobilises central Inorganic Change team and in-country coordinators
Buyer and Seller Inorganic Change teams share lists of functional leads to enable joint planning
Joint and individual governance established based on Mobilisation Toolkit

Define key milestones required to enable these process and achieve a seamless transfer of ownership at Legal Day 1 (LD1)

subs: Internal and joint Inorganic Change meetings weekly / bi-weekly to align on priorities and joint risks/issues

conditional.text: Define a plan for Absa policy and control adoption
Agree a financial and regulatory consolidation plan
Submit a version of the programme plan to the regulator alongside the request for approval
Set up TSA exit team and define timeline for complete TSA exit

optional.text: Translate the project plan into project management software (e.g., Jira, MSP)
Link governance into bank-level governance such as Board meetings, StratCos, etc

stages.title: Programme Execution

stages.title: Business Testing
stages.purpose: Standalone testing is narrower in operational scope but must provide sufficient assurance over governance, reporting, funding, access, controls and service continuity

role.text: Inorganic Change Team role is to coordinate and govern testing across business and technology teams, not to perform testing itself.

timelineDrivers.text: Testing expertise in-house (testing SMEs within each team means scripts require less review and testing can happen faster)
Capacity within teams to accommodate testing (needs to be balanced with BAU, build, other deal-related work)
Scale of change (scale of change is likely to be low when in this archetype, but some change may occur when updating reporting, liquidity, or governance)
Downstream systems (impact of changes on multiple downstream systems requires more extensive end-to-end testing)

subs: Interfaces established between Absa and the target

optional.text: Ensure client-facing employees are briefed on the transfer and its operational impact, however minimal

role.text: Coordinate the logistical preparation of the DRs, support the operations and legal teams in defining the runbook, support the execution of the DRs either as logistical support or by acting as Migration Coordinators (MCs).

necessary.text: Work with the legal and operations teams to define cutover plan which details every activity down to the minute required to transfer ownership and reporting of the acquired bank to Absa

subs: Opening balance sheet and accounting treatment

conditional.text: TSA activation may also be tested during DRs if applicable

optional.text: Hold a 'Table-top DR' before the true DRs take place, to run through the runbook without having to set up full DR environments and logistics

nuances.text: DRs can be narrower in focus for this archetype and fewer in number, with 2 DRs including one table-top DR often sufficient due to the lack of change

artefacts.text: Approved DR strategy: this will cover DR scope, sequencing, success measures and rehearsal cadence (Absa transaction specific)

role.text: Drive the collation of evidence across execution, testing, and DRs to present a case for a Go/No-Go decision to the Steering Committee. Liaise with functional leads and AEs to ensure they can clearly state the recommendation of their area.

timelineDrivers.text: Likelihood for a no-go (no-go decisions require additional justification and discussion)
Existing evidence (if evidence has to be specially sourced and collated, timelines may increase)
SPA stipulations (some SPAs stipulate when Go/No-Go decisions must take place, and how long discussions may last)

necessary.text: Assess the success of DRs, and confirm that all issues from the final DR have been remediated or have clear timelines for remediation
Ensure that at least one successful end to end DR has taken place

subs: Absa and seller obligations as stipulated in the SPA

conditional.text: TSA readiness may also be included in decision making should these be required

optional.text: Announce the decision on the local stock exchange to ensure clients / market is aware (e.g., SENS announcement)

nuances.text: As the business will be operated as standalone, Go/No-Go decisions should focus more on regulatory, reporting, financial, and governance conditions, rather than data migration and client readiness

Coordinate cross-workstream dependencies and stakeholder communications through the cutover timeline.

timelineDrivers.text: Scale of activity required over cutover (how much true change is required for the bank to continue running as standalone)
Length of individual activities (some activities may last 24 hours + depending on their nature)
Length of time the bank can shut down without impacting service (some jurisdictions have payments flowing over the weekend, others do not)

necessary.text: As the business will be operated as standalone, cutover should focus on:
subs: Continuity of services of the acquired business
Implementation of access and security changes

necessary.text: Walk through the plan again with teams to confirm understanding, roles, and responsibilities
Sign off final cutover plan with all AEs
Coordinate contingency planning across all workstreams, gathering scenarios and planning for potential issues which may arise over the cutover

Execute on testing activities planned in the runbook to ensure all systems are working as planned

Communicate with clients on the success of the cutover
Hold regular check-ins to ensure smooth transition to Hypercare

necessary.text: Each asset, process, capability, should be classified as either:
Define key workstreams required based on the deal-archetype and SPA specifics, including rough size of each workstream
Define workstream charters per workstream, setting out objective, purpose, success metrics, key personnel, skills, and ownership

Jointly carry out workstream blueprints across buyer and seller, laying out each business process related to the workstream, which the seller will stop, which the buyer will start, and which will carry on as is
Define key milestones required to enable these process and achieve a seamless cutover at Legal Day 1 (LD1), with clear separation of buyer owned, seller owned, and jointly owned milestones
Support each workstream to define a detailed, L2 plan below this to enable the meeting of these milestones
Hold joint workshops across buyer and seller to discuss and agree on these milestones
Identify milestones with key dependencies across workstreams, and document these dependencies in detail
Set up a buyer-obligation and dependency tracker to ensure buyer is held accountable for conditions precedent

Identify the critical path, and dates/factors will have a material impact on completion, and which of these can be controlled (e.g., regulatory approval or bank-wide change freezes cannot be controlled, data migration solution build and test is critical to LD1 success, etc)
Translate the milestones into an overarching project plan to be tracked weekly
Agree initial LD1 readiness criteria per workstream with the buyer, and track these outcomes (key performance indicators which will enable cutover, e.g., for HR, 100% of consultations complete)
Agree on internal governance cadence which will sync with joint governance laid out in the SPA, including:
subs: Internal and joint Inorganic Change meetings weekly / bi-weekly to align on priorities and joint risks/issues
Working group / workstream led sessions to discuss key risks, issues, and progress
Internal Steering Committee sessions to escalate Absa-specific risks and issues, and receive guidance on key decisions
Joint Steering Committee sessions to discuss joint risks and issues, and coordinate cross-party solutions

necessary.text: Translate DD findings and governance structures into onboarding materials which clearly articulate the purpose and objectives of the deal, how execution will run day to day, roles and responsibilities, and escalation pathways

conditional.text: Submit a version of the programme plan to the regulator alongside the request for approval
Create a detailed workstream plan for employee / tech transfer
Define a TSA service catalogue and exit plan
Set up TSA exit team and define timeline for complete TSA exit
Define a stranded cost remediation plan
Set up a Separation Management Office run by the Inorganic Change Team to lead the separation from Absa's side

optional.text: Translate the project plan into project management software (e.g., Jira, MSP)
Link governance into bank-level governance such as Board meetings, StratCos, etc

nuances.text: Sold components cannot operate independently, so missing capabilities must be stood up by the buyer by Day 1
Particularly small divestments may not be required dedicated, full-time capacity on the Absa side. This is also dependent on the capabilities of the buyer's teams

artefacts.text: Regulatory commitments and approval timelines (Absa transaction specific)
Previous transaction playbooks with lessons learned (Absa transaction specific)

stages.title: Programme Execution
stages.purpose: Execute on agreed milestones, run governance cadence, and extract required business for transfer.

role.text: Inorganic Change Team acts as the central hub in the execution phase, driving workstream level execution, tracking RAID items, defining SteerCo material, and holding those responsible for separation accountable, whilst ensuring the buyer is making significant progress

timelineDrivers.text: Regulatory approval timelines
Deal perimeter and scope
New product build (additional product build by the buyer requires more delivery time)
Data complexity (Complex structures require a more nuanced data migration solution)
TSA service plan (High number of TSAs can lead to faster initial completion, with work backloaded into TSA execution and exit)

necessary.text: Conduct programme management activities: run governance processes including workstream sessions, Exec SteerCos, and Joint Buyer/Seller SteerCos; set up and track risks and issues in a central RAID log, and escalate to SteerCo as appropriate
Separate applications, infrastructure, access rights and interfaces which will remain in the retained business
Separate financial reporting, ledger, controls, and regulatory reporting from the retained business
Ensure buyer access to retained business information is removed or limited
Ensure the divested business' value is maintained ahead of LD1, to avoid complications in completion and valuation
Remediate stranded costs within the retained organisation
Track buyer obligations, flag issues, and escalate to Joint SteerCo as appropriate
Provide regular updates to the Board and Bank Leadership Forums on progress against plan, key risks and issues, and LD1 viability
Engage the regulator regularly to update progress and assess approval timelines
Conduct contingency and scenario planning for if approvals arrive later than anticipated, and define final possible date for receipt before LD1 must move
Build out detailed client communication plan across buyer and seller, and keep clients updated on the progress of the programme, and when they can expect to be onboarded
Share a data dictionary detailing data structures across source systems for the buyer to consume
Support the buyer with source-to-target mapping across all systems to enable the build of core data migration solution
Support the build of the data migration solution to Extract, Transform, and Load (ETL) solution across all source systems into target systems
Ensure the data migration solution is tested using dummy data aligned to the data dictionary, or where possible, real client data
Agree with the buyer what data can be transferred ahead of LD1, accounting for regulatory and data-privacy conditions
Define success criteria across all workstreams, and continually measure progress against these
Provide the buyer with regularly updated financials to track the progress of the divested business
Novate, assign or replicate contracts which will be transferring to the buyer
Extract and segregate the transferring client and business data from the rest of the Absa estate
Set up a Clean Room for the buyer to conduct KYC/AML checks, which should be entirely 'airgapped'
If TSAs are in place, monitor service delivery and exit planning

optional.text: Conduct change management activities for project execution teams to drive continued buy-in and morale (e.g., team socials, rewards, etc)

nuances.text: Sale of part of the balance sheet may not include the transfer of client relationships. This Should be assessededed, if included, the transfer of client data will form a significant part of execution

artefacts.text: Detail project plan built out from mobilisation and planning stage (Absa transaction specific)
Previous project playbooks with lessons learnt (Absa transaction specific)

templates.text: Joint buyer and seller status report template
Programme RAID log template with added SteerCo escalation if necessary

stages.title: Business Testing
stages.purpose: Check that the buyer can operate the new business, and that Absa can continue to operate after the transfer

role.text: Inorganic Change Team role is to coordinate and govern testing across business and technology teams, not to perform testing itself.

timelineDrivers.text: Scale of business process change
Testing expertise in-house (testing SMEs within each team means scripts require less review and testing can happen faster)
Capacity within teams to accommodate testing (needs to be balanced with BAU, build, other deal-related work)
Complexity of process change (complex new systems or products require significant testing)
Downstream systems (impact of changes on multiple downstream systems requires more extensive end-to-end testing)

necessary.text: Ensure the buyer has detailed all business process changes occurring as part of the deal to be included in testing
Detail any business or technology changes impacting the retained business on Absa's side
Work with technology teams to understand the requirements for testing environments, including end-to-end environments
Ensure retained business regression test scripts are created which ensure:
subs: Transferring balances, records, and populations reconcile
Retained applications and interfaces continue functioning
TSA processes and service levels work as designed
Regulatory and fin-crime reporting remains working as expected

necessary.text: Book these environments well in advance, or flag if suitable environments do not yet exist and must be built
Designate a testing lead within each workstream responsible for coordinating and executing tests assigned to them
Drive execution of test scripts by the business, with oversight from the testing team
Once individual processes are validated, test every process end-to-end, including the feed into downstream systems like AML, finance, and HR systems
Set up a testing-specific defect log to track issues to closure
Re-test issues post closure end-to-end, to ensure the fix has not created additional issues
Secure executive and business sign off on testing closure, with any open items clearly detailed

conditional.text: Support the buyer to test the flow of data into and out of HR systems such as Workday
Test that only data in the scope of the deal is coming across, and data related to products outside of the perimeter is filtered out
Support the buyer to test that any new systems stood up can receive data as expected
Test that systems transferring to the buyer can migrate as expected, with no disruption in service to either buyer or Absa
Set up an independent testing team to liaise with business and technology to drive test script creation and sign off

optional.text: Conduct Production Validation Testing to check that new functionality works in production as well as in test environments
Set up testing-specific governance, and feed into programme governance
Conduct friendly client testing to ensure that end-to-end flows work in a real world scenario

nuances.text: Small divestments may not require a dedicated independent testing team, as the bulk of testing work will sit within the buyer's remit

artefacts.text: Previous business testing programmes with lessons learnt, including a scenario-based risk mitigation plan (Absa transaction specific)
Business testing process flows and customer journeys (Absa transaction specific)

stages.title: LD1 Readiness
stages.purpose: Ensure new clients are onboarded to buyer systems, communicate requirements and functionality with clients, and set up an orderly transfer to the buyer

role.text: Oversee the standing up of an LD1 Readiness stream, and tracking both Absa and buyer progress and risks as part of programme management to assess critical risks to LD1

timelineDrivers.text: Scale of client transfer (more clients require additional communications alongside the buyer and more information transfer)
Complexity of client product mix (complex products and multi-product portfolios increase time to onboard and offboard)
Availability of client data (high-quality client contact data removes time spent sourcing it internally)
Client responsiveness (heavily reliant on clients responding to outreach and providing documentation)

necessary.text: Ensure all offboarding activities are taking place for assets and liabilities moving off the balance sheet (e.g., closing nostros)
Ensure impact on wider balance sheet is understood and planned for (e.g. capital adequacy, funding implications)
Define Absa's role in the Hypercare model for post go-live, and how much support the buyer requires from Absa experts

conditional.text: Ensure the buyer has defined a 'drop-dead date' for when onboarding must begin to meet LD1

Ensure the buyer has detailed all client documentation required to enable onboarding, and perform a gap analysis to understand which Absa can supply, and which the buyer must source from clients directly
Determine which clients require notification, consent or contractual novation
Share client contact details are with the buyer as early as possible, and track client outreach
Allocate responsibility for each client interaction between seller and buyer
Share Absa risk profiles of clients, to enable the buyer to understand which clients are high risk, and which some documentation can be obtained post-LD1
Track client consents, objections, attrition and transfer exceptions, and offboard clients who cannot or will not transfer (due to buyer risk appetite, client attrition, etc)
Agree servicing arrangements for clients pending transfer, and monitor conduct and reputational risks from client communications
Share existing required KYC / AML documentation across transferring clients
Support the buyer in setting up client accounts, profiles, products, permissions, and mandates ahead of time to enable Dress Rehearsals and testing

optional.text: Assess with the buyer whether some clients can be onboarded early to conduct friendly-client testing with new to bank clients

nuances.text: Sale of part of the balance sheet may not include the transfer of client relationships. This Should be assessededed, if included, the transfer of client data will form a significant part of LD1 Readiness

stages.title: Dress Rehearsals
stages.purpose: Testing end-to-end approach to cutover in order to raise and resolve any issues which would prevent a successful separation

role.text: Coordinate the logistical preparation of the DRs, support the Data Migration team in defining the runbook, support the execution of the DRs either as logistical support or by acting as Data Migration Coordinators (DMCs).

timelineDrivers.text: Time remaining post buyer build and test (if build and test finishes well ahead of LD1, more DRs can take place)
Number of Dress Rehearsals (DRs) (more DRs require a longer timeframe)
Down-time between DRs (minimum 2 weeks between DRs is recommended)

necessary.text: Work with the Data Migration and Technology teams to define cutover plan which details every activity down to the minute required to wind down the Absa business and ensure all relevant data and funds are transferred to the buyer, as well as making sure the retained business functions as expected
Ensure that runbook activities include provision for testing of continued regulatory and financial reporting, as well as financial reconciliation on the buyer's side
Hold runbook run-through sessions with all activity owners and back-ups to ensure everyone is clear on expectations
Define success metrics for DRs, with a clear understanding of what is acceptable in the first DR vs the final DR
Agree which data sets will be dummy / anonymised, and which will be real client data
Define roles and responsibilities across DRs and Cutover, including Data Migration Controllers running the runbook
Execute logistical support required to enable 24/7 DRs to take place such as building access, food requirements, accommodation, travel, Wi-Fi, security, facilities, and back-up plans

Define the governance processes to take place during DRs including the command centre, regular executive updates, escalation pathways, war room protocols, issue resolution processes, and continency decision making
Collate a DR playbook summarising success criteria, logistical information, key contacts, governance processes, and timelines
Define and test rollback, contingency, and partial transfer scenarios to ensure Minimal disruption to clients in these instances
Confirm after each DR that retained data has not been transferred
Run a minimum of 4 DRs across weekends, with at least 2 weeks in between each
Each DR should execute the runbook end-to-end, and track issues which arise for remediation
Hold DR retros to note lessons learnt and iterate into subsequent DRs
Track the remediation of issues ahead of subsequent DRs

conditional.text: Include DR activities which simulate the exit of liquidity and capital, and ensure the business has prepared processes to address this

optional.text: Hold a 'Technical DR' before the true DRs take place, to test only the migration solution, and ensure this is not a blocker to future DRs

nuances.text: For small divestments, DRs and runbooks can narrow their focus to extracting relevant data and ensuring it is passed correctly to the buyer, with minimal disruption to the retained business

artefacts.text: Approved DR strategy: this will cover DR scope, sequencing, success measures and rehearsal cadence (Absa transaction specific)
Previous DR completion records with timestamps, success measure results and lessons learnt (Absa transaction specific)

stages.title: Go/No-Go
stages.purpose: Formally discuss and approve/disapprove whether all workstreams and parties are sufficiently ready to proceed with separation

role.text: Drive the collation of evidence across execution, testing, and DRs to present a case for a Go/No-Go decision to the Steering Committee. Liaise with functional leads and AEs to ensure they can clearly state the recommendation of their area.

timelineDrivers.text: Likelihood for a no-go (no-go decisions require additional justification and discussion)
Existing evidence (if evidence has to be specially sourced and collated, timelines may increase)
SPA stipulations (some SPAs stipulate when Go/No-Go decisions must take place, and how long discussions may last)

necessary.text: Assess the success of DRs, and confirm that all issues from the final DR have been remediated or have clear timelines for remediation
Ensure that at least one successful end to end DR has taken place
Discuss residual risks and mitigation plans across each workstream, with each AE laying out in turn testing results, DR success, and residual risks related to their area
For each residual risk, lay out the potential risk to go-live, likelihood, and mitigation plans
Gather evidence that key conditions have been met such as:
subs: Data extraction and reconciliation in DRs
Buyer obligations as stipulated in the SPA

necessary.text: Gather all AEs / SteerCo members to formally make and document the Go/No-Go decision internally, allowing any reservations to be noted and addressed
Gather buyer and seller AEs to formally make the joint Go/No-Go decision
Formally document go/no position with the buyer and communicate to clients, employees, and regulators

conditional.text: Distinguish between:
Include Go/No-Go decision points related to buyer client onboarding, novations, and account set ups if client relationships are in-scope for transfer

optional.text: Announce the decision on the local stock exchange to ensure clients / market is aware (e.g., SENS announcement)
Brief the media on the decision, with a series of prepared remarks

nuances.text: Go/No-Go may need to account for buyer client onboarding and set up should client transfer form part of the divestment

artefacts.text: Go/No-Go criteria (owned by Inorganic Change Team to use throughout this decision making process)
M&A Learning Academy materials on governance and decision rights

stages.title: Cutover
stages.purpose: Execute the controlled separation and transfer of the agreed business perimeter while maintaining continuity across both the divested and retained businesses

role.text: Coordinate the logistical preparation of the cutover, based upon successful DR. Support the execution of the cutover
Run the central control function, coordinating Absa activities and linking in with the buyer, and overseeing workstream execution against approved runbook.
Coordinate cross-workstream dependencies and stakeholder communications through the cutover timeline.

timelineDrivers.text: Scale of activity required over cutover
Length of individual activities (some activities may last 24 hours + depending on their nature)
Length of time the bank can shut down without impacting service (some jurisdictions have payments flowing over the weekend, others do not)

necessary.text: Work with Data Migration and Technology to define the final cutover plan, iterated during DRs
Freeze and extract the final transferring population ahead of cutover
Reconcile assets and liabilities to assess funding requirements, and execute financial settlement and completion-account activities
Ensure required legal documents are signed over cutover to formally transfer legal and operational control to the buyer
Ensure Absa system access to divested business is revoked or modified
Walk through the plan again with teams to confirm understanding, roles, and responsibilities
Sign off final cutover plan with all AEs
Coordinate contingency planning across all workstreams, gathering scenarios and planning for potential issues which may arise over the cutover
Define any additional governance to be in place during cutover vs DRs (e.g., additional executive updates, final decision gates, etc)
Execute on cutover plan, including agreed-upon governance gates
Execute on testing activities planned in the runbook to ensure all retained business systems are working as planned
Hold final checkpoint to assess success of the cutover, ensure retained systems continue to function, and assess Absa support required in mitigation plans for issues
Continue to communicate with the buyer once they open post-cutover to assess issues and provide support where needed

conditional.text: Communicate with clients on the success of the cutover, and remind them of new channels into the buyer
Extract and freeze client data should this be in scope
Communicate any residual issues to clients which remain post-cutover, and detail timelines for remediation
Activate buyer access and TSA services

optional.text: Brief the media on a successful cutover, with pre-prepared executive remarks
Issue an announcement on the stock exchange regarding the successful cutover

nuances.text: Cutover of client data will also be included if this is in scope. If not, the cutover will focus on the moving of agreed assets and liabilities

artefacts.text: Approved cutover runbook, including a time-sequenced plan: activities, owners, dependencies, control gates, and completion criteria (Absa transaction specific)

stages.title: Hypercare
stages.purpose: Stabilise the retained business, ensure TSAs are active as required, resolve any residual issues from cutover, and support buyer Hypercare.

role.text: Monitor a consolidated view of incidents post cutover, and monitor the Hypercare team's triage and remediation efforts
Support the Hypercare team in escalating issues through agreed governance in order to prevent any financial, regulatory or client harm
Assess readiness to exit Hypercare using an agreed checklist and criteria, coordinating a formal handover to BAU
Lead regular updates to executives on tracking of strategic and financial outcomes

timelineDrivers.text: Whether clients are transferring (transferring clients means additional time required to triage and resolve issues)
Capacity within Hypercare team (smaller team takes longer to resolve issues)
Complexity of transfer (a transfer of complex clients with complex products likely requires more dedicated service time)
Success of cutover (issues on cutover mean an extended Hypercare period will likely be needed to stabilise clients and resolve issues)

necessary.text: Set up a dedicated team to monitor residual cutover issues, retained business issues, and any post-cutover data corrections or additions required
Triage issues for remediation, add them to a backlog, and flag with technology / BAU teams as required
Escalate persistent or P1 issues immediately, through a dedicated escalation pathway
Stand up and coordinate war-rooms as necessary to remediate P1 issues quickly and avoid disruption
Gradually hand off servicing to BAU teams by transitioning issue resolution and triage into the BAU process, prioritising only the most serious issues for Hypercare as time passes
Track divestment objectives such as cost, asset/liability transfer, volumes, etc. as soon as LD1, and provide updates to executives on progress against objectives
Hold daily touchpoints with AEs to flag the most important issues and discuss remediation plans

conditional.text: Set up dedicated client communications teams to ensure retained clients remain in the loop post LD1
Hold regular touchpoints with client-facing teams to discuss client sentiment and assess action plans
Support the buyer's Hypercare for systems which have transitioned from Absa to buyer
Monitor TSA performance, track progress towards exit, and remove remaining entanglements
Complete financial true-ups and track stranded cost removal
Resolve any transfer exceptions or data inaccuracies
Monitor warranties, indemnities, and potential claims
Confirm buyer deletion or return of Absa data

optional.text: Reach out to clients directly to assess sentiment

nuances.text: Dedicated client-focused Hypercare will be required should client transfer be in scope for the deal

templates.text: TSA service dashboard and exit plan

stages.title: Due Diligence
stages.purpose: Determine whether the acquisition creates value, what you are actually buying, and what needs to be protected contractually. Legal & CorpDev lead; other areas input where required. Activities below relate to key items for the integration team to consider during this process, they do not override current DD processes

role.text: Extract information from the DD process necessary to properly plan and run the divestment
Act as M&A SMEs to provide oversight, bringing a practical, Absa oriented lens which goes beyond financials and ensures nuances are identified and caught based on previous experience

timelineDrivers.text: Deal perimeter (broader perimeter requires more detailed review by the seller)
Product complexity (more complex products are harder for a seller to model and project)
Maturity of DD teams (experienced teams can pre-empt buyer questions and data requests ahead of time)
Buyer availability (heavily reliant on buyer capacity to review and assess materials)

necessary.text: Ensure virtual data room set up to share confidential documentation and ensure it persists after deal signature
Ensure an NDA process to wall-cross those who need access to confidential information is set up
Ensure buyer has the requisite information access controls set up to protect Absa confidential information
Ensure potential leakage of confidential, client or retained-business information is assessed
Understand the sale perimeter: which assets and liabilities transfer, how will the buyer interact with what Absa is not selling?

Build an initial view of project divestment costs, leveraging comparable deals, including TSA costs and retained-business remediation costs. All assumptions in planning costs must be defensible and informed by functional experts
Build or oversee build of a detailed business case comparing forecasted benefits of divestment to project costs and continued running costs
Ensure services the divested business currently receives from Absa are identified
Ensure subject matter experts are engaged to conduct cyber, technology, security, compliance DD to ensure that a deep understanding of these elements is gained during DD, to inform accurate planning
Ensure tax implications have been assessed and remediation planned

conditional.text: Ensure that cost implication of the people movement has been assessed, and agree whether severance costs will be incurred
Ensure total cost of ownership of transferring technology has been understood and identify potential cost savings
Access to this early stage of the lifecycle may not always be possible given the broader business context, but it should be requested given its importance to execution

optional.text: Review lessons learnt from previous deals
Engage a subset of buyer clients to assess current pain points and identify any potential deal red flags (e.g. compliance issues, pricing mismatches, in-scope technology issues)

nuances.text: Case for sale must account for economies/diseconomies of scale inherent in selling part but not all of a business (e.g., cost base may not be halved by removing half the balance sheet)
DD must account for business line synergies inherent in selling part but not all of a business (i.e., are existing business lines not being sold harmed by the sale of some others)

artefacts.text: Previous transaction materials and lessons learnt (Absa transaction specific)

stages.title: Legal Drafting & Signature
stages.purpose: Ensure the Sale and Purchase Agreement (SPA) reflects reality of programme delivery, and enables execution. Legal & CorpDev lead, other areas input where required. Activities below relate to key integration considerations, they do not overwrite the current processes.

role.text: Ensure legals reflect execution reality, and timelines are realistic
Ensure legals include provisions which will support execution, such as data sharing
Ensure any go-live dates are based on realistic assumptions around regulatory approval and client onboarding timelines
Leverage lessons learned from previous deals to ensure legals address any historic pain points

timelineDrivers.text: Deal complexity (complex deals require additional protections and conditions)
Employee transfer (employee transfer requires an additional agreement drafted)
Technology ownership (addenda may be required to stipulate technology requirements)
Pre-signing alignment (pre-agreed valuations and completion mechanisms will speed up drafting)
DD quality (high quality DD will allow defensible assumptions to be made in the legals, otherwise these will have to be assessed during this phase)
Regulatory complexity (multiple regulators across multiple jurisdictions increases complexity in drafting legals)

necessary.text: Engage external lawyers to lead SPA drafting and negotiation, informed by internal legal opinion
Negotiate transaction terms including valuation, adjustment principles, completion mechanisms, and payment terms
Ensure price, adjustments and effective transfer date are agreed
Coordinate and confirm the signing sequence between Absa, the buyer and other parties
Document employee transfer, retention, severance, and knowledge-transfer obligations
Set out which items will transfer from Absa to the buyer automatically under agreed regulatory processes (e.g., Section 54), and which will have to be manually transferred
Detail novation processes for items not automatically transferring, whether independent legal opinions on contracts are required, and where liability sits during transfer
Set out the joint governance mechanisms across buyer and seller at a high level (e.g., the scheduling of joint Steering Committees, appointment of Transaction Directors from each party)
Set out joint escalation mechanisms for programme-level issues, as well as dispute resolution mechanisms
Set out stipulations and timings for the sharing of client data, including whether business cases are required, and what can and can't be shared ahead of regulatory approval
Set out conditions precedent for completion, including funds transfer, assets/liabilities transfer, regulatory approval, and board approval
Agree signatures required on each side
Set out completion date precedent on regulatory approval date(s), rather than a pre-agreed specific date
Set out a joint communications plan to clients from both buyer and seller, including timelines for when buyer can engage the clients
Place clear obligations on the buyer for regulatory approvals, onboarding and operational readiness
Define how incomplete transfers or rejected clients will be treated

conditional.text: Detail exact employees (anonymized) to be transferred
Detail seller hiring/redundancy stipulations whilst completion is in progress (e.g. maximum salary to be hired, redundancy processes)
Detail technology maintenance requirements of Absa, and stipulations on major changes
Detail FX payment mechanisms, including adjustments for FX risk and longer settlement times
Define ownership and licensing of shared Intellectual Property
Establish TSAs, service levels, pricing, liabilities, and exit dates
Access to this early stage of the lifecycle may not always be possible given the broader business context, but it should be requested given its importance to execution

optional.text: Set SPA change control mechanisms
Set up SPA access mechanisms for project team members
Socialise with functional leads ahead of signature

nuances.text: S197 or equivalent should be attached to the SPA as an addendum
Any joint technology agreements should be attached as addenda

artefacts.text: DD summary and agreed deal decisions (Absa deal specific)

stages.title: Mobilisation & Planning
stages.purpose: Define the key activities which must take place to enable LD1 to take place on the agreed date, and surface dependencies

role.text: Inorganic Change team should lead the mobilisation effort across Absa: briefing functional leads / AEs, onboarding teams, executing the NDA process, creating onboarding materials, briefing teams on detailed plan creation, and supporting the buyer to lead joint planning efforts

timelineDrivers.text: Deal complexity (complex deals need more workstreams to execute)
Geographical scope (multiple geographies require more coordination)
Existing knowledge (teams familiar with these deals can draft a detailed plan much faster, and understand dependencies)
Available resource (resource constraints mean activities take longer)
Buyer capabilities (joint planning is reliant on the buyer's more detailed plan being ready for discussion)

necessary.text: Set up mobilisation hierarchy:
subs: Board appoints executive sponsor for the deal
Transaction Director and Executive Sponsor agree Accountable Executives for each function / workstream
AE selection should be informed by their expected responsibilities, detailed in the Hub and Spoke Operating Model
AEs appoint functional workstream leads, who appoint in-country leads
Transaction Director mobilises central Inorganic Change team and in-country coordinators
Buyer and Seller Inorganic Change teams share lists of functional leads to enable joint planning
Joint and individual governance established based on Mobilisation Toolkit

necessary.text: Each asset, process, capability, should be classified as either:
Set up a Separation Management Office run by the Inorganic Change Team to lead the separation from Absa's side
