artefacts.text: Previous business testing programmes with lessons learnt, including a scenario-based risk mitigation plan (Absa transaction specific)
Business testing process flows and customer journeys (Absa transaction specific)

stages.title: Client Continuity & LD1 Readiness
stages.purpose: Communicate plans and functionality with clients, and set up an orderly transfer to the buyer

role.text: Oversee the standing up of an LD1 Readiness stream, and tracking both Absa and buyer progress and risks as part of programme management to assess critical risks to LD1

timelineDrivers.text: Scale of client transfer (more clients require additional communications alongside the buyer)

necessary.text: Allocate responsibility for each client interaction between seller and buyer
Share Absa risk profiles of clients, to enable the buyer to understand which clients are high risk, and which some documentation can be obtained post-LD1
Share existing required KYC / AML documentation across transferring clients
Define Absa's role in the Hypercare model for post go-live, and how much support the buyer requires from Absa experts
Identify client contracts with change-of-control provisions
Confirm how complaints and conduct issues will be handled
Monitor client attrition and reputational risk
Communicate any brand, ownership or contact changes

conditional.text: Prepare client-facing employees transferring by ensuring clients have their new contact details for once they have transferred to the buyer

nuances.text: Dedicated LD1 Readiness capacity on the buyer and seller side is less critical if the business is being run as standalone, as clients generally remain with the same legal entity and do not require full buyer onboarding. Focus is instead on clear communication of timelines, and monitoring attrition risk

stages.title: Dress Rehearsals
stages.purpose: Testing end-to-end approach to separation in order to raise and resolve any issues which would prevent a successful separation

role.text: Coordinate the logistical preparation of the DRs, support the operations and legal teams in defining the runbook, support the execution of the DRs either as logistical support or by acting as Migration Coordinators (MCs).

timelineDrivers.text: Number of Dress Rehearsals (DRs) (more DRs require a longer timeframe)
Down-time between DRs (minimum 2 weeks between DRs is recommended)

necessary.text: Ensure that runbook activities include provision for testing of continued regulatory and financial reporting, as well as financial reconciliation on the buyer's side
Hold runbook run-through sessions with all activity owners and back-ups to ensure everyone is clear on expectations
Define success metrics for DRs, with a clear understanding of what is acceptable in the first DR vs the final DR
Define roles and responsibilities across DRs and Cutover, including Data Migration Controllers running the runbook
Execute logistical support required to enable 24/7 DRs to take place such as building access, food requirements, accommodation, travel, Wi-Fi, security, facilities, and back-up plans

Define the governance processes to take place during DRs including the command centre, regular executive updates, escalation pathways, war room protocols, issue resolution processes, and continency decision making
Collate a DR playbook summarising success criteria, logistical information, key contacts, governance processes, and timelines
Confirm after each DR that retained data has not been transferred
Run a minimum of 2 DRs across weekends, with at least 2 weeks in between each
Each DR should execute the runbook end-to-end, and track issues which arise for remediation
Hold DR retros to note lessons learnt and iterate into subsequent DRs
Track the remediation of issues ahead of subsequent DRs
Include DR activities which test legal completion, transfer of ownership, and purchase price settlement
Assess financial deconsolidation and treasury and funding transition during DRs
Assess continuity of regulatory reporting within Absa group during DRs

conditional.text: Include DR activities which relate to the set up of brand new systems or migration of Absa technology into buyer environments
Include DR activities which simulate TSA activation

optional.text: Hold a 'Table-top DR' before the true DRs take place, to run through the full runbook with all owners, without having to execute each step in the proper environments

nuances.text: As the buyer will run the business as standalone, scale of DRs can be significantly reduced, and driven by the level of operational change occurring.
A tabletop rehearsal plus one full completion rehearsal may be sufficient where the entity continues on its existing systems

artefacts.text: Approved DR strategy: this will cover DR scope, sequencing, success measures and rehearsal cadence (Absa transaction specific)
Previous DR completion records with timestamps, success measure results and lessons learnt (Absa transaction specific)

stages.title: Go/No-Go
stages.purpose: Formally discuss and approve/disapprove whether all workstreams and parties are sufficiently ready to proceed with separation

role.text: Drive the collation of evidence across execution, testing, and DRs to present a case for a Go/No-Go decision to the Steering Committee. Liaise with functional leads and AEs to ensure they can clearly state the recommendation of their area.

timelineDrivers.text: Likelihood for a no-go (no-go decisions require additional justification and discussion)
Existing evidence (if evidence has to be specially sourced and collated, timelines may increase)
SPA stipulations (some SPAs stipulate when Go/No-Go decisions must take place, and how long discussions may last)

necessary.text: Assess the success of DRs, and confirm that all issues from the final DR have been remediated or have clear timelines for remediation
Ensure that at least one successful end to end DR has taken place
Discuss residual risks and mitigation plans across each workstream, with each AE laying out in turn testing results, DR success, and residual risks related to their area
For each residual risk, lay out the potential risk to go-live, likelihood, and mitigation plans
Gather evidence that key conditions have been met such as:
subs: Buyer obligations as stipulated in the SPA
Agreement and acceptance of residual separation risks

necessary.text: Gather all AEs / SteerCo members to formally make and document the Go/No-Go decision internally, allowing any reservations to be noted and addressed
Gather buyer and seller AEs to formally make the joint Go/No-Go decision
Formally document go/no position with the Buyer and communicate to clients, employees, and regulators
Include a Go/No-Go decision related to employee readiness, including the completion of key conditions such as consultations

conditional.text: Distinguish between:

optional.text: Announce the decision on the local stock exchange to ensure clients / market is aware (e.g., SENS announcement)
Brief the media on the decision, with a series of prepared remarks

nuances.text: Go/No-Go should focus on the buyer's readiness to run the business independently, and Absa's assurance that no continuing operations will be impacted, distinguishing legal completion readiness from any longer-term buyer integration activity

artefacts.text: Go/No-Go criteria (owned by Inorganic Change Team to use throughout this decision making process)
M&A Learning Academy materials on governance and decision rights

stages.title: Legal Completion & Control Handover
stages.purpose: Execute the controlled separation of the full business while maintaining continuity, and legally pass ownership to the buyer

role.text: Coordinate the logistical preparation of the cutover, based upon successful DR. Support the execution of the cutover
Run the central control function, coordinating Absa activities and linking in with the buyer, and overseeing workstream execution against approved runbook.
Coordinate cross-workstream dependencies and stakeholder communications through the cutover timeline.

timelineDrivers.text: Scale of activity required over cutover
Length of individual activities (some activities may last 24 hours + depending on their nature)
Length of time the bank can shut down without impacting service (some jurisdictions have payments flowing over the weekend, others do not)

necessary.text: Define the final cutover plan, iterated during DRs
Ensure required legal documents are signed over cutover to formally transfer legal and operational control to the buyer
Ensure Absa system access to divested business is revoked or modified
Walk through the plan again with teams to confirm understanding, roles, and responsibilities
Sign off final cutover plan with all AEs
Coordinate contingency planning across all workstreams, gathering scenarios and planning for potential issues which may arise over the cutover
Define any additional governance to be in place during cutover vs DRs (e.g., additional executive updates, final decision gates, etc)
Execute on cutover plan, including agreed-upon governance gates
Execute on testing activities planned in the runbook to ensure all remaining Abse-group systems are working as planned
Hold final checkpoint to assess success of the cutover, ensure retained systems continue to function, and assess Absa support required in mitigation plans for issues
Continue to communicate with the buyer to assess issues and provide support where needed
Execute purchase-price settlement and transfer shares and legal title.
Complete Board resignations and appointments and transfer governance and delegated authorities
Replace Absa funding and guarantees
Confirm that the target and remaining Absa group are operational

conditional.text: Communicate any residual issues to clients which remain post-cutover, and detail timelines for remediation
Activate TSAs and begin to track towards exit

optional.text: Brief the media on a successful cutover, with pre-prepared executive remarks
Issue an announcement on the stock exchange regarding the successful cutover

nuances.text: Cutover for a deal of this type will be the least complex, focused largely on transfer of legal ownership, as the business should largely continue running as previously, with only the ownership structures, reporting, and liquidity management changing

artefacts.text: Approved cutover runbook, including a time-sequenced plan: activities, owners, dependencies, control gates, and completion criteria (Absa transaction specific)

stages.title: Hypercare
stages.purpose: Support a stable transition of ownership, resolve residual seller obligations and complete Absa's exit from the business.

role.text: Support the Hypercare team in escalating issues through agreed governance in order to prevent any financial, regulatory or client harm
Assess readiness to exit Hypercare using an agreed checklist and criteria, coordinating a formal handover to BAU
Lead regular updates to executives on tracking of strategic and financial outcomes

timelineDrivers.text: Capacity within Hypercare team (smaller team takes longer to resolve issues)
Success of cutover (issues on cutover mean an extended Hypercare period will likely be needed to stabilise clients and resolve issues)

necessary.text: Set up a dedicated team to monitor residual cutover issues and retained business issues
Triage issues for remediation, add them to a backlog, and flag with technology / BAU teams as required
Escalate persistent or P1 issues immediately, through a dedicated escalation pathway
Stand up and coordinate war-rooms as necessary to remediate P1 issues quickly and avoid disruption
Gradually hand off servicing to BAU teams by transitioning issue resolution and triage into the BAU process, prioritising only the most serious issues for Hypercare as time passes
Track divestment objectives such as cost, asset/liability transfer, volumes, etc. as soon as LD1, and provide updates to executives on progress against objectives
Hold daily touchpoints with AEs to flag the most important issues and discuss remediation plans
Conduct completion-account and purchase-price true-ups
Ensure closure of intra-group accounts and interfaces
Confirmation of buyer data-return or deletion obligations
Ensure post-completion support is within the bounds of SPA and TSAs

conditional.text: Monitor TSA performance, track progress towards exit, and remove remaining entanglements
Monitor warranties, indemnities, and potential claims

nuances.text: Detailed, specific Hypercare capacity may not be required from the Absa side if the buyer is running the business as standalone with minimal operational and technical change

templates.text: TSA service dashboard and exit plan

components.name: Central M&A Hub
components.summary: Permanent core team that owns the M&A method, mobilises every deal and holds programme control from pre-signing through hypercare.
components.purpose: Hold Absa's inorganic delivery capability in one place so each deal starts from a codified method rather than from scratch, and so execution discipline is consistent across archetypes and geographies.
responsibilities: Own and maintain the codified lifecycle, archetype classification and artefact set
Mobilise the deal: archetype call, delivery shape, resourcing plan and governance stand-up
Run integrated planning, milestone tracking, risk and dependency management
Chair the transaction working group and prepare steering committee material
Run readiness, dress rehearsals and go/no-go evidence packs
Capture lessons learnt and feed them back into the method
services: Deal mobilisation in a defined number of working days
Integrated plan and critical path on a single baseline
Programme reporting, RAID and decision log
Template and artefact library with worked examples
decisionRights: Sets the delivery method, plan baseline and reporting cadence
Confirms the deal archetype and mobilisation shape
Owns the go/no-go recommendation to the steering committee
Can escalate directly to the executive sponsor
Cannot change deal scope, price or commercial terms
governance: Reports into the transaction director and the deal steering committee
Directs functional and regional spoke leads on delivery matters
Interfaces with Corporate Development pre-signing and with Internal Audit throughout
capabilities: M&A programme leadership and PMO discipline
inputs: Deal thesis, structure and indicative timetable from Corporate Development
Due diligence findings and conditions precedent
outputs: Post-deal lessons learnt and method updates

components.name: Functional and regional spokes
components.summary: South African functional workstreams paired with in-country regional workstreams, mobilised according to the deal archetype.
components.purpose: Deliver the functional and country-level change required to complete the transaction, using people who already run the business rather than a parallel organisation.
responsibilities: Own functional delivery to the agreed milestone dates
Provide effort estimates, resource names and dependencies at mobilisation
Raise risks, issues and decisions into the transaction working group
Confirm functional readiness ahead of dress rehearsals and cutover
Own local regulatory and market obligations in each in-country spoke
services: Functional impact assessment and target design
Delivery of functional change against the integrated plan
In-country execution and local regulator engagement
decisionRights: Approve functional design and functional readiness within policy
Nominate and release delivery resources within their function
Cannot move an agreed milestone without working-group approval
Cannot accept a local regulatory obligation outside mandate
governance: Spoke leads sit on the transaction working group chaired by the Hub
Regional spoke leads report functionally to their SA counterpart and locally to the country executive
Escalation runs spoke lead, Hub, transaction director, steering committee
capabilities: Functional subject-matter depth with delivery experience
Local regulatory and market knowledge in each geography
Ability to plan, estimate and hold a milestone date
inputs: Archetype, perimeter and integrated plan from the Hub
Diligence findings relevant to the function
outputs: Functional plans, designs and readiness evidence

components.name: Partner accelerator network
components.summary: Pre-qualified external providers that can be mobilised quickly where Absa lacks specialist advice or short-term delivery capacity.
components.purpose: Remove the delay and cost of sourcing external help mid-deal by pre-agreeing categories, providers and mobilisation routes before a transaction starts.
responsibilities: Maintain pre-qualified provider categories and commercial arrangements
Define trigger points where external support is expected
Onboard, direct and exit partners against a defined scope and outcome
Ensure knowledge transfers back into Absa before partners leave
services: Specialist advice on regulatory, tax, legal and technical questions
Short-term delivery capacity for peak load
Independent assurance on migration and readiness
decisionRights: The Hub recommends the need; the transaction director approves the spend
Partners hold no Absa decision rights and cannot sign off readiness
governance: Requested through the Hub, approved by the transaction director, contracted by Procurement
Partners report to the accountable Absa spoke lead, never directly to steering
outputs: Mobilised partner teams against defined scope
Capability retained in Absa at exit

change-management.keyRole: Owns the business change approach needed to embed new or separated ways of working across impacted teams.
responsibilities: Conduct change impact assessments across roles, processes, controls, systems, clients and country teams.
Define the change strategy, adoption plan, training needs, engagement approach and business-readiness evidence.
Support HR with organisational impacts and Communications / Marketing with change narrative and stakeholder messaging.
Coordinate readiness interventions for teams adopting new processes, systems, hand-offs or control routines.
Measure adoption during testing, LD1 readiness and hypercare; drive corrective actions where take-up is weak.
Drive broader programme morale and sentiment
boundaryItems: HR owns employment terms, consultation, onboarding and people-transfer obligations.
Communications / Marketing owns messaging channels and approved client content.
Operations & Servicing and Product own process and proposition design; Change owns adoption and behavioural readiness.
Change should hand over to business-unit change managers where available, and HR teams in other circumstances at the end of the programme
change-management.centralHubRelationship: Relationship with Central Hub: the SA Functional Spoke owns change adoption decisions and evidence while the Central Hub sets programme standards, coordinates dependencies and escalates transaction-wide issues.
regionalRelationship: Regional Spokes should own local execution as a minimum, with ownership scaling based on maturity, including local change impacts, stakeholder engagement, training coordination, adoption activity, sentiment monitoring and issue resolution where they have capacity and delegated authority.

Function Authority retains change strategy, methodology, adoption standards, leadership narrative, central challenge and execution support where regional maturity, capability or capacity is insufficient.

As regional maturity increases, local ownership should expand from input and capacity support into delivery of change interventions, adoption evidence and handover activity, with Function Authority retaining central standards and specialist support.

milestoneIntro: The key milestones below are organised as a baseline set, with additional milestones required for more complex deal archetypes split out below as required.

As deal archetypes scale from balance sheet to partial business to full business, each milestone should be assessed against stakeholder impact, confidentiality restrictions, regulatory approvals, brand change, client and colleague volumes, channel complexity and the degree of joint execution required with the counterparty.
serviceCatalogue: Stakeholder mapping and stage-gated message strategy
Confidentiality, leak response and crisis communications
Regulator, client, colleague, media and wider stakeholder communications
Joint communications governance, drafting, validation and approval management
Channel, campaign and content planning across human, digital and self-service channels
Brand, customer proposition and marketing transition
LD1, cutover, issue and hypercare communications
Stakeholder insight, reputation monitoring and BAU handover

activitySets.heading: Balance Sheet Acquisition - baseline activities

milestones.name: Communications and marketing strategy approved (4 weeks)
activities: Define communications objectives, guiding principles, critical outcomes and the role of communications and marketing across the transaction.

Map regulator, client, colleague, media and other stakeholder groups by stage gate, then work backwards from the required stakeholder outcome. Gather inputs on required communications from all other workstreams
Align the strategy with the transaction narrative, customer proposition, programme plan, change approach and applicable regulatory restrictions.

milestones.name: Confidentiality, leak and crisis communications protocol established (3 weeks)
activities: Confirm insider-list restrictions, what may be communicated at each stage and the approved response if information leaks before signing or approval.
Prepare holding statements, escalation routes, spokesperson responsibilities and rapid approval arrangements for reputational or service issues.
Test crisis scenarios with Legal, Compliance, Risk, the Central Hub and relevant regional leadership.

milestones.name: Joint communications governance and approval route agreed (4 weeks)
activities: Define who drafts, validates, approves and releases each communication type, including clear authority to speak to clients and employees.
Agree counterparty review timelines, version control, evidence requirements and escalation for delayed or duplicative approvals.
Maintain an integrated communications calendar linked to regulatory approvals, client readiness, cutover and LD1 milestones.

milestones.name: Stakeholder messages, content and channel plan completed (6 weeks)
activities: Develop a single core narrative with tailored messages for regulators, clients, colleagues, media and other relevant audiences.
Sequence communications so audiences can absorb the information, prioritising critical messages rather than over-sharing, working with each impacted workstream to gather inputs and signoff
Select the appropriate mix of relationship-led, contact-centre, email, web, social, event, digital hub and self-service channels for each audience.

milestones.name: Client and colleague-facing teams briefed and equipped (4 weeks)
activities: Prepare relationship-manager, leader, contact-centre and frontline briefing packs, FAQs, scripts and referral routes.
Use client-facing colleagues as subject-matter contributors and reassurance channels while maintaining approved-message controls.
Confirm query ownership, service escalation and rapid content-update processes with Operations, Product, Human Capital and Change Management.

milestones.name: LD1 communications and post-launch monitoring completed (4 weeks)
activities: Execute regulatory, client, colleague, media and market communications in the approved sequence around cutover and LD1.
Monitor reach, engagement, questions, sentiment, service issues and reputational indicators across all channels during hypercare.
Refresh messages and content where audiences have not seen, understood or acted on the initial communications, then hand ongoing activity to BAU owners.

activitySets.heading: Partial Business Acquisition - additional activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Transferred, retained and shared stakeholder populations segmented (5 weeks)
activities: Separate transferring, retained, excluded and shared client and colleague populations, including key relationship, regulatory and media stakeholders.
Define differentiated messages, timing and support routes for each cohort to prevent confusion or inconsistent treatment.

milestones.name: Brand, collateral and campaign transition plan completed (6 weeks)
activities: Identify affected brand assets, customer materials, websites, digital journeys, campaigns, sponsorships and physical collateral.
Define co-branding, rebranding, withdrawal, replacement and approval requirements for transferred and retained propositions.
Plan targeted acquisition, retention or reassurance activity for priority customer segments while protecting the retained business narrative.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Acquisition A (integrated) - further additional activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Integrated brand and marketing transition strategy approved (8 weeks)
activities: Define the target brand architecture, customer proposition, migration story and phased transition from the acquired brand to Absa.
Map the complete estate of brand, campaign, digital, physical, sponsorship and client-facing assets requiring change.
Agree brand-use controls, legal and regulatory approvals, production lead times, budget and prioritisation for LD1 and post-LD1 activity.

milestones.name: Enterprise launch campaign and digital information hub readied (6 weeks)
activities: Build a central information hub with audience-specific content, FAQs, videos, updates and clear routes to human support.
Prepare coordinated web, social, direct, event, relationship and internal campaign assets using one approved narrative.
Test content accessibility, channel capacity, analytics, update ownership and the ability to respond quickly to emerging questions.

milestones.name: Integrated client, colleague and market launch executed (5 weeks)
activities: Coordinate leader communications, employee cascades, client engagement, media activity and marketing launch around the integration sequence.
Maintain a unified narrative across Business, Human Capital, Change, Legal, Compliance, Digital and frontline teams.
Monitor reputation, customer response, employee sentiment and campaign performance, then adjust the first-100-day plan.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Acquisition B (standalone) - new activity set
activitySets.lead: Standalone:

milestones.name: Standalone stakeholder, reputation and communications strategy approved (5 weeks)
activities: Define the standalone business narrative, stakeholder outcomes and communications principles for regulators, clients, colleagues, media and partners.
Map stage-gated stakeholder needs, local market sensitivities, reputation risks and leadership expectations.
Agree how the standalone narrative relates to Absa group messaging while preserving local relevance and delegated authority.

milestones.name: Standalone communications governance and operating model established (5 weeks)
activities: Define communications and marketing roles, decision rights, approval routes, spokespersons, budget, agency support and regional execution responsibilities.
Establish confidentiality, leak, crisis, issues-management and rapid-response protocols.
Confirm the BAU content calendar, channel ownership, measurement approach and handover requirements.

milestones.name: Standalone brand and customer proposition developed (8 weeks)
activities: Define brand architecture, identity, positioning, customer proposition, tone of voice and market-entry or continuity narrative.
Create or adapt the required brand assets, campaign materials, websites, social presence, templates and physical collateral.
Secure Legal, Compliance, regulatory and executive approvals for the standalone brand and marketing proposition.

milestones.name: Regulator, client, colleague and media programmes readied (4 weeks)
activities: Develop audience-specific plans, messages, notices, briefing packs, FAQs, events and relationship-led engagement.
Prepare client-facing teams, contact centres, leaders and employee representatives to explain the standalone model consistently.
Agree joint communications and speaking rights with the counterparty for every restricted or interdependent audience.

milestones.name: Standalone digital hub and service communication channels launched (6 weeks)
activities: Launch a durable information hub and self-service content for clients and colleagues, supported by clear human escalation routes.
Confirm web, social, email, contact-centre, event and frontline channels can publish and update approved content at scale.
Test analytics, content ownership, accessibility and issue-response procedures before LD1.

milestones.name: Standalone launch and first-100-day campaign executed (8 weeks)
activities: Execute the approved launch sequence across regulator, client, colleague, media and marketing channels.
Track awareness, engagement, sentiment, reputation, service demand and campaign effectiveness through hypercare.
Refine messages and marketing activity, close launch issues and transfer ongoing communications to the standalone BAU team.

milestones.name: Divestment communications and marketing strategy approved (4 weeks)
activities: Define communications objectives, stakeholder outcomes and message principles for the sale perimeter and retained Absa business.
Map regulators, affected clients, colleagues, media and other stakeholders by transaction stage and information need.
Align the strategy with the sale narrative, legal agreements, regulatory process, separation plan and retained customer proposition.

milestones.name: Confidentiality, leak and crisis communications protocol established (3 weeks)
activities: Confirm insider-list restrictions, announcement triggers and permitted communications before signing, approval and completion.
Prepare leak responses, holding statements, spokesperson arrangements and escalation routes for reputational or service issues.
Test scenarios involving clients, colleagues, regulators, media and public-market disclosure where applicable.

milestones.name: Buyer and seller communications governance agreed (4 weeks)
activities: Define drafting, validation, approval and release responsibilities, including authority to contact clients and colleagues.
Agree joint review timelines, version control, sign-off evidence and escalation for delayed or conflicting messages.
Maintain a joint communications calendar aligned to regulatory approval, separation, cutover and completion milestones.

milestones.name: Client, colleague and regulator communications pack approved (6 weeks)
activities: Prepare tailored notices, FAQs, leader packs, frontline scripts and support routes for affected and retained audiences.
Sequence communications to preserve confidence, explain continuity and avoid disclosing information before approvals permit it.
Brief relationship managers, leaders, contact centres and employee representatives before each release.

milestones.name: Completion communications and post-sale monitoring completed (4 weeks)
activities: Execute regulatory, client, colleague, media and market communications in the approved completion sequence.
Monitor questions, sentiment, reputation, client attrition signals and service issues across all channels.
Refresh content, close communications issues and hand retained and residual obligations to BAU owners.

activitySets.heading: Partial Business Sale - additional divestment activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Transferred, retained and shared audiences segmented (5 weeks)
activities: Separate transferred, retained, excluded and shared client and colleague populations and their communication rights.
Develop differentiated messages, channels and support routes for each population while keeping the overall narrative coherent.
Reconcile audience lists with Human Capital, Product, Operations, Data Migration and Legal separation records.

milestones.name: Marketing asset separation and brand controls completed (6 weeks)
activities: Separate brand, campaign, website, social, data, sponsorship and collateral assets between transferred and retained businesses.
Define temporary brand use, co-branding, licensing, removal and approval requirements through separation.
Protect the retained Absa proposition through targeted reassurance, retention and market communications.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Sale A (buyer integrates) - further additional divestment activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Buyer integration communications handover agreed (5 weeks)
activities: Provide the buyer with approved stakeholder maps, message history, FAQs, communication commitments, open issues and channel information.
Agree the transition from Absa-led to buyer-led client, colleague and media communications.
Confirm Absa review rights and escalation routes where buyer integration messages affect retained obligations or reputation.

milestones.name: Absa exit brand and reputation protections implemented (4 weeks)
activities: Execute brand removal, asset transfer, public narrative and retained-business reassurance in line with the buyer integration plan.
Track misuse of Absa brand, inconsistent customer messaging and unresolved public or employee queries.
Transfer residual communications, claims and reputation issues to named Legal, BAU or post-completion owners.

milestones.name: Completion and market transition campaign executed (4 weeks)
activities: Coordinate completion announcements, client and colleague messages, website changes, social content and media activity.
Provide frontline teams with final buyer-integration messages and clear support routes.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Sale B (standalone) - complete divestment activity set
activitySets.lead: Standalone:

milestones.name: Standalone divestment stakeholder and communications strategy approved (5 weeks)
activities: Define the stakeholder narrative and outcomes for the standalone buyer, affected clients, colleagues, regulators, media and Absa retained business.

Agree how Absa and buyer narratives will remain aligned through completion and separation.

milestones.name: Buyer communications governance and capability assessed (5 weeks)
activities: Assess the buyer's communications and marketing team, approval routes, spokespersons, channels, agencies and crisis capability.

Agree BAU handover criteria, evidence and timing for standalone communications ownership.

milestones.name: Brand, marketing and channel separation completed (8 weeks)
activities: Inventory and separate brand rights, websites, social accounts, campaign assets, content, sponsorships, templates and physical collateral.
Define buyer identity, transition branding, market positioning and customer proposition for standalone operation.
Complete required asset transfer, licensing, de-branding, production and approval activity before LD1.

milestones.name: Client, colleague, regulator and media programmes approved (8 weeks)

milestones.name: Standalone launch campaign and digital information hub readied (6 weeks)

milestones.name: Completion, hypercare and final communications handover completed (8 weeks)

compliance.keyRole: Owns the compliance execution framework that makes the transaction controlled, regulator-ready and aligned to Absa policy.
responsibilities: Define applicable compliance obligations, approval paths, policy standards and completion evidence across the deal lifecycle.
Identify where conditions can be pre-agreed with regulators, and where data sharing can be agreed before full approval is received.
Identify compliance remediation, including regulatory approvals or notifications, policy exceptions, conduct risks, financial-crime controls, privacy constraints and outsourcing controls.
Advise on confidentiality, clean-room access, data sharing, client engagement, customer communications and restricted actions as the programme moves into execution
Validate local regulatory constraints that affect shared-service, Group Interchange, TSA and synergy assumptions with Finance & Tax, Legal & CorpDev and Regional Spokes.
Track compliance conditions, regulatory commitments, completion attestations and LD1 readiness evidence with the Central Hub.
Coordinate with Risk / Credit, KYC / AML, Data Migration, Product, Operations & Servicing, HR and Finance & Tax to embed compliance obligations in workstream plans.
boundaryItems: Legal & CorpDev owns formal legal advice, transaction-document drafting, legal opinions and legal sign-off where required.
KYC / AML owns file-level due diligence, screening and remediation execution; Compliance sets policy interpretation, approval standards and control expectations.
Risk / Credit owns risk appetite and credit decisions; Central Hub owns programme coordination; Compliance owns compliance interpretation, approvals and readiness evidence.
compliance.centralHubRelationship: Relationship with Central Hub: the SA Functional Spoke owns compliance execution decisions and evidence while the Central Hub sets programme standards, coordinates dependencies and escalates transaction-wide issues.
regionalRelationship: Regional Spokes should own local execution as a minimum, with ownership scaling based on maturity, including local regulatory engagement, submission drafting, local control evidence, monitoring of local conditions and country compliance actions where they have capacity and delegated authority.

Function Authority retains group compliance interpretation, policy standards, financial-crime, conduct, privacy and outsourcing positions, central challenge and execution ownership where regional maturity, capability or capacity is insufficient.

As regional maturity increases, local ownership should expand from evidence provision into local approval execution and regulator-facing activity, with Function Authority retaining group standards, specialist challenge and reserved approvals.

necessityRows.archetype: Balance Sheet Acquisition
necessityRows.rationale: Balance sheet archetypes usually do not include the transfer of real-estate assets, as these are often tied to employee transfer or larger business integration of branches, ATMs etc

necessityRows.archetype: Partial Business Acquisition
necessityRows.rationale: Required if the partial perimeter includes real estate asset transfer such as offices, branches, or ATMs

necessityRows.archetype: Full Business Acquisition A (Buyer integrates the business)
necessityRows.rationale: Core because these archetypes usually involve early estate diligence, workplace design, property transfer, fit-out, employee moves, certifications and portfolio optimization, ATM/branch rationalization where required

necessityRows.archetype: Full Business Acquisition B (Buyer runs the business standalone)
necessityRows.rationale: Core because these archetypes usually involve early estate diligence, workplace design, property transfer, fit-out, employee moves, certifications and portfolio optimization, ATM/branch rationalization where required

necessityRows.archetype: Balance Sheet Sale
necessityRows.rationale: Balance sheet archetypes usually do not include the transfer of real-estate assets, as these are often tied to employee transfer or larger business integration of branches, ATMs etc

necessityRows.archetype: Partial Business Sale
necessityRows.rationale: Required if the partial perimeter includes real estate asset transfer such as offices, branches, or ATMs

necessityRows.archetype: Full Business Sale A (Buyer integrates the business)
necessityRows.rationale: Core because these archetypes usually involve early estate diligence, workplace design, property transfer, fit-out, employee moves, certifications and portfolio optimization, ATM/branch rationalization where required

necessityRows.rationale: Core because these archetypes usually involve early estate diligence, workplace design, property transfer, fit-out, employee moves, certifications and portfolio optimization, ATM/branch rationalization where required

cres.keyRole: Protects business continuity across the property estate while delivering the property, facilities and workplace changes required for integration, separation and longer-term estate optimisation. CRES confirms that critical premises and workplace services are operationally ready for LD1 and that property obligations are controlled through transition.
responsibilities: Engage from due diligence to define the property and facilities perimeter, identify critical premises and surface long-lead estate dependencies before transaction terms and plans are fixed.
Assess owned and leased properties, occupancy, capacity, condition, utilisation, critical services, property contracts, costs, constraints and opportunities across the transaction perimeter.
Define the estate strategy and treatment for each location, including retain, transfer, assign, consolidate, relocate, fit out, share, sublet, terminate or dispose.
Develop property options, affordability assessments, business cases, capital and operating cost estimates, architecture input and governance submissions.
Manage leases, property agreements, landlord interfaces and facilities contracts with Legal, Procurement, Finance & Tax and in-country CRES teams.
Plan and deliver workplace design, construction, fit-out, moves, facilities mobilisation and long-lead procurement, allowing up to six months where new or materially changed premises are required.
Coordinate certifications, health and safety, physical security, access control, parking, utilities, workplace technology, cleaning, maintenance, catering and employee-facing workplace services.
Own the end-to-end workplace journey with Human Capital and Change Management, including employee impact,
Define and execute plans for branch and ATM rationalization and harmonization where required, driven by in-country teams
boundaryItems: CRES owns the property, workplace and facilities journey; Human Capital and Change Management own broader people impacts, communications and adoption with CRES input.
Procurement owns commercial sourcing and supplier process; CRES defines property and facilities requirements, technical specifications, service standards and acceptance evidence.
cres.centralHubRelationship: Relationship with Central Hub: CRES owns property, facilities and workplace decisions and evidence while the Central Hub integrates the estate roadmap into the programme plan, tracks long-lead dependencies and budget impacts, applies quality assurance and escalates readiness risks.
regionalRelationship: Regional Spokes should own local execution as a minimum, with ownership scaling based on maturity, including site surveys, landlord and supplier engagement, local approvals, facilities mobilisation, moves and readiness evidence where capability and capacity allow. Regional teams must own ATM and branch-related activities

Function Authority retains estate strategy, standards, architecture, affordability challenge, complex property decisions and execution ownership where regional maturity, capability or capacity is insufficient.

As regional maturity increases, ownership should expand from local evidence and coordination into end-to-end country estate delivery, with Function Authority retaining standards, specialist challenge and reserved approvals.

mandateRows.hubRole: Integrates site decisions, dependencies, assumptions and timing into the programme plan and decision calendar.
mandateRows.governance: CRES leadership, deal sponsor, business owner, Finance & Tax, Legal & CorpDev and country leadership.
mandateRows.escalation: Critical site, occupancy, ownership, lease, customer or operational dependency is unclear or disputed.

spokeAuthority: Recommends estate option, design basis, affordability, capital and operating spend, and property business case.
mandateRows.hubRole: Tests plan and budget impact, coordinates governance and tracks approved spend against the integrated plan.
mandateRows.governance: CRES investment governance, Finance & Tax, Procurement and accountable executive approvals.
mandateRows.escalation: Funding gap, approval delay, long-lead item or affordability issue threatens readiness.

mandateRows.area: Lease, property contract and landlord route
spokeAuthority: Defines required assignment, novation, variation, termination, new lease, consent and landlord negotiation positions.
mandateRows.hubRole: Tracks legal, counterparty and completion dependencies and escalates delays through programme governance.
mandateRows.governance: CRES, Legal & CorpDev, Procurement, Finance & Tax and local governance as applicable.
mandateRows.escalation: Consent, title, lease, contract or landlord issue affects transaction terms, occupancy or LD1.

spokeAuthority: Approves functional requirements, workplace standards, architecture, fit-out scope, facilities model and acceptance criteria.
mandateRows.hubRole: Coordinates cross-workstream dependencies, critical path, budget and readiness reporting.
mandateRows.governance: CRES design and delivery governance, Physical Security, Technology, Human Capital, Change and country leadership.
mandateRows.escalation: Design freeze, contractor, certification, technology, security or move dependency threatens delivery.

spokeAuthority: Defines the plan and required activities to rationalise ATMs and Branches, working alongside product and technology teams to assess location and usage
mandateRows.hubRole: Coordinates cross-workstream dependencies, critical path, budget and readiness reporting.
mandateRows.governance: CRES, Legal & CorpDev, Procurement, Business, Technology and local governance as applicable.

activities: Deliver partitions, access changes, signage, move activity, storage, equipment and workplace technology dependencies.
Coordinate employee and customer communications, site disruption controls and move support.
Validate separation effectiveness, service continuity and residual safety or security exceptions.

milestones.name: LD1 premises transition and residual handover completed (8 weeks)
activities: Implement access, security, facilities, signage, records, workplace and employee service changes.
Confirm buyer and Absa retained premises are safe, operational and appropriately separated at LD1.
Hand over retained obligations, TSA services, open defects and property actions to named post-close owners.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Sale A (buyer integrates) - further additional divestment activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Buyer integration estate handover agreed (6 weeks)
activities: Define the property data, lease, asset, facilities, compliance and site-operating pack required by the buyer.
Confirm buyer integration actions align with property rights, consents, customer needs and Absa retained obligations.
Set handover acceptance criteria, owners and dates through joint readiness governance.

milestones.name: Absa premises exits and consolidation delivered (10 weeks)
activities: Plan and execute relocations, closures, lease exits, asset removals and reinstatement obligations.
Coordinate contractors, suppliers, employee moves and service continuity across the affected portfolio.
Evidence vacant possession, decommissioning, landlord acceptance and financial close-out where required.

milestones.name: Retained exposure and TSA exit closed (10 weeks)
activities: Track residual leases, guarantees, shared services, access rights, defects, claims and buyer dependencies after LD1.
Complete TSA exit, access removal, supplier changes and property obligation transfer.
Close or transfer remaining risks with approved evidence and accountable BAU owners.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Sale B (standalone) - complete divestment activity set
activitySets.lead: Standalone:

milestones.name: Standalone estate sale perimeter and strategy approved (8 weeks)
activities: Define the complete estate, facilities, supplier, employee and compliance perimeter required by the buyer.
Set the property transfer route, buyer standalone assumptions, retained Absa obligations and critical dates.
Approve the separation roadmap, governance, cost and evidence standards.

milestones.name: Buyer standalone facilities model mobilised (12 weeks)
activities: Confirm buyer facilities leadership, country execution capability, supplier model, standards and escalation routes.
Establish utilities, maintenance, cleaning, security, workplace and other essential service arrangements.
Test supplier mobilisation, contract readiness and operating procedures before completion.

milestones.name: Leases, titles and property contracts transferred (10 weeks)
activities: Complete due diligence, landlord negotiation, title actions, consents, assignments, novations and notices.
Track buyer and Absa conditions, documents, payments and evidence against the completion plan.
Resolve rejected consents or delayed transfers through approved interim or TSA arrangements.

milestones.name: Standalone workplace readiness demonstrated (10 weeks)
activities: Deliver required fit-out, access, facilities, safety, security, signage, storage and workplace technology dependencies.
Complete certifications, inspections, site readiness reviews and remediation across all critical premises.
Confirm employee and customer journeys can operate without unsupported Absa intervention.

milestones.name: Completion and property handover executed (6 weeks)
activities: Execute site, key, access, asset, record, contract and compliance evidence handover to the buyer.
Operate joint command and escalation arrangements for property and facilities issues through LD1.
Confirm retained Absa locations, information and physical assets remain protected.

milestones.name: Residual property obligations and TSA services closed (12 weeks)
activities: Monitor service performance, lease or title actions, claims, defects, reinstatement and retained exposure after completion.
Complete TSA exit, access removal, supplier separation and evidence archive.
Transfer any remaining obligations to accountable buyer or Absa BAU owners and close programme governance.

data-migration.keyRole: Owns the data migration delivery path from source-to-target mapping through cutover and reconciliation
responsibilities: Agree source and target data dictionaries, source-system access, target-system requirements and secure transfer protocols
Define source-to-target mapping, transformation logic, data cleansing, exception handling and reconciliation approach
Conduct data quality assessments, both on the structure and business usage of masked fields, and the detailed content of unmasked fields once received
Build and test migration routines, controlled extracts, mock loads, reporting data feeds and rollback
Coordinate data cuts, dress rehearsals, final data load, reconciliation and migration sign-off
Manage data migration defects, quality issues, lineage evidence and handover to BAU data owners.
boundaryItems: Technology owns environments, interfaces and platform build
Independent Assurance independently validates migration design and results
Business workstreams own the business meaning and acceptance criteria for their data fields
data-migration.centralHubRelationship: Relationship with Central Hub: the SA Functional Spoke owns data migration decisions and plan which should form the backbone of the programme plan owned by the Central Hub
regionalRelationship: Regional Spokes should own local execution as a minimum, with ownership scaling based on maturity, including source-data evidence, local data-owner sign-off, cleansing, reconciliation support, cutover steps and exception resolution where they have capacity and delegated authority.

Function Authority retains migration design, source-to-target standards, central tooling, reconciliation methodology, control evidence standards and execution ownership where regional maturity, capability or capacity is insufficient.

As regional maturity increases, local ownership should expand from evidence provision into data cleansing, reconciliation, mock-load support and cutover activity, with Function Authority retaining standards, specialist challenge and reserved approvals.

milestoneIntro: The key milestones below are organised as a baseline set, with additional milestones required for more complex deal archetypes split out below as required.

As deal archetypes scale from balance sheet to partial business to full business, each baseline activity should be assessed against the complexity factors laid out in the deal archetype documentation.
Service catalogue:
serviceCatalogue: Source to target mapping
Migration solution design
ETL solution build and test
Cutover planning
Dress rehearsal coordination and leadership

activitySets.heading: Balance Sheet Acquisition - baseline activities

milestones.name: Data migration solution and data dictionary requirements defined (4 weeks)
activities: Confirm data domains, source systems, target systems, field ownership, mandatory attributes and record-level controls for the transaction perimeter.
Agree data dictionaries, naming standards, reference data, data lineage expectations and evidence required for business acceptance.
Define transfer protocols, controls, permissions and storage locations for files

milestones.name: Data structure and usage assessment (2 weeks)
activities: Work with counterparty to assess the structure of data tables and structures provided in a masked format, to understand key differences, gaps, and quality issues
Engage both Absa and Counterparty business stakeholders to understand what each field is actually used for, and whether there are any key differences between Absa and Counterparty practices

milestones.name: Source-to-target mapping conducted and business sign off secured (5 weeks)
activities: Profile source data, identify quality gaps and map each source field to target fields, business rules and transformation logic
Confirm Product, Operations, Finance, Risk and Compliance acceptance for the business meaning of mapped fields
Track unresolved mapping decisions, assumptions and exclusions

milestones.name: Data migration ETL solution design complete (6 weeks)
activities: Design extraction, transformation, load, validation, exception handling and reconciliations
Define control totals, balancing checks, audit trail, rollback approach and defect severity rules
Confirm Technology environment, connectivity, storage and scheduling dependencies needed to run the ETL solution

milestones.name: Data migration ETL solution build complete (8 weeks)
activities: Build ETL routines, migration scripts, validation reports, exception reports and reconciliation outputs.
Configure access, environments, run controls and source-file intake processes with Technology.
Complete unit testing and evidence capture before handing into SIT or mock-run cycles.

milestones.name: Data migration testing, including build, SIT, and mock runs (6 weeks)
activities: Run build testing, SIT, data-quality testing and mock migration cycles against agreed success criteria.
Validate completeness, accuracy, record counts, balances, rejected records, exceptions and usability
Log defects, retest fixes and obtain acceptance for exceptions from data owners and business

milestones.name: Unmasked data quality assessment (1 week)
activities: Conduct a full data quality assessment on unmasked data once received
Flag any material quality issues, structural differences, or unexpected deviations from masked data previously provided
Define remediation plan or operational workarounds for cutover

milestones.name: Cutover planning conducted (2 weeks)
activities: Build the data cutover runbook covering extracts, freezes, transfer windows, load sequence, validations, rollback and communications
Align cutover timing with Technology, Operations, E2E Testing, Finance, Risk, Compliance and Client Readiness.
Confirm owners, timings, dependencies, evidence and fallback decision points for final load

milestones.name: Dress Rehearsals led and assessed (3 weeks)
activities: Run dress rehearsals using production-like data, production-like timing and agreed success criteria
Assess rehearsal outcomes for data quality, run duration, reconciliation, exception handling and downstream readiness.
Update migration design, cutover runbook and readiness evidence based on rehearsal findings.

milestones.name: Data Migration readiness assessed (2 weeks)
activities: Issue a readiness view covering mapping, build, testing, reconciliation, exceptions, cutover plan and residual data risks.
Confirm no unresolved data-quality issue prevents go/no-go, regulatory evidence, customer outcomes or financial reporting.
Transfer open data actions to hypercare or BAU with clear ownership

activitySets.heading: Partial Business Acquisition - additional activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Assessment of data perimeter undertaken (3 weeks)
activities: Separate transferring, retained, shared and excluded records, including customer, product, operational, employee and reporting data
Define data ownership and retention requirements across Absa and counterparty
Identify data sets that require local country input, privacy review, regulator consideration or business sign-off

milestones.name: Employee data scoped and solution built (8 weeks)
activities: Confirm employee data fields required for consultation, onboarding, payroll, benefits, pensions and HR systems.
Apply privacy, access, masking or unmasked data controls with Human Capital, Legal, Compliance and Technology.
Build and test secure employee data extracts, validations and transfer evidence.

milestones.name: Technology platform transfer data requirements understood and solution built (8 weeks)
activities: Identify platform, access, configuration, reference-data and reporting data needed to support technology transfer or integration.
Agree hand-off boundaries with Technology - data migration owns data content and Technology owns platform build and environments
Build and test feeds, files, conversion rules and reconciliation outputs required for platform transfer.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Acquisition A (integrated) - further additional activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: External data migration assurance partners engaged and collaboration underway (3 weeks)
activities: Confirm assurance scope, evidence requests, data access, sample approach and timing with Independent Assurance and external partners.
Align assurance work with Risk, Internal Audit, Technology and Client readiness to avoid duplicate evidence requests.
Track assurance findings and remediation actions through migration governance.

milestones.name: Assessment of external parallel solution to Absa solution accuracy, and remediation (7 weeks)
activities: Compare external parallel-build results to Absa migration outputs across record counts, balances, samples, rejects and exceptions.
Investigate variances, agree root cause, update transformation logic or source data remediation and retest
Document accepted residual differences with accountable business, Finance and Risk owners.

milestones.name: Joint agreement on data migration readiness with external assurance (2 weeks)
activities: Obtain readiness agreement covering mapping, ETL build, mock runs, dress rehearsals, reconciliations and residual defects.
Confirm readiness evidence can support LD1 go/no-go
Agree post-LD1 monitoring and exception ownership with data owners

activitySets.heading: Full Business Acquisition B (standalone) - new activity set

milestones.name: Assessment of data perimeter undertaken (3 weeks)
activities: Define the full data perimeter required for standalone operation, including customer, product, finance, risk, compliance, employee, supplier and reporting data.
Identify retained seller data, Absa-owned data, third-party data and local country data required for Day 1 and BAU operation.
Agree data governance, data owners, retention requirements and privacy controls for the standalone business.

milestones.name: Source-to-target mapping conducted and business sign off secured (5 weeks)
activities: Map all required source fields to standalone target systems, reporting structures, controls and operating processes.
Confirm business, product owner, operations, finance, risk and compliance acceptance for mapped data and exclusions.
Track unresolved mapping decisions through governance

milestones.name: Data migration ETL solution design complete (6 weeks)
activities: Design full extraction, transformation, load, validation, reconciliation, audit and rollback routines for standalone
Define migration run sequencing for core systems, channels, reporting platforms, HR systems and supplier or third-party data feeds
Confirm environment, integration and infrastructure requirements with Technology.

milestones.name: Data migration ETL solution build complete (8 weeks)
activities: Build migration routines, validation reports, exception reporting, reconciliation dashboards and evidence outputs.
Configure secure data stores, transfer processes, scheduling and access controls.
Complete build testing and technical readiness checks before mock-runs

milestones.name: Data migration testing, including build, SIT, and mock runs (6 weeks)
activities: Run iterative SIT and mock migration cycles using production-like volumes and business acceptance criteria
Validate completeness, accuracy, timeliness, control totals, downstream usability and reporting outputs
Remediate defects, retest fixes and confirm exceptions

milestones.name: Cutover planning conducted (2 weeks)
activities: Build a data cutover runbook covering source freezes, final extracts, load windows, validations, rollback and readiness reporting.
Align data cutover with Technology deployment, Operations readiness, Finance reporting, HR onboarding and Compliance obligations.
Confirm resource coverage, run ownership and escalation for cutover and post-LD1 data issues.

milestones.name: Dress Rehearsals led and assessed (3 weeks)
activities: Run dress rehearsals across all data domains needed for the standalone operating model.
Measure run duration, failure points, reconciliation performance, exception handling and downstream process readiness.
Update migration routines, operating procedures and readiness evidence after each rehearsal.

milestones.name: Data Migration readiness assessed (2 weeks)
activities: Issue final readiness evidence covering full data migration scope, build, tests, defects, reconciliation, cutover and residual risks.
Confirm data owners, Technology, Risk, Compliance, Finance and Independent Assurance accept readiness or residual issues.
Transfer open defects and monitoring obligations into hypercare and BAU data governance.

activitySets.heading: Balance Sheet Sale - baseline divestment activities

milestones.name: Data migration solution and data dictionary requirements defined alongside buyer (6 weeks)
activities: Agree buyer and Absa data requirements, file formats, data dictionary, field definitions, controls and evidence standards
Confirm secure transfer protocols, confidentiality constraints, privacy requirements and regulatory limits on data sharing
Define buyer and seller ownership for mapping queries, rejected records, reconciliation and acceptance

milestones.name: Assessment of retained data assets and data perimeter undertaken (3 weeks)
activities: Identify data that transfers, data that remains with Absa, shared records, historical records, reporting data and excluded records.
Confirm Absa retention, archive, access removal, legal hold and regulator requirements
Map data dependencies to Finance, Risk, Compliance, Operations, Technology and Legal obligations.

milestones.name: Support of buyer with source-to-target mapping complete (5 weeks)
activities: Provide source data definitions, lineage, sample files, field logic and guidance to support mapping
Respond to buyer mapping queries through the Central Hub and formal issue process.
Track buyer acceptance, open questions and mapping risks that affect transfer readiness.

milestones.name: Data cuts pulled and provided to buyer (4 weeks)
activities: Extract agreed data cuts in line with timing, approval, privacy and confidentiality controls
Validate record counts, balances, control totals, completeness and file integrity before transfer.

milestones.name: Joint testing of the migration solution complete (6 weeks)
activities: Support buyer test cycles with source-file explanations, defect triage and reconciliation evidence.
Validate Absa-side extract routines, retained data controls and transfer evidence.

milestones.name: Dress rehearsals led from Absa perspective, supporting buyer activities (3 weeks)
activities: Run Absa extract and transfer steps during buyer dress rehearsals using agreed success criteria.
Confirm timing, file transfer, evidence capture, exception handling and escalation routes work as planned.
Update Absa runbooks and buyer hand-off processes based on rehearsal outcomes.

milestones.name: Absa readiness to provide accurate and complete data assessed (2 weeks)
activities: Issue an Absa readiness view covering data completeness, accuracy, extract controls, transfer controls and open defects.
Confirm readiness with Legal, Compliance, Risk, Finance and relevant data owners before LD1.
Transfer residual issues to post-LD1 support or BAU owners.

activitySets.heading: Partial Business Sale - additional divestment activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Employee data scoped and provided to buyer (6 weeks)
activities: Agree employee data fields, privacy controls, approvals, timing and transfer route with Human Capital, Legal and Compliance.
Validate completeness, accuracy and file integrity before buyer transfer.

milestones.name: Technology platform data required for transfer scoped and provided (8 weeks)
activities: Identify platform, access, configuration, reporting and reference data required by the buyer for transfer
Confirm with Technology which data is required for platform readiness and which remains a technology build responsibility.
Extract, validate and transfer agreed platform data through controlled channels.

milestones.name: Retained and shared data controls confirmed (6 weeks)
activities: Define controls for shared data, retained records, data access, reporting and TSA-backed processes
Validate that Absa retained data remains complete, accurate and available after transfer.
Confirm data owner handover and monitoring for post-LD1 exceptions.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Sale A (buyer integrates) - further additional divestment activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: External data migration assurance partners engaged and collaboration underway (3 weeks)
activities: Agree assurance scope, evidence needs, data access and timing with the buyer, Independent Assurance and external partners.
Coordinate assurance activity with Risk, Technology, Legal and Client Readiness.
Track findings, remediation and sign-off dependencies through joint governance.

milestones.name: Assessment of external parallel solution to Absa solution accuracy, and remediation (7 weeks)
activities: Compare Absa extract outputs to external or buyer parallel results across counts, balances, samples, rejects and exceptions.
Investigate differences, correct source extracts or transformation logic and retest.
Agree residual variances with buyer, Finance, Risk and data owners.

milestones.name: Joint agreement on data migration readiness with external assurance (2 weeks)
activities: Secure agreement on data readiness, open defects, accepted residual risks and post-LD1 monitoring.
Confirm assurance evidence can support integration, Absa exit controls
Transfer residual data issues to buyer, Absa BAU or post-completion obligation owners.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Sale B (standalone) - complete divestment activity set

milestones.name: Assessment of data migration solution requirements from Absa group to support standalone run state (7 weeks)
activities: Define data Absa must provide for the buyer to run the divested business standalone, including historical, operational, regulatory and reporting data.
Confirm data dependencies linked to TSA services, buyer platform build, local country requirements and retained Absa obligations.
Agree evidence standards and data ownership for post-completion support.

milestones.name: Data migration solution and data dictionary requirements defined alongside buyer (6 weeks)
activities: Agree target file formats, field definitions, lineage, validation rules, privacy controls and acceptance criteria with the buyer.
Define data dictionary ownership, mapping query process and version control.
Confirm access, confidentiality and approval gates before data is shared.

milestones.name: Support of buyer with source-to-target mapping complete (5 weeks)
activities: Provide source-system definitions, data lineage, transformation assumptions and sample records to support buyer mapping.
Resolve buyer queries and local country data questions through the formal issue route.
Track buyer mapping acceptance and open risks through joint governance.

milestones.name: Data cuts pulled and provided to buyer (4 weeks)
activities: Execute agreed data extracts, quality checks, control totals and secure file transfers.
Evidence file versions, approvals, transfer times, buyer receipt and reconciliation results.
Manage rejected records, late data changes and restatement requirements.

milestones.name: Joint testing of the migration solution complete (6 weeks)
activities: Support buyer testing and Absa-side retained control testing across standalone run-state data.
Validate transferred data against agreed completeness, accuracy and usability criteria.
Close defects or agree residual issues with accountable owners.

milestones.name: Absa readiness to provide accurate and complete data assessed (2 weeks)
activities: Issue final Absa data readiness sign-off for standalone transfer, including retained records and post-LD1 support obligations.
Confirm open exceptions, monitoring and ownership with buyer, Legal, Compliance, Risk and Finance.
Archive migration evidence for audit, regulator and post-completion dispute support.

e2e-testing.name: E2E Testing

necessityRows.archetype: Balance Sheet Acquisition
necessityRows.rationale: Required to prove data, account, system, reporting, servicing and controls are working correctly, but can be scaled up as build completion approaches

necessityRows.archetype: Partial Business Acquisition
necessityRows.rationale: Required because these archetypes introduce material process and platform changes which must be trained end to end

necessityRows.archetype: Full Business Acquisition A (Buyer integrates the business)
necessityRows.rationale: Required because these archetypes introduce material process and platform changes which must be trained end to end

necessityRows.archetype: Full Business Acquisition B (Buyer runs the business standalone)
necessityRows.rationale: Required because these archetypes introduce material process and platform changes which must be trained end to end

necessityRows.archetype: Balance Sheet Sale
necessityRows.rationale: Not required as large scale impact is usually limited, and testing can be absorbed into business / tech functions

necessityRows.archetype: Partial Business Sale
necessityRows.rationale: Conditional based on the scale of change impacting the retained business

necessityRows.archetype: Full Business Sale A (Buyer integrates the business)
necessityRows.rationale: Required to test buyer integration dependencies, Absa exit controls, retained services and post-LD1 support flows.

necessityRows.archetype: Full Business Sale B (Buyer runs the business as standalone)
necessityRows.rationale: Conditional based on the scale of change impacting the retained business

e2e-testing.keyRole: Owns end-to-end testing strategy, execution evidence, testing coordination, and defect governance across customer, colleague, data, technology, operations, supplier and readiness journeys.
responsibilities: Define end-to-end test strategy, test scope, entry criteria, exit criteria, evidence standards and defect governance.
Define success criteria for mock runs and dress rehearsals before execution, including data completeness, accuracy, reconciliation and operational acceptance.
Coordinate test journeys across Data Migration, Technology, Operations, Finance, Risk, Compliance, Procurement, HR, Change and Legal dependencies.
Coordinate testing of customer, colleague, system, reporting, control, digital, cards, supplier, payment and servicing journeys that affect LD1 readiness.
Maintain defect triage, retest, acceptance, workaround and residual-risk evidence through readiness governance.
Provide test evidence into LD1 go/no-go, assurance, regulator, Internal Audit and post-LD1 hypercare decisions.
boundaryItems: Technology owns technical build, environments and technical test execution; E2E Testing owns integrated journey coverage and evidence completeness.
Data Migration owns migration execution and reconciliations; E2E Testing validates that migrated data supports end-to-end business outcomes
Operations & Servicing owns operational process design and acceptance; E2E Testing validates that processes work across hand-offs.
Business, operations, and technology teams own the execution of testing, E2E Testing facilitates and coordinates
Risk and Independent Assurance challenge testing evidence, success criteria and residual risk acceptance.
e2e-testing.centralHubRelationship: Relationship with Central Hub: E2E Testing owns test design, execution evidence and defect governance while the Central Hub coordinates cross-workstream dependencies, decision cadence, issue escalation and readiness reporting.
regionalRelationship: Regional Spokes should own local execution as a minimum, with ownership scaling based on maturity, including process walkthroughs, user acceptance support, local data and testers, mock runs, dress rehearsals, defect retesting and local evidence production where they have capacity and delegated authority.

Function Authority retains test strategy, entry and exit criteria, evidence standards, integrated journey coverage, defect governance and execution ownership where regional maturity, capability or capacity is insufficient.

As regional maturity increases, local ownership should expand from test support into local execution, defect remediation and readiness sign-off, with Function Authority retaining standards, specialist challenge and reserved approvals.

mandateRows.area: Test strategy, scope and success criteria
spokeAuthority: Defines E2E test strategy, journeys, entry and exit criteria, mock run and dress rehearsal success criteria.
mandateRows.hubRole: Coordinates cross-workstream agreement and tracks readiness implications.
mandateRows.governance: E2E Testing, Client Readiness, Technology, Operations, Data Migration, Risk and Independent Assurance.
mandateRows.escalation: Success criteria are undefined, scope omits digital/cards/local journeys, or test entry criteria are not met.

spokeAuthority: Validates that migrated data supports business outcomes, reporting, controls and reconciliations.
mandateRows.hubRole: Tracks defects, evidence and cross-workstream dependencies.
mandateRows.governance: Data Migration, Finance, Risk, Compliance, Operations and IA where required.
mandateRows.escalation: Data completeness or accuracy cannot be evidenced, or no owner can confirm comfort with the data.

mandateRows.area: Digital, cards and operational journey coverage
spokeAuthority: Owns integrated test coverage for digital journeys, cards, operations, servicing, customer and colleague outcomes.
mandateRows.hubRole: Coordinates dependency resolution where test outcomes affect LD1.
mandateRows.governance: Technology, Operations, Product, Cards, Digital, Risk and LD1 governance.
mandateRows.escalation: Digital readiness is uncertain, 70k cards production is untested, or operational hand-offs fail.

spokeAuthority: Controls defect triage, retest, workaround evidence, acceptance criteria and residual test risk view.
mandateRows.hubRole: Escalates defects affecting LD1 or assurance evidence.
mandateRows.governance: E2E Testing, Risk, Independent Assurance, workstream owners and programme SteerCo.
mandateRows.escalation: Defects remain open without accepted workaround, or residual test risk is not approved.

spokeAuthority: Provides E2E testing recommendation for LD1 readiness, completion or cutover decision forums.
mandateRows.hubRole: Integrates recommendation into go/no-go pack and governance minutes.
mandateRows.governance: Client Readiness, accountable executive, programme SteerCo and relevant control functions.
mandateRows.escalation: Go/no-go decision proceeds without evidence, local sign-off or accepted test exceptions.

capabilityRows.category: Specific Project Manager required?
capabilityRows.content: No - E2E Testing is effectively a project management / onboarding oversight function focused on tracking testing coverage and execution. The workstream lead must have project management capabilities

capabilityRows.category: Baseline capabilities
capabilityRows.content: Test strategy definition, testing best practice, test case definition, acceptance criteria, project management, data analysis, stakeholder management

capabilityRows.category: Incremental capabilities by deal archetype / complexity
capabilityRows.content: Testing of complex business process change, employee/HR systems testing, production testing

capabilityRows.category: Specialist capabilities triggered by deal characteristics
capabilityRows.content: Understanding of product specific testing requirements (e.g., testing of back to back trades), physical process testing (e.g., facilities)
