Data completeness and accuracy test evidence
Digital, cards and operational readiness testing
Defect triage, retest and acceptance
Local and counterparty test coordination
Readiness evidence for assurance and go/no-go
Hypercare test defect transition

activitySets.heading: Balance Sheet Acquisition - baseline activities

milestones.name: E2E test strategy and scope agreed (3 weeks)
activities: Define integrated test journeys, scenarios, entry criteria, exit criteria, evidence standards and ownership.
Include customer, colleague, data, operations, technology, finance, risk, compliance, supplier and reporting hand-offs.
Confirm local and counterparty participation required for each test journey.

milestones.name: Data completeness and accuracy test criteria defined (3 weeks)
activities: Agree how the programme will evidence comfort with data completeness and accuracy.
Define reconciliation thresholds, exception handling, data owner sign-off and defect severity rules.
Align data testing with Risk, Independent Assurance, Finance, Compliance and Data Migration.

milestones.name: Defect governance and retest cadence live (2 weeks)
activities: Operate defect triage, owner allocation, retest scheduling, workaround assessment and acceptance decisions.
Escalate defects that affect regulatory approval, CPs, risk appetite, customer outcomes or LD1 timing.
Maintain test evidence and residual-risk decisions in the readiness pack.

milestones.name: LD1 test recommendation issued (1 week)
activities: Provide E2E test status, unresolved defects, accepted workarounds and residual test risk for go/no-go.
Confirm hypercare monitoring for post-LD1 test defects and operational issues.
Transfer open defects to BAU or hypercare owners.

activitySets.heading: Partial Business Acquisition - additional activities

milestones.name: Partial perimeter journey coverage completed (4 weeks)
activities: Test transferring, retained and shared service journeys across Absa, counterparty and country hand-offs.
Validate TSA-supported processes, retained-service controls and exception routing.
Confirm customer, account, reporting and operational outcomes for in-scope and out-of-scope items.

milestones.name: Local and counterparty test execution mobilised (4 weeks)
activities: Assign local testers, evidence owners and counterparty participants for each shared journey.
Confirm environment access, test data and availability for country teams.
Escalate participation or evidence gaps through Central Hub governance.

milestones.name: Boundary defects and workarounds accepted (2 weeks)
activities: Track defects where ownership crosses buyer, seller, country, central or TSA boundaries.
Validate workarounds and residual risk with Risk and Independent Assurance.
Confirm partial acquisition test readiness for LD1 and post-LD1 monitoring.

activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

activitySets.heading: Full Business Acquisition A (integrated) - further additional activities

milestones.name: Integrated business journey testing completed (6 weeks)
activities: Test full integrated customer, colleague, operations, finance, compliance, risk and reporting journeys.
Validate migrated data through downstream systems, controls and customer outcomes.
Confirm user acceptance and local execution evidence where country activity remains in scope.

milestones.name: Digital and cards readiness tested (4 weeks)
activities: Include digital onboarding, servicing, channel access, customer notifications and issue flows in E2E scope.
Plan and execute high-volume cards testing, including 70k card production, fulfilment, activation and servicing where relevant.
Escalate readiness gaps where digital or cards testing affects customer go-live.

milestones.name: Dress rehearsal exit recommendation agreed (1 week)
activities: Assess dress rehearsal outcomes against pre-agreed success criteria.
Confirm data, systems, people, supplier and operational evidence supports go-live.
Provide defect, workaround and residual risk view to Client Readiness and Risk.

activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

activitySets.heading: Full Business Acquisition B (standalone) - new activity set

milestones.name: Standalone test estate and governance established (5 weeks)
activities: Define standalone test environments, data, access, users, tools, defect workflow and evidence repository.
Confirm test coverage for every standalone operating process required at LD1.
Set governance cadence for testing, assurance, readiness and local sign-off.

milestones.name: Full standalone lifecycle testing completed (6 weeks)
activities: Test customer, product, finance, people, supplier, operations, risk, compliance and reporting lifecycles.
Validate control operation, system access, data flows, reconciliations and issue escalation without seller support.
Confirm local and central teams can operate test-passed processes from LD1.

milestones.name: Cutover and command-centre rehearsals completed (4 weeks)
activities: Run cutover, fallback, command-centre, incident and communications rehearsals before LD1.
Confirm success criteria and go/no-go inputs for standalone launch.
Transition open defects into hypercare with named owners.

activitySets.heading: Balance Sheet Sale - baseline divestment activities
activitySets.lead: Not required

activitySets.heading: Partial Business Sale - additional divestment activities

milestones.name: Carve-out and TSA test journeys designed (3 weeks)
activities: Test shared-service, TSA, retained Absa and buyer journeys across all hand-offs.
Confirm test scenarios for access, data, reports, customer outcomes, supplier dependencies and operational exceptions.
Define success criteria for TSA entry and TSA exit readiness.

milestones.name: Boundary and local execution testing completed (6 weeks)
activities: Validate in-country journeys, buyer interactions and retained Absa processes where local execution remains material.
Track defects by buyer, seller, country and TSA owner.
Confirm workarounds and residual risks are accepted before LD1.

milestones.name: TSA exit test plan launched (3 weeks)
activities: Plan regression and exit testing for shared-service wind-down.
Track defects that could extend TSA reliance or Absa obligations.
Provide test evidence to TSA exit governance.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Sale A (buyer integrates) - further additional divestment activities

milestones.name: Buyer integration test dependencies aligned (5 weeks)
activities: Agree buyer and Absa test responsibilities, environments, data, cutover windows and evidence-sharing constraints.
Validate buyer integration dependencies that affect Absa retained services or TSA obligations.
Escalate buyer readiness gaps through joint governance.

milestones.name: Absa exit and retained control tests completed (5 weeks)
activities: Test Absa access removal, retained reporting, data separation, supplier exits and TSA-supported hand-offs.
Confirm Absa controls remain effective while the buyer integrates the business.
Provide readiness evidence for integration dependency closure.

milestones.name: Post-LD1 defect ownership transferred (3 weeks)
activities: Transfer defects to buyer, Absa BAU, TSA or post-completion obligation owners.
Monitor post-LD1 issues until buyer integration risks no longer affect Absa.
Archive test evidence for audit and dispute support.

activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

activitySets.heading: Full Business Sale B (standalone) - complete divestment activity set

milestones.name: Buyer standalone test scope confirmed (3 weeks)
activities: Define buyer standalone test evidence Absa requires before service exit or obligation closure.
Confirm tests for data, controls, reporting, access, customers, employees, suppliers and operations.
Agree evidence-sharing, confidentiality and sign-off route with Legal and the buyer.

milestones.name: Full separation and exit testing completed (6 weeks)
activities: Test Absa exit from systems, services, supplier support, customer support and data access.
Validate buyer standalone readiness where Absa retains risk until exit evidence is accepted.
Escalate defects that could delay TSA exit, regulatory approval or post-completion closure.

milestones.name: Final test evidence archive completed (1 week)
activities: Archive go/no-go packs, test results, defects, approvals, workarounds and closure evidence.
Confirm all defects have buyer, Absa BAU or legal obligation owners.
Close E2E Testing when residual issues are no longer programme-owned.

finance-tax.keyRole: Owns finance and tax execution from deal economics through completion and LD1. Owns Group Interchange, TSA operation and BAU transition, and ensuring commercials, ledgers, liquidity, tax, reporting and controls remain operating
responsibilities: Provide Finance input to the deal memo, pricing, costing, revenue, premium-to-NAV, goodwill, amortisation, stranded-cost, synergy and group P&L assumptions.
Define completion accounts, purchase price adjustments, funds flow, accounting treatment, tax exposures, funding, liquidity, settlement and FX requirements.
Own the finance side of Group Interchange and TSA service management, including service charging, recharges, buy-backs, cost recovery, invoicing and dispute controls
Define which finance-related services, reporting routines, payments, controls and processes must start, stop or continue across Absa, the acquired business, the seller or the buyer.
Align acquired or disposed business finance policies, ledgers, reporting standards, close calendars, account structures and control requirements to the agreed transaction model.
Coordinate Group Tax advice centrally while ensuring local tax, statutory reporting and regulatory finance requirements are captured through in-country teams.
Validate historic financial data, local ledgers, trial balances, management information, reconciliation approach and local reporting constraints with Regional Spokes.
Test finance data, ledgers, processes, payments, reports, P&L impacts, month-end close and reconciliation controls before LD1.
Confirm finance readiness for signing, completion, cutover, first close, hypercare and BAU handover.
boundaryItems: Legal & CorpDev owns transaction-document drafting and commercial negotiation route; Finance & Tax supplies costing, revenue, scenario planning, tax, accounting, completion mechanics, Group Interchange and TSA charging inputs.
Central Hub owns integrated programme governance and TSA dependency tracking; Finance & Tax owns financial design, recharge, buy-back, P&L and control evidence for Group Interchange and TSA services.

Procurement owns supplier contracting and third-party continuity; Finance & Tax owns spend baselining, payment-route design, cost allocation, stranded-cost analysis and supplier-related financial controls.
Technology and Data Migration own system build and data movement; Finance & Tax owns ledger mapping, finance data validation, accounting rules, reporting outputs and reconciliation requirements.

Regional Spokes own local finance evidence, local statutory reporting, close-calendar constraints and local regulatory finance nuance, with Group Finance and Group Tax retaining group-level standards and technical positions.
finance-tax.centralHubRelationship: Relationship with Central Hub: the SA Functional Spoke owns finance and tax execution decisions and evidence while the Central Hub sets programme standards, coordinates dependencies, tracks TSA and Group Interchange critical path items, and escalates transaction-wide issues.
regionalRelationship: Regional Spokes should own local execution as a minimum, with ownership scaling based on maturity, including local ledger evidence, statutory reporting inputs, local tax data, close-calendar constraints, reconciliations and first-close support where they have capacity and delegated authority.

Function Authority retains group accounting and tax positions, Group Interchange and TSA charging standards, completion accounts, group reporting, central review and execution ownership where regional maturity, capability or capacity is insufficient.

As regional maturity increases, local ownership should expand from evidence provision into ledger mapping, local reporting readiness, local tax execution and first-close activity, with Function Authority retaining group standards, specialist challenge and reserved approvals.
finance-tax.externalDependencies: External or counterparty dependencies are managed through the Central Hub governance route where timing, financial data, TSA charging, completion accounts, tax, approvals or joint readiness affect signing, completion or LD1.

milestoneIntro: The key milestones below are organised as a baseline set, with additional milestones required for more complex deal archetypes split out below as required.

As deal archetypes scale from balance sheet to partial business to full business, each baseline activity should be assessed against the complexity factors laid out in the deal archetypes documentation, and assessed for whether its size or scope increases as a result of deal specifics.
serviceCatalogue: Deal economics, pricing and scenario support
Completion mechanics, funds flow and treasury readiness
Group Interchange, TSA charging and recharge / buy-back management
Finance policy, ledger mapping and reporting readiness
Tax, liquidity, FX and regulatory finance coordination
Close, reconciliation, cutover and hypercare control

activitySets.heading: Balance Sheet Acquisition - baseline activities

milestones.name: Finance input to deal economics provided (3 weeks)
activities: Build costing, revenue, stranded-cost and synergy assumptions for in-scope transfer
Document what premium or discount to NAV represents, including goodwill, technology, client, funding or other value drivers
Model amortisation, impairment, capital, liquidity and group P&L impacts

milestones.name: Completion mechanism and funds flow designed (4 weeks)
activities: Define purchase price adjustment approach, completion accounts, effective transfer date, settlement route, bank account requirements and payment cut-offs
Confirm liquidity, FX, funding, capital, bad-debt and late-payment exposures
Coordinate with Legal & CorpDev so finance mechanics, tax protections, completion evidence and post-completion obligations are in documents

milestones.name: Financial data and ledger baseline validated (4 weeks)
activities: Request historic financials, trial balances, portfolio balances, P&L run-rate, account structures and supporting evidence
Map in-country ledgers into Absa group account structures and hierarchies
Identify remediation required through system migration, configuration, manual posting or workaround

milestones.name: Tax and regulatory finance position assessed (6 weeks)
activities: Confirm Group Tax view, local tax obligations, transfer pricing etc implications.
Capture local reporting, regulatory finance and capital-reporting requirements through Regional Spoke
Validate whether local regulatory constraints affect shared-service, funding, liquidity or synergy assumptions

milestones.name: LD1 finance readiness tested (4 weeks)
activities: Test ledger postings, reporting outputs, management information, reconciliation controls, funds flow and exception handling alongside regional spoke
Rehearse completion entries, payment instructions, account confirmations, close timetable and escalation route
Confirm manual workarounds for unresolved ledger, reporting or payments

milestones.name: Hypercare and BAU managed (4 weeks)
activities: Monitor reconciliations, reporting cycle, tax, liquidity, FX, TSA charges and open completion items
Hand over finance controls, reporting routines, issue logs and residual actions to BAU Finance
Critical dependency: incomplete historic financials, unmapped ledgers or unresolved local reporting constraints can delay completion, first close or group reporting.

activitySets.heading: Partial Business Acquisition - additional activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of

milestones.name: Financial impact of employee or tech transfer assessed (4 weeks)
activities: Identify shared services required to transfer employees or technology, and understand finance implications on TSAs or deal valuation
Document and remediate tax implications of employee transfer
Work with HR to understand impact of employee packages on finances, including bonus payments
Work with seller to understand total cost of ownership of transferring technology, and ensure it appears in forecasts

milestones.name: Group Interchange and TSA finance model established (5 weeks)
activities: Confirm which finance-related services must start, stop or continue between Absa, the seller and the acquired business
Design or re-use service charge, recharge, buy-back, VAT, tax, invoicing, MI, dispute and exit mechanics
Provide finance inputs to TSA schedules, service descriptions, charging clauses, exit milestones and completion conditions

milestones.name: Local finance transition plan mobilised (4 weeks)
activities: Map local month-end close timings, reporting standards, statutory obligations and finance ways of working
Support in-country testing of finance data, local ledgers, reporting outputs and process hand-offs
Track local tax, reporting and regulatory finance obligations centrally while keeping execution with the accountable local teams

activitySets.heading: Full Business Acquisition A (integrated) - further additional activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of

milestones.name: Finance integration blueprint agreed (5 weeks)
activities: Map target finance policies, controls, reporting standards, close calendar and account structures to Absa Group Finance, Group Tax and Treasury requirements
Align acquired ledgers to Absa group account structures, cost centres, product hierarchies and management reporting.
Decide whether each finance gap is remediated through migration, configuration, manual posting, reporting adjustment or control

milestones.name: Acquisition accounting and value tracking completed (6 weeks)
activities: Finalise purchase accounting, goodwill, premium-to-NAV allocation, amortisation, impairment and group P&L treatment.
Set synergy, stranded-cost, one-off cost and integration-cost tracking against the business case
Agree forecast, budget, capital, liquidity and management reporting changes for the integrated business

milestones.name: Integrated close and control model tested (4 weeks)
activities: Test month-end close, reconciliations, reporting outputs, finance interfaces, account ownership and control attestations.
Validate local teams can adopt Absa reporting timings and finance processes, Change Management support where ways of working change
Confirm legacy finance processes are retired, migrated or controlled through approved temporary workarounds

milestones.name: Post-LD1 finance integration managed (4 weeks)
activities: Monitor group reporting, first integrated close, tax filings, TSA exit, synergy delivery, cost removal and residual defects
Transfer ongoing finance ownership to BAU Finance, Group Tax, Treasury and local finance teams

activitySets.heading: Full Business Acquisition B (standalone) - new activity set
activitySets.lead: Standalone:

milestones.name: Standalone finance control model defined (5 weeks)
activities: Confirm the acquired business can operate under Absa ownership with its own ledgers, finance governance, reporting, tax, liquidity, controls
Define Absa oversight forums, reporting packs, financial-control attestations, escalation routes and retained local decision rights
Confirm local finance capability, capacity and cultural ways of working that may affect first close or ongoing reporting

milestones.name: Deal economics and standalone value case maintained (3 weeks)
activities: Maintain pricing, costing, revenue, premium-to-NAV, goodwill, amortisation, stranded-cost and group P&L assumptions for the standalone state
Agree forecast, budget, capital, liquidity and management reporting treatment for Absa ownership

milestones.name: Completion, funding and tax model agreed (4 weeks)
activities: Design completion accounts, funds flow, account authority, settlement, liquidity, FX, capital, tax and payment evidence
Confirm Group Tax, local tax, statutory reporting, regulatory finance and transfer-pricing requirements.

milestones.name: Group Interchange and TSA services established (5 weeks)
activities: Define which Absa or seller services start, stop or continue, including finance operations, reporting, payment, tax and controls
Set service charges, recharges, buy-backs, invoice routes, evidence requirements, dispute controls and exit milestones

milestones.name: Ledger and reporting interface tested (6 weeks)
activities: Map local ledgers to Absa group reporting
Set feeds, manual journals, reporting templates and recon controls.

milestones.name: LD1 and first-close readiness confirmed (4 weeks)
activities: Rehearse payments, reporting submissions, finance data transfer, controls
Monitor first close, reporting quality, liquidity, tax filings, Group Interchange charges, TSA billing and unresolved finance exceptions through hypercare.

activitySets.heading: Balance Sheet Sale - baseline divestment activities

milestones.name: Sale economics and PnL assessed (3 weeks)
activities: Confirm sale perimeter, book value, NAV, premium or discount, exposure, residual revenue, direct costs, stranded costs
Model group PnL, capital, liquidity, tax, amortisation, impairment and reporting impacts
Track retained cost, synergy, TSA revenue, service charge and cost-removal assumptions against business case

milestones.name: Completion mechanism and funds flow designed (4 weeks)
activities: Define purchase price adjustment approach, completion accounts, effective transfer date, cash and debt treatment, settlement route, bank account requirements and payment cut-offs
Confirm liquidity, FX, tax leakage, bad-debt and late-payment exposures
Coordinate with Legal & CorpDev so finance mechanics, obligations, tax protections and completion evidence are reflected in transaction docs

milestones.name: Financial data and records prepared (4 weeks)
activities: Build balance list, supporting ledgers, historic financials, PnL run-rate, buyer data-room materials and recon evidence
Separate transferred records from retained Absa records, tax records, reporting evidence and audit requirements
Define data-sharing restrictions and clean-room arrangements with Compliance, Data Migration and Legal & CorpDev

milestones.name: Retained service and Group Interchange model assessed (5 weeks)
activities: Identify Absa services that must continue, stop or be charged to the buyer or disposed business through TSA or Group Interchange arrangements
Set recharge, buy-back, cost recovery, invoicing, tax, MI, dispute and exit mechanics

milestones.name: Tax and local reporting position assessed (6 weeks)
activities: Confirm Group Tax view, local tax filings, transfer pricing and retained tax obligation
Capture local reporting, regulatory finance and capital-reporting requirements through Regional Spoke

milestones.name: LD1 finance readiness tested (4 weeks)
activities: Test balance transfer, reporting removal, retained-business reporting, reconciliations, funds flow, buyer hand-off and exception handling
Rehearse completion entries, payment instructions, buyer finance hand-off, close timetable and escalation route

milestones.name: Hypercare and BAU close-out managed (4 weeks)
activities: Monitor obligations, queries, reconciliations, tax filings, TSA billing, stranded costs and completion items

activitySets.heading: Partial Business Sale - additional divestment activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Shared service and Group Interchange plan defined (5 weeks)
activities: Identify finance services Absa continues to provide, buyer services that need TSA support, services that must stop at completion
Set recharge, buy-back, service charge, tax, invoice, dispute and exit mechanics for partial perimeter
Provide finance inputs to TSA schedules, buyer hand-off packs and retained-service governance

milestones.name: Retained-business finance readiness protected (4 weeks)
activities: Test retained Absa reporting, cost-centre changes, ledger separation, payment routes, reconciliations and local close timetable
Track buyer finance dependencies, retained control actions, local tax reporting and stranded-cost reduction through governance

activitySets.heading: Full Business Sale A (buyer integrates) - further additional divestment activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of,

milestones.name: Buyer integration finance hand-off completed (4 weeks)
activities: Provide agreed financial data, ledger mapping, historical financials, completion accounts, service charge assumptions and reconciliation evidence to support integration
Coordinate buyer questions, completion evidence, TSA billing set-up and retained Absa reporting through Central Hub
Confirm buyer integration does not disrupt retained Absa continued business

milestones.name: Absa finance separation and value tracking completed (5 weeks)
activities: Remove disposed business from Absa reporting, forecasts, budgets, cost centres, management information
Track TSA billing, recharge, stranded-cost unwind, tax filings, retained liabilities and true-ups

activitySets.heading: Full Business Sale B (standalone) - complete divestment activity set

milestones.name: Standalone buyer finance operating model assessed (5 weeks)
activities: Confirm whether the disposed business can operate under buyer ownership with standalone ledgers, reporting, close calendar, bank accounts, tax, liquidity, controls and finance governance
Identify Absa support required for finance operations, reporting, payments, tax, reporting, controls and management information during transition
Define buyer finance governance, reporting packs, escalation routes, control attestations and local decision rights

milestones.name: Separation mechanics and completion model agreed (4 weeks)
activities: Create standalone opening balance sheet, completion accounts, funds flow, account authority, settlement, liquidity, FX, capital and tax evidence
Separate Absa reporting structures, retained records, obligations, audit, tax files from disposed
Confirm buyer readiness for first close, local reporting, tax filings and finance controls

milestones.name: Group Interchange and TSA finance services defined (5 weeks)
activities: Set service delivery agreements, service scope, prices, recharge and buy-back mechanics, VAT, tax, invoicing, MI, dispute controls and exit milestones
Confirm which Absa services continue, stop or transfer, and how Finance monitors service consumption and cost recovery

milestones.name: Buyer readiness and retained Absa controls tested (4 weeks)
activities: Test reporting separation, payment routes, bank access, ledger hand-off, control evidence, service charge process and close timetable.
Rehearse completion entries, buyer hand-off, TSA finance calls, reporting submissions, fallback and escalation route.

milestones.name: Standalone completion and hypercare managed
activities: Monitor first close, reporting quality, liquidity, tax filings, Group Interchange charges, TSA billing, retained Absa obligations and stranded-cost unwind

Significant number of currencies that are new to the bank
Complex or opaque true-up / completion process
Significant level of interchange or TSA charges involved

hr.name: Human Capital

necessityRows.archetype: Balance Sheet Acquisition
necessityRows.rationale: Balance sheet archetypes, by definition, do not include people transfer

necessityRows.archetype: Partial Business Acquisition
necessityRows.rationale: Conditional where partial archetypes create transferring and retained employee populations, consultation obligations, payroll and benefits decisions, and onboarding needs

necessityRows.archetype: Full Business Acquisition A (Buyer integrates the business)
necessityRows.rationale: Required to integrate people, organisation design, reward, benefits, payroll, systems, training, culture and retention into Absa.

necessityRows.archetype: Full Business Acquisition B (Buyer runs the business standalone)
necessityRows.rationale: Required to stand up or retain a complete Human Capital operating model, payroll, benefits, policies, local people capability and employee governance.

necessityRows.archetype: Balance Sheet Sale
necessityRows.rationale: Balance sheet archetypes, by definition, do not include people transfer

necessityRows.archetype: Partial Business Sale
necessityRows.rationale: Conditional where partial archetypes create transferring and retained employee populations, consultation obligations, payroll and benefits decisions, and onboarding needs

necessityRows.archetype: Full Business Sale A (Buyer integrates the business)
necessityRows.rationale: Required to support buyer-led people integration while managing Absa seller obligations, consultation, data transfer and residual employee risk.

necessityRows.archetype: Full Business Sale B (Buyer runs the business as standalone)
necessityRows.rationale: Required to execute full employee transfer or separation, buyer standalone people readiness, Absa exits and post-completion people obligations.

hr.keyRole: Human Capital owns employee-transfer execution and people readiness, including terms, consultation, onboarding, payroll, benefits, reward, employee data, retention and people transition into BAU.
responsibilities: Confirm employee perimeter, roles, grades, contracts, terms, benefits, reward, payroll, pensions, unions, mobility, wellness and consultation obligations.
Bring employee legal into due diligence so Human Capital can plan transfer mechanics, consultation timing, S197 implications, CP dependencies and negotiation points early.
Define people-transfer approach, organisational design, leadership appointments, retention interventions, reward / REM decisions and onboarding requirements.
Plan and execute employee consultation, employee engagement, offer or transfer processes, union engagement and employee-data controls with Legal and Compliance.
Stand up or transition payroll, pension, benefits, HR systems, manager readiness, training and day-one access for transferring employees.
Coordinate strategic employee communications with Communications and Change
Track employee acceptance, resignations, key-person risk, wellbeing, cultural adaptation and post-LD1 people issues.
boundaryItems: Legal owns legal interpretation of employment-transfer obligations, commercial provisions and CPs that affect people activity.
Change Management owns adoption of new ways of working; Human Capital provides people expertise, employee readiness inputs and change impact detail.
Communications / Marketing owns channels, tone and approval flow; Human Capital owns employee content and consultations
Technology owns HR system access, employee data tooling and identity integration; Human Capital owns employee data requirements and people readiness
hr.centralHubRelationship: Relationship with Central Hub: Human Capital owns people-transfer and HR readiness decisions and evidence while the Central Hub coordinates dependencies, decision timing, issue escalation and integration of people milestones into the wider programme plan.
regionalRelationship: Regional Spokes should own local execution as a minimum, with ownership scaling based on maturity, including employee data, local consultation steps, unions, payroll and benefits inputs, employee engagement, wellbeing actions and local HR readiness where they have capacity and delegated authority.

Function Authority retains people-transfer standards, consultation integrity, reward and REM decisions, central workforce planning, specialist HR support and execution ownership where regional maturity, capability or capacity is insufficient.

As regional maturity increases, local ownership should expand from evidence and local nuance into consultation support, people-readiness execution and hypercare activity, with Function Authority retaining standards, specialist challenge and reserved approvals.

spokeAuthority: Defines Human Capital scope, people-transfer route, consultation plan, employee-data needs and people readiness evidence.
mandateRows.hubRole: Tracks people milestones, dependencies and unresolved people risks in the integrated plan.
mandateRows.governance: Human Capital, Legal, Compliance, business owner, Change, Communications and relevant country governance.
mandateRows.escalation: Employee population, transfer route, consultation trigger, union exposure or S197 impact is unclear.

mandateRows.area: Terms, reward, benefits, payroll and pensions
spokeAuthority: Approves reward / REM approach, benefits treatment, payroll stand-up, pension transition planning and employee offer inputs.
mandateRows.hubRole: Coordinates cross-workstream timing and escalation where people items affect LD1 or completion.
mandateRows.governance: Human Capital, Employment Legal, Finance & Tax, pension trustees/regulators where applicable.
mandateRows.escalation: Benefits are contractual or policy-based and need negotiation, pension approval delays activity, or payroll readiness is at risk.

spokeAuthority: Owns employee content, consultation integrity and people-readiness messaging inputs.
mandateRows.hubRole: Coordinates message timing with programme milestones and approval gates.
mandateRows.governance: Communications, Change Management, Legal, Human Capital and buyer/seller leadership.
mandateRows.escalation: Ownership between current employer, new employer, HR, Change and Communications is unclear.

spokeAuthority: Confirms onboarding, HR systems, access, L&D, manager readiness and employee sign-off requirements.
mandateRows.hubRole: Tracks readiness evidence and critical-path dependencies across Technology, Finance and Operations.
mandateRows.governance: Technology, Finance & Tax, Learning, Operations, business owners and LD1 readiness governance.
mandateRows.escalation: Employee data transfer, system onboarding, payroll setup or training completion is not evidenced.

mandateRows.governance: Human Capital, business leadership, Change, Risk and post-LD1 BAU governance.

capabilityRows.category: Specific Project Manager required?
capabilityRows.content: Yes - Needed to run weekly agendas, specialist inputs, buyer check-ins, handover documentation, wellness and retention through a long transaction

milestoneIntro: The key milestones below are organised as a baseline set, with additional milestones required for more complex deal archetypes split out below as required.

As deal archetypes scale from balance sheet to partial business to full business, each baseline activity should be assessed against the complexity factors laid out in the deal archetype documentation.
Service catalogue:
serviceCatalogue: Employee perimeter and data assessment
Employment legal DD support
Consultation planning and execution
Organisational design and Reward / REM, benefits, payroll and pension transition
Resource management - project and BAU continuity planning
Cultural alignment and harmonisation
Employee communications inputs (alongside Comms & Change)
Training and employee readiness coordination
Onboarding, training, payroll, HR systems and access readiness
Retention, wellness and post-LD1 people monitoring

activitySets.heading: Balance Sheet Acquisition - baseline activities
activitySets.lead: Not required

activitySets.heading: Partial Business Acquisition - additional activities

milestones.name: Human Capital mobilisation and employee scope confirmed (3 weeks)
activities: Identify employees, contractors, managers, specialist roles, key people and country populations affected by the deal.
Confirm whether unions, S197, consultation, payroll, benefits, pension or employee-data activities are triggered.
Assign dedicated Human Capital workstream lead and PM support where deal scale requires it.

milestones.name: Employment legal due diligence completed (5 weeks)
activities: Bring employee legal into DD to identify transfer obligations, CP dependencies, employee terms and negotiation points.
Review contracts, policies, reward / REM, benefits, discounted banking products, pension arrangements and employee liabilities.
Identify whether employees are union members and whether local consultation or regulator involvement is required.

milestones.name: Consultation and employee communications plan agreed and executed (6 weeks)
activities: Define consultation steps, employee engagement route, leadership briefings and approval timing.
Agree with Change and Communications whether the current employer or new employer leads each communication.
Prepare strategic employee communications for late-stage uncertainty, wellness, retention and cutover emotion.
Execute and track consultations, assessing employee reactions and adapting where required
Hold individual one-to-one meetings where required to explain contract, level, and benefits
Work with seller to collate employee questions, and set up FAQs, as well as regular townhalls structured around a question theme

milestones.name: Cultural alignment analysis and remediation plan complete (4 weeks)
activities: Assess key cultural differences between Absa and seller, and impact on operating model
Define remediation activities such as training, townhalls, one-to-one meetings, and social sessions
Sequence, plan, and execute remediation activities, and conduct pulse surveys to track impact

milestones.name: Payroll, benefits, pension and employee-data readiness planned (8 weeks)
activities: Define payroll stand-up or transition requirements, banking policy benefits, contractual benefits and reward decisions.
Confirm pension fund approval requirements and earliest permissible employee communication or process start date.
Agree employee data transfer requirements with Technology, including completeness, accuracy, privacy and system onboarding needs.

milestones.name: Organisational design complete (4 weeks)
activities: Work with business and functional areas to discuss leveling and role cards for incoming employees
Map these roles into existing Absa structures and define reporting lines
Socialise these with both incoming employees and managers, and iterate where significant issues arise
Define the approach to transferring portfolios of client facing employees: kept as-is, adapted, or merged into Absa portfolios

milestones.name: Onboarding, training and people readiness evidenced (6 weeks)
activities: Plan system onboarding, manager readiness, L&D compliance, functional training and technical training.
Track employee sign-offs, acceptance, resignations, key-person risks and readiness evidence.
Confirm Human Capital inputs to LD1 readiness and post-LD1 people monitoring

milestones.name: Employee data, systems and finance dependencies managed (6 weeks)
activities: Coordinate employee data extraction, masking or unmasked data submission with Legal, Compliance and Technology.
Align payroll and employee-cost treatment with Finance & Tax, including any Completion Statement or booking impacts.
Escalate system onboarding or employee data issues before they affect training or day-one access.

milestones.name: Post-LD1 people stability monitored (4 weeks)
activities: Monitor attrition, employee sentiment, capability gaps, payroll errors, benefits issues and onboarding defects.
Resolve people risks through hypercare with HR, Change, Communications, Technology and Finance.
Transfer residual people actions to BAU HR owners after stabilisation.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Acquisition A (integrated) - further additional activities

milestones.name: Integrated organisation and leadership model approved (5 weeks)
activities: Design the integrated organisation, leadership appointments, role mapping, spans, grades and reporting lines.
Agree retention and talent interventions for critical roles and key-person dependencies.
Confirm cultural integration and team adaptation activities with Change Management.

milestones.name: Terms, reward, benefits and payroll migration executed (8 weeks)
activities: Map employees onto Absa terms, reward, payroll, benefits, pension and HR policy arrangements.
Negotiate or remediate contractual and policy benefits, including banking benefits where relevant.
Complete payroll, HR system, access and employee record migration before LD1.

activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

activitySets.heading: Full Business Acquisition B (standalone) - new activity set

milestones.name: Standalone Human Capital operating model designed (5 weeks)
activities: Define standalone HR organisation, policies, committees, vendor support, employee relations and payroll operating model.
Confirm local HR capability, outsourced support, employment legal support and regulatory-relations expertise required before LD1.
Agree how central standards will apply to standalone country or business HR execution.

milestones.name: Payroll, pension and benefits infrastructure stood up (8 weeks)
activities: Build or transition payroll, pension, benefits, HRIS, employee records, access, reporting and controls.
Obtain pension fund or regulatory approvals needed before employee transition processes can begin.
Complete data migration and reconciliation for employee records and payroll-ready information.

milestones.name: Standalone people policies and capability embedded (6 weeks)
activities: Stand up policies, handbooks, employee relations, wellness, talent, reward, learning and onboarding processes.
Train local HR, managers and employees on the standalone ways of working.
Confirm employee communications, consultation evidence and BAU HR governance are operational.

milestones.name: People readiness and BAU handover completed (4 weeks)
activities: Evidence employee onboarding, manager readiness, payroll readiness, benefits readiness and support model readiness.
Monitor post-LD1 people issues through a dedicated hypercare cadence.
Close Human Capital programme actions only when BAU HR owners have accepted residual obligations.

activitySets.heading: Balance Sheet Sale - baseline divestment activities
activitySets.lead: Not required

activitySets.heading: Partial Business Sale - additional divestment activities

milestones.name: Retained and transferring workforce split executed (8 weeks)
activities: Map employees to buyer, retained Absa, TSA support, redeployment or exit categories.
Confirm management structures, reporting lines and retained capability for Absa after separation.
Manage union, consultation and employee relations implications of the partial sale.

milestones.name: Seller and buyer responsibilities agreed (5 weeks)
activities: Confirm whether buyer leads change for transferring employees and what seller-side change remains with Absa.
Agree employee communications ownership between current employer, new employer, HR, Change and Communications.
Track buyer onboarding and Absa retained team readiness through joint governance.

milestones.name: Payroll, benefits and pension split managed (8 weeks)
activities: Separate payroll, benefits, pension, reward and employee data between transferring and retained populations.
Resolve contractual and policy benefits that need buyer negotiation or Absa residual treatment.
Confirm regulatory or pension fund approvals before dependent activities begin.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Sale A (buyer integrates) - further additional divestment activities

milestones.name: Buyer-led people integration supported (6 weeks)
activities: Provide employee data, consultation evidence and transition inputs needed for buyer integration where permitted.
Track buyer onboarding, payroll, systems, training and employee support readiness.
Escalate buyer readiness gaps that could create Absa residual employee risk.

milestones.name: Absa seller-side change and retained obligations managed (4 weeks)
activities: Run seller-side change for retained Absa teams, TSA support teams and leaders affected by the divestment.
Manage morale, wellness, retention and knowledge-transfer risk around cutover.
Close retained Absa HR actions after buyer integration stabilises.

milestones.name: Post-transfer people support transitioned (4 weeks)
activities: Track employee queries, payroll issues, benefits issues, employee relations matters and residual commitments after LD1.
Transfer open items to buyer, Absa BAU or post-completion obligation owners.
Archive Human Capital evidence for legal, audit and regulatory purposes.

activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

activitySets.heading: Full Business Sale B (standalone) - complete divestment activity set

milestones.name: Complete people separation route executed (8 weeks)
activities: Transfer or exit the full employee population, including managers, HR support, payroll, benefits, pensions and employee records.
Confirm buyer standalone HR model can operate without Absa programme support.
Resolve union, consultation, regulatory and pension dependencies before completion or LD1.

milestones.name: Buyer standalone Human Capital handover completed (4 weeks)
activities: Transfer permitted employee documentation, onboarding evidence, policies, issue logs and open people commitments to the buyer.
Support buyer set-up of payroll, benefits, HR systems, learning, wellness and employee relations where agreed.
Confirm local country execution and outsourced specialist support are no longer dependent on Absa.

milestones.name: Absa people exit and wind-down completed (8 weeks)
activities: Close Absa employee communications, redeployment, retained-team change and TSA staffing obligations.
Monitor claims, disputes, payroll corrections, benefit true-ups and post-completion commitments.
Close the Human Capital workstream when all residual people obligations have named BAU or buyer owners.

Multi-jurisdictional employee transfer
Complex reward packages
Very different organisational cultures

independent-assurance.name: Independent Assurance / External Audit

necessityRows.archetype: Balance Sheet Acquisition
necessityRows.rationale: Not typically required on smaller acquisitions with limited wider impact on the Absa business, unless specified by the regulator

necessityRows.archetype: Partial Business Acquisition
necessityRows.rationale: Required because independent review of governance, controls, migration, and readiness is critical to a successful go-live across these archetypes

necessityRows.archetype: Full Business Acquisition A (Buyer integrates the business)
necessityRows.rationale: Required because independent review of governance, controls, migration, and readiness is critical to a successful go-live across these archetypes

necessityRows.archetype: Full Business Acquisition B (Buyer runs the business standalone)
necessityRows.rationale: Optional as limited integration work in this archetype does not necessitate standalone workstream, however significant work aligning governance models may benefit from independent oversight

necessityRows.archetype: Balance Sheet Sale
necessityRows.rationale: Not typically required on smaller disposals with limited wider impact on Absa, unless specified by a regulator

necessityRows.archetype: Partial Business Sale
necessityRows.rationale: Optional as the majority of integration work will sit with the buyer, so independent review is not as critical on the Absa side

necessityRows.archetype: Full Business Sale A (Buyer integrates the business)
necessityRows.rationale: Required because independent review of governance, controls, migration, and readiness is critical to a successful go-live across these archetypes

necessityRows.archetype: Full Business Sale B (Buyer runs the business as standalone)
necessityRows.rationale: Optional as limited integration work in this archetype does not necessitate standalone workstream, however significant work aligning governance models may benefit from independent oversight

independent-assurance.keyRole: External independent assurers provide objective assurance over whether programme governance, controls, migration, testing, cutover and readiness evidence are sufficient to support transaction decisions. They assess and report; they do not own delivery remediation or programme decision-making.
responsibilities: Perform independent assessment of programme governance, decision quality, delivery controls, issue escalation and readiness evidence.
Assess whether workstream plans, milestones, risks, dependencies, decisions and evidence are sufficient to support signing, completion, LD1 and post-LD1 decisions.
Review control design and operating-readiness evidence across business, operations, technology, data, risk, compliance, finance, procurement and people activity.
Assess migration design, source-to-target mapping, ETL controls, data completeness, data accuracy, reconciliations, exceptions and fallback arrangements.
Assess test strategy, SIT, E2E testing, mock runs, dress rehearsals, defect triage, retesting, accepted workarounds and test-exit evidence.
Assess cutover readiness, command-centre arrangements, contingency plans, hypercare entry criteria and BAU handover evidence.
Assess specific high-risk readiness areas such as digital delivery, cards production and fulfilment, customer communications, regulatory evidence and TSA controls where applicable.
Raise independent findings, recommendations, assurance opinions and residual concerns to the agreed programme governance forums.
Validate remediation closure evidence for agreed findings without taking ownership of delivery remediation.
Maintain an evidence trail that can support programme governance, Internal Audit, regulator-facing reviews and post-completion audit requirements.
boundaryItems: Delivery workstreams own execution, remediation and evidence production; external independent assurers assess the adequacy of that evidence and the credibility of readiness conclusions.
The Central Hub owns programme governance, integrated planning, RAID tracking and evidence coordination; external independent assurers assess whether those controls are operating effectively.
Risk owns the 2LOD risk judgement and risk appetite route; external independent assurers provide independent evidence-based assurance over risk-related programme controls and readiness evidence.
Internal Audit provides 3LOD assurance where commissioned; external independent assurers provide the independent assurance procedures and opinions defined in their engagement scope.
independent-assurance.centralHubRelationship: Relationship with Central Hub: the Central Hub provides the integrated plan, governance materials, evidence owners, issue logs and access to workstreams; external independent assurers assess whether the programme evidence supports the required decisions and report findings through the agreed governance route.
regionalRelationship: Regional Spokes should own local execution as a minimum, with ownership scaling based on maturity, including evidence collation, control-owner walkthroughs, local context, access facilitation and remediation evidence where they have capacity and delegated authority.

Function Authority retains assurance scope, testing approach, independent assessment, findings, opinions and central escalation where regional maturity, evidence quality, capability or capacity is insufficient.

As regional maturity increases, local teams should provide stronger self-evidencing and direct assurance responses, while Function Authority retains objective assessment, specialist challenge and independent reporting.
independent-assurance.externalDependencies: External or counterparty dependencies are managed through the Central Hub governance route where buyer, seller, country, regulator or third-party evidence is required for assurance procedures.

spokeAuthority: Assess whether governance forums, packs, decisions, RAID management, dependency tracking and issue escalation are effective and evidence-based.
mandateRows.hubRole: Provides governance materials, decision logs, RAID logs, plan data and access to programme forums.
mandateRows.governance: Programme SteerCo, accountable executive, Central Hub, workstream leads and Internal Audit where relevant.
mandateRows.escalation: Decisions are made without evidence, SteerCos are cancelled or ineffective, or material issues are not escalated in time.

spokeAuthority: Assess whether control design, control ownership, operating-readiness evidence, risk acceptances and remediation closure support the readiness conclusion.
mandateRows.hubRole: Coordinates evidence owners and tracks assurance findings through programme governance.
mandateRows.governance: Risk, Compliance, Operations, Technology, Finance, Procurement, HR and relevant business owners.
mandateRows.escalation: Control evidence is incomplete, remediation is not evidenced, or ownership remains unclear at go/no-go.

spokeAuthority: Assess migration design, mapping, ETL controls, data completeness, accuracy, reconciliation, exceptions and fallback evidence.
mandateRows.hubRole: Coordinates data evidence, defect ownership and dependency escalation.
mandateRows.governance: Data Migration, Technology, Finance, Risk, Compliance and Data Governance.
mandateRows.escalation: No accountable owner can evidence comfort with data completeness or accuracy, or migration exceptions threaten LD1.

mandateRows.area: Testing, mock runs and dress rehearsals
spokeAuthority: Assess test strategy, scope coverage, SIT, E2E journeys, mock runs, dress rehearsals, defect triage, retesting and success criteria.
mandateRows.hubRole: Coordinates test evidence and routes readiness implications into go/no-go governance.
mandateRows.governance: E2E Testing, Technology, Operations, Data Migration, Risk and Client Readiness.
mandateRows.escalation: Success criteria are undefined, critical journeys are untested, defects lack accepted workarounds, or retest evidence is weak.

spokeAuthority: Assess cutover runbooks, command-centre model, fallback, go/no-go pack, hypercare entry and BAU handover evidence.
mandateRows.hubRole: Provides readiness pack, issue status, decisions and cross-workstream dependencies.
mandateRows.governance: Client Readiness, accountable executive, workstream leads, Risk, Compliance and Internal Audit where relevant.
mandateRows.escalation: Readiness recommendation is unsupported, fallback is not viable, or residual findings are not assigned to owners.

capabilityRows.category: Specific Project Manager required?
capabilityRows.content: NA - to be defined and stood up by the external team

capabilityRows.category: Baseline capabilities
capabilityRows.content: Governance, decision-making, RAID controls, issue escalation, CP evidence and remediation closure assessment; large scale programme management; experience delivering M&A deals;

capabilityRows.category: Incremental capabilities by deal archetype / complexity
capabilityRows.content: Deep understanding of source-to-target mapping, ETL controls, data completeness, accuracy, reconciliations, exceptions and migration readiness; ability to build parallel migration solutions; executive migration readiness reporting

capabilityRows.category: Specialist capabilities triggered by deal characteristics
capabilityRows.content: Regulatory relations where engaged by regulator; technology, digital, cards, TSA, operational, financial, risk, compliance, people risk assessment ability

milestoneIntro: The key milestones below describe the assessment activity expected from external independent assurers, with additional assurance procedures required for more complex deal archetypes split out below as required.
As deal archetypes scale from balance sheet to partial business to full business, assurance procedures should be assessed against the complexity factors laid out in the deal archetype documentation.
serviceCatalogue: Programme governance and decision-quality assessment
Control design and readiness evidence assessment
Migration design, ETL and reconciliation assurance
Data completeness and accuracy assurance
Testing, mock run and dress rehearsal assurance
Cutover, contingency and LD1 readiness assessment
Finding, recommendation and remediation closure validation
Independent readiness opinion and evidence archive

activitySets.heading: Balance Sheet Acquisition - baseline activities

milestones.name: Assurance scope and evidence request confirmed (2 weeks)
activities: Confirm the assurance procedures, workstreams, milestones, evidence standards, sample approach and reporting dates in the agreed engagement scope.
Request programme governance packs, integrated plans, RAID logs, workstream plans, testing evidence, migration evidence and readiness criteria.
Document any limitation on assurance coverage caused by missing evidence, confidentiality constraints or timing restrictions.

milestones.name: Programme governance and control assessment completed (4 weeks)
activities: Assess whether programme governance is operating with clear decisions, owners, due dates, issue escalation and dependency control.
Review control design and readiness evidence for business, operations, technology, data, risk, compliance, finance and supplier impacts.
Validate that findings and remediation actions are owned by delivery teams and tracked through governance.

milestones.name: Testing and rehearsal assurance completed (4 weeks)
activities: Assess test strategy, SIT, E2E scope, mock runs, dress rehearsals, defect severity, retesting and accepted workarounds.
Validate whether success criteria were defined before test execution and whether outcomes were assessed against them.
Review evidence for high-risk journeys such as digital channels, cards, customer servicing or operational hand-offs where in scope.

milestones.name: Independent readiness opinion issued (2 weeks)
activities: Provide assurance findings, residual concerns and independent readiness view for completion, LD1 go/no-go and hypercare entry.
Validate remediation closure evidence for material findings without taking ownership of delivery remediation.
Archive assurance evidence, findings, management responses and closure decisions for audit and regulator use.

activitySets.heading: Partial Business Acquisition - additional activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Partial perimeter and retained dependency assurance completed (4 weeks)
activities: Assess whether transferring, retained, shared and excluded processes are clearly defined and evidenced.
Review TSA controls, retained Absa dependencies, local control ownership and buyer or seller hand-offs.
Raise findings where boundary ownership or evidence quality is unclear.

milestones.name: Local and shared-service evidence assessed (4 weeks)
activities: Sample country evidence, local walkthroughs, local control operation and retained-service evidence where relevant.
Assess whether local evidence supports central readiness conclusions and regulatory commitments.
Document gaps where country, central or counterparty evidence is inconsistent.

milestones.name: Migration and data assurance completed (4 weeks)
activities: Assess source-to-target mapping, ETL controls, migration runbooks, reconciliation thresholds, exception handling and audit trail.
Review evidence for data completeness, data accuracy, control totals, rejected records and downstream usability.
Raise findings where migration evidence cannot support go/no-go or regulator-facing conclusions.

milestones.name: Partial acquisition readiness opinion issued (2 weeks)
activities: Report assurance findings across migration, controls, testing, shared services and retained dependencies.
Validate closure evidence for priority findings before LD1 or agreed governance gates.
Confirm residual findings have accountable Absa, seller or buyer owners.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Acquisition A (integrated) - further additional activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Integrated governance and control assurance completed (4 weeks)
activities: Assess whether integrated workstream governance, decision quality, issue escalation and control ownership support the go-live decision.
Review integrated controls across operations, technology, data, risk, compliance, finance, procurement and HR.
Validate that readiness evidence is consistent across workstream sign-offs and assurance findings.

milestones.name: Integrated migration, testing and operational assurance completed (4 weeks)
activities: Assess data migration, reconciliation, E2E journeys, mock runs, dress rehearsals and operational readiness evidence for the integrated business.
Review digital, cards, customer, colleague and service-transition evidence where those journeys affect LD1.
Raise findings where defects, workarounds or residual risks are not supported by evidence.

milestones.name: Integrated LD1 assurance view issued (2 weeks)
activities: Provide an independent view of whether the integrated business is ready for LD1 and hypercare entry.
Identify conditions, residual findings and evidence gaps that should be visible in go/no-go governance.
Validate closure or owner assignment for findings that remain open after LD1.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Acquisition B (standalone) - new activity set

milestones.name: Standalone assurance approach executed (4 weeks)
activities: Assess standalone governance, committees, policies, controls, workstream ownership, local operations and evidence standards.
Review whether the standalone business can operate required processes without programme or seller support from LD1.
Document evidence gaps affecting board, exco, regulator or LD1 decisions.

milestones.name: Standalone systems, data and operating controls assessed (4 weeks)
activities: Assess standalone technology, data, reporting, access, supplier, HR, finance, risk and compliance controls.
Review migration and testing evidence across all data domains and operating processes required for standalone launch.
Validate contingency, command-centre and hypercare arrangements for standalone operation.

milestones.name: Regulator-facing and LD1 assurance opinion issued (2 weeks)
activities: Provide independent findings and readiness view for regulator-facing evidence, completion and LD1 go/no-go.
Validate management responses and remediation closure for material findings.
Archive assurance workpapers, conclusions and evidence for future audit or regulatory review.

activitySets.heading: Balance Sheet Sale - baseline divestment activities

milestones.name: Sale perimeter and retained Absa evidence assessed (4 weeks)
activities: Assess transferred data, retained data, retained controls, completion-condition evidence and buyer hand-off controls.
Review whether Absa can evidence accurate and complete data provision to the buyer.
Assess whether retained Absa obligations and risks have named owners and monitoring arrangements.

milestones.name: Buyer hand-off and separation testing assessed (4 weeks)
activities: Review buyer-facing data cuts, joint testing, transfer controls, defect handling and separation rehearsals.
Assess Absa-side access removal, retained service continuity and control operation after transfer.
Raise findings where buyer dependencies create unresolved Absa readiness or residual-risk issues.

milestones.name: Sale readiness assurance opinion issued (2 weeks)
activities: Provide independent findings for completion, LD1, TSA entry and post-LD1 support decisions.
Validate closure evidence for material findings before governance decisions.
Archive evidence for post-completion review, audit and dispute support.

activitySets.heading: Partial Business Sale - additional divestment activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Carve-out and shared-service assurance completed (4 weeks)
activities: Assess shared services, TSA controls, retained Absa controls, buyer dependencies and local execution evidence.
Review access, data, supplier, employee, operations and reporting controls across the carved-out perimeter.
Document findings where shared ownership or evidence boundaries are unclear.

milestones.name: TSA control and exit evidence assessed (4 weeks)
activities: Assess TSA service levels, reporting, issue escalation, control evidence, exit criteria and buyer readiness evidence.
Review whether TSA defects could extend Absa obligations or residual risk.
Validate closure evidence for findings linked to TSA entry or exit.

milestones.name: Partial sale assurance view issued (2 weeks)
activities: Provide assurance findings across retained business, transferred perimeter, TSA services and local country activity.
Identify readiness conditions and evidence gaps for LD1 and TSA governance.
Confirm residual findings have buyer, Absa BAU or TSA owners.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Sale A (buyer integrates) - further additional divestment activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Buyer integration dependency assurance completed (4 weeks)
activities: Assess Absa evidence that supports buyer integration while protecting retained Absa controls, data and confidentiality.
Review buyer integration dependencies that affect Absa TSA services, exit controls or residual obligations.
Raise findings where buyer readiness evidence is insufficient for Absa to reduce support safely.

milestones.name: Absa exit control assurance completed (4 weeks)
activities: Assess access removal, interface changes, retained-system controls, data separation, supplier exits and post-LD1 support evidence.
Review assurance evidence over retained customer, operational, regulatory and financial controls.
Validate remediation closure for findings that affect Absa retained obligations.

milestones.name: Post-LD1 assurance handover completed (2 weeks)
activities: Provide findings and residual concerns into TSA, BAU or post-completion obligation governance.
Confirm open findings have accountable buyer, Absa BAU or legal obligation owners.
Archive assurance evidence for audit, regulator and dispute support.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Sale B (standalone) - complete divestment activity set

milestones.name: Buyer standalone readiness evidence assessed (4 weeks)
activities: Assess buyer standalone evidence where Absa remains exposed until service exit or obligation closure.
Review standalone controls, systems, data, suppliers, operations, people, governance and regulator evidence where in scope.
Document limitations where buyer evidence cannot be independently validated by Absa's assurer.

milestones.name: Full separation and Absa wind-down assurance completed (4 weeks)
activities: Assess Absa exit controls, transferred data, residual records, access removal, contract closure and TSA exit evidence.
Review findings that could delay regulatory approval, TSA exit or Absa obligation closure.
Validate management responses and closure evidence for material separation findings.

milestones.name: Final assurance close-out issued (2 weeks)
activities: Issue final assurance findings, residual concerns, closure status and evidence archive for governance.
Confirm all residual findings have buyer, Absa BAU or post-completion obligation owners.
Close assurance activity once evidence, conclusions and management responses are complete.

sizingDrivers: Data migration scope spans a broad range of products
Data in scope for transfer is complex
Significant number of source or target systems exist
Data in scope for transfer contains a large number of records
Buyer or seller Data Migration Team lacks experience
Governance structures within the deal span broad range of the business
Impacted processes are business-critical

internal-audit.keyRole: Provides independent, risk-based third-line assurance over whether programme governance, risk management, controls and readiness evidence are designed and operating effectively across the transaction. Internal Audit reports findings and residual risk through its independent governance route; it does not own programme delivery, remediation or the go-live decision.
responsibilities: Engage early enough to assess the transaction risk profile, define a proportionate audit and assurance plan and allow management sufficient time to remediate findings before LD1.
Maintain independence from programme delivery while obtaining access to governance forums, plans, status reporting, RAID logs, budgets, decisions, testing evidence and accountable executives.
Assess whether programme governance, roles, decision rights, executive accountability, PMO disciplines, reporting and escalation routes are clear and operating effectively.
Review whether material transaction risks and controls are identified, owned, monitored, accepted and escalated through an effective three-lines model.
Perform risk-based deep dives across financial controls, regulatory delivery, technology, cyber, data migration, operations, customer outcomes, people, suppliers, TSA services and business readiness.
Review cutover planning, rollback and contingency, go/no-go criteria, readiness attestations, evidence quality and residual risk presented to decision-makers.
Issue findings in real time, agree accountable management actions and due dates, escalate overdue or material items and independently validate closure evidence.
Provide a clear independent view of residual risk entering LD1 and complete post-go-live review, handover and lessons learned where within approved scope.
boundaryItems: The Central Hub and workstreams own governance and delivery controls; Internal Audit independently assesses them and does not design or operate remediation.
Risk owns second-line risk oversight and acceptance processes; Internal Audit provides third-line assurance over the adequacy and effectiveness of risk management and controls.

Independent Assurance / External Audit performs its commissioned external assurance scope; Internal Audit retains its own mandate, reporting line and professional judgement while coordinating coverage to reduce unnecessary duplication.
E2E Testing and Data Migration own test and migration execution and evidence; Internal Audit assesses governance, coverage, control performance, exceptions and readiness conclusions.
Accountable executives and programme governance make go/no-go and risk acceptance decisions; Internal Audit provides independent findings and a residual-risk view to inform those decisions.
internal-audit.centralHubRelationship: Relationship with Central Hub: the Central Hub provides integrated programme information, evidence access and remediation coordination; Internal Audit independently sets and executes its approved scope, reports findings through audit governance and escalates material concerns without becoming part of programme management.
regionalRelationship: Regional Spokes should own management responses, evidence production and remediation execution for in-country findings where they have the authority, capability and capacity.

Function Authority and Group Internal Audit retain audit scoping, methodology, rating, reporting, closure validation and specialist review where regional audit maturity, independence, capability or capacity is insufficient.

As regional maturity increases, local Internal Audit teams may perform delegated fieldwork and follow-up, while Group Internal Audit retains consolidated coverage, quality review and reporting for transaction-wide risks.

Issue findings early enough for management to correct fragmented accountability or weak programme controls.

milestones.name: Critical control and readiness deep dives completed (8 weeks)
activities: Select risk-based reviews across financial, regulatory, operational, technology, data, customer and supplier controls.

milestones.name: Data migration, testing and rehearsal assurance completed (8 weeks)
activities: Review migration reconciliation, transformation controls, exceptions, test coverage, defect severity and evidence retention.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Acquisition A (integrated) - further additional activities

milestones.name: Enterprise testing and cutover assurance completed (10 weeks)
activities: Assess end-to-end test coverage, non-functional testing, defect management, environment readiness and evidence quality.

milestoneIntro: The key milestones below are organised as a baseline set, with additional milestones required for more complex deal archetypes split out below as required.

As deal archetypes scale from balance sheet to partial business to full business, each baseline activity should be assessed against the complexity factors laid out in the deal archetype documentation.

activitySets.heading: Balance Sheet Acquisition - baseline activities

milestones.name: Client readiness criteria and population confirmed (2 weeks)
activities: Define which clients, accounts, products and channels must be ready to transact on LD1.
Agree evidence standards for onboarding documentation, Operations onboarding status, training and channel setup.
Establish the client readiness tracker, owner model, update cadence and escalation route.

milestones.name: Client documentation and contact tracker mobilised (3 weeks)
activities: Identify required client documentation, mandates, forms, consents and contact points.
Track client outreach, document receipt, missing information and ageing exceptions.
Escalate missing documentation or client non-response to Operations, Relationship teams and governance forums.

milestones.name: Operations onboarding progress tracked (3 weeks)
activities: Track onboarding status across Operations queues without taking execution ownership from Operations.
Monitor blockers, rejected submissions, rework, dependencies and expected completion dates by client cohort.
Maintain a consolidated view of clients ready, not ready or conditionally ready for LD1.

milestones.name: Channel setup and client training tracked (3 weeks)
activities: Track channel and platform setup, entitlements, credentials, limits and access dependencies.
Support preparation of client training materials and track delivery by client or cohort.
Record training completion, outstanding attendance, client questions and support needs.

milestones.name: Client transactability confirmed for LD1 (1 week)
activities: Prepare the client readiness input to go/no-go, including ready/not-ready status and residual conditions.
Confirm treatment for clients not ready to transact, including manual workarounds or post-LD1 follow-up.
Hand over open client readiness items to Operations, Relationship teams and hypercare owners.

activitySets.heading: Partial Business Acquisition - additional activities

milestones.name: Expanded client readiness perimeter agreed (2 weeks)
activities: Segment transferred, retained and shared clients by product, geography, channel and relationship owner.
Map client readiness dependencies across seller, Absa, Operations, regional teams and any TSA-supported services.
Prioritise high-value, high-risk or time-critical clients for early documentation, onboarding and training tracking.

milestones.name: Client onboarding and training execution driven (4 weeks)
activities: Track bulk client documentation packs, outreach responses, Operations onboarding status and rejected items.
Monitor channel enablement and training delivery across each client cohort and regional execution team.
Drive closure of ageing items through workstream leads while keeping execution with Operations and client-facing teams.

milestones.name: LD1 client readiness exceptions governed (2 weeks)
activities: Maintain an exception log by client, issue, owner, required decision and LD1 impact.
Escalate documentation, training, onboarding or channel setup blockers that could stop client transacting on LD1.
Agree customer treatment, fallback route and post-LD1 owner for clients not fully ready by LD1.

activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

activitySets.heading: Full Business Acquisition A (integrated) - further additional activities

milestones.name: Integrated client readiness plan aligned across workstreams (3 weeks)
activities: Consolidate client readiness inputs from Operations, Channels, Product, KYC / AML, Communications, Change
Define client criticality tiers and the readiness evidence required for each tier.
Align client communications, training, channel activation and Operations onboarding to one integrated readiness plan.

milestones.name: Full client training and channel migration tracked (5 weeks)
activities: Track training material production, client session delivery, attendance, follow-up questions and support needs.
Monitor channel setup, access credentials, tokens, limits, entitlements and client activation evidence.
Confirm support arrangements for clients using migrated or newly enabled channels at LD1.

milestones.name: Client transactability test evidence collected (3 weeks)
activities: Coordinate friendly client validation where required with Operations, Channels and E2E Testing.
Capture evidence that priority clients can access channels, submit transactions and receive expected support.
Drive closure of blockers raised through client readiness checks, testing or rehearsal activity.

milestones.name: LD1 client support and hypercare handover agreed (2 weeks)
activities: Confirm command-centre routes for client questions, transaction failures and channel access issues.
Hand over open client readiness issues to hypercare with owner, due date and customer treatment.
Track first-day client transactability issues until Operations and BAU owners accept ongoing ownership.

activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

activitySets.heading: Full Business Acquisition B (standalone) - new activity set

milestones.name: Standalone client readiness model designed (4 weeks)
activities: Define how the standalone business will prove clients can transact on LD1 across products, channels and regions.
Confirm readiness owners, evidence standards, support routes and escalation forums for the standalone client base.
Map dependencies on seller support, regional teams, Operations, technology, channels and client-facing teams.

milestones.name: Standalone onboarding, training and channel setup tracked (6 weeks)
activities: Track client documentation, onboarding status, channel setup, access credentials and training by client cohort.
Monitor readiness progress for priority clients and clients requiring local, regulatory or product-specific support.
Drive resolution of readiness gaps while keeping execution ownership with Operations and accountable business teams.

milestones.name: Standalone client support and transactability confirmed (2 weeks)
activities: Prepare go/no-go evidence showing which clients are ready, conditionally ready or not ready to transact on LD1.
Confirm fallback handling, client communications and hypercare routes for unresolved readiness exceptions.
Transfer residual client readiness actions to standalone BAU and hypercare owners after LD1.

milestones.name: Client documentation, query and training tracker driven (5 weeks)

milestones.name: LD1 client handoff and support model live (3 weeks)
