legal.keyRole: Legal & CorpDev own the pre-signature process, including DD and legal drafting, as set out in current Absa processes. During execution, CorpDev tracks the business case, Legal tracks CPs and obligations, and both advise the programme on how signed deal terms affect completion, LD1 and post-close delivery.
responsibilities: Run the pre-signing transaction process with the deal sponsor, including origination support, non-binding offer, governance route, advisor mobilisation and deal-team cadence - as per existing processes

Develop and maintain the business case with Finance & Tax, including commercial rationale, strategic benefits, counterparty performance updates, valuation assumptions and value-tracking implications - as per existing processes
Provide ultimate signoff on DD, owned by business areas - as per existing processes

Own the transaction-document route across NBO, SPA, BSA, TSA, disclosure letter, CP schedule, warranties, covenants, indemnities, completion deliverables, standard-template deviations and related legal instruments - as per existing processes
Translate DD mitigations and functional execution requirements into transaction documents. Bring in the Inorganic Change team pre-signature to ensure the migration plan reflects execution reality.
Track CPs, approvals, litigation stays, legal consents, disclosure items, template reviews, product-specific documentation and post-signing obligations through an integrated obligations log.
Track the progress against the business case post-signing through to completion, and escalate risks
Provide legal advice and assurance to Central Hub, programme leadership and functional workstreams on what is permissible under signed documents and applicable country law.
Coordinate external counsel, local counsel and accounting-firm support where specialist depth, jurisdictional nuance or capacity is required, with clear turnaround expectations and escalation paths.

Hand over signed obligations, legal constraints, residual risks, open issues, document deviations and lessons learned to Central Hub, the business owner and BAU Legal / CorpDev owners after completion or LD1.
boundaryItems: Business workstreams own integration or separation execution; Legal & CorpDev supports by converting DD issues and execution requirements into legal terms and advising on signed-document constraints.

Compliance owns compliance interpretation, regulatory approval standards and regulatory-condition execution; Legal owns legal drafting, CP interpretation and legal obligation tracking, with Compliance as a critical dependency on regulatory CPs.

Finance & Tax owns valuation inputs, accounting, tax, completion accounts, funds flow, Group Interchange, TSA charging and financial-control evidence; CorpDev owns the business case and transaction-governance route with Finance input.

Central Hub owns integrated programme discipline, dependency management, weekly stakeholder reporting and Client readiness; Legal & CorpDev owns transaction-document content, CP interpretation and legal readiness evidence
Central Hub owns programme planning, mobilisation, and execution governance post-signature; Legal & CorpDev own pre-signature planning, governance, and mobilisation

Country Legal provides local legal nuance, local counsel coordination, local evidence, local drafting review and local-law advice; SA Legal leads as transaction SME where central drafting, governance and negotiation control are required.
Central Hub should be engaged during DD on acquisitions and early in complex or big-bang disposals so people, customer and operating-model implications are visible before legal terms are finalised.
legal.centralHubRelationship: Relationship with Central Hub: the Functional Spoke owns Legal and CorpDev transaction decisions, legal interpretation, CP tracking and business-case control while the Central Hub sets programme standards, maintains integrated dependency visibility, coordinates weekly stakeholder reporting and escalates transaction-wide issues.
regionalRelationship: Regional Spokes should own local execution as a minimum, with ownership scaling based on maturity, including local DD evidence, local-law advice, local counsel coordination, local drafting review, approvals evidence and local execution constraints where they have capacity and delegated authority.

Function Authority retains transaction drafting, negotiation control, CorpDev deal governance, legal interpretation, CP tracking, business-case control and execution ownership where regional maturity, capability or capacity is insufficient.

As regional maturity increases, local ownership should expand from evidence and local-law input into delegated local counsel decisions, local approval execution and legal readiness activity, with Function Authority retaining transaction consistency, specialist challenge and reserved approvals.

milestoneIntro: The key milestones below are organised as a baseline set, with additional milestones required for more complex deal archetypes split out below as required.

Activities before contract signing reproduce the existing Absa M&A process. They do not change ownership, controls, approvals, DD scope, testing, reporting or governance. The operating-model requirement is limited to involving the relevant Business Area, country, integration and functional specialists at the appropriate point, subject to confidentiality, and handing DD risks and obligations into execution.
Pre-signature timing remains determined by the existing transaction process and deal timetable.
Service catalogue:
serviceCatalogue: Existing Absa transaction process and GIC governance support
Deal team, insider-list, confidentiality and adviser coordination
Business Area-led due diligence oversight, risk register and policy-gap tracking
Transaction-document drafting, negotiation, signing and records management
Suspensive conditions, approvals, consents and obligations tracking
Mandatory Day 1 readiness and completion support
Legal implementation, integration and separation advice
Business-case tracking and post-implementation reporting support

activitySets.heading: Balance Sheet Acquisition - baseline activities

milestones.name: Existing Absa deal origination and governance process completed (as per existing processes)
activities: The Project Sponsor obtains Corporate Development advice on strategy, approval criteria, initial valuation, deal structure and project management, in line with the existing Absa process.

Corporate Development and Group Corporate Legal help establish the Deal Team, governance, insider list, conflict-clearance route, confidentiality controls and adviser model already required by the existing process.

The Project Sponsor includes the relevant Business Area, country, integration and functional representatives early enough to assess execution implications, subject to confidentiality and need-to-know restrictions.

milestones.name: Existing GIC in-principle, offer and business-case process completed (as per existing processes)
activities: The Business Area prepares the in-principle GIC application and Business Case, with Corporate Development guidance and Project Sponsor sign-off, using the existing approval route.
Corporate Development and Group Corporate Legal prepare the offer and engage advisers in accordance with existing mandates and legal policies.
Relevant functional and country specialists provide strategic, financial, tax, regulatory, operational and integration inputs without changing Business Area ownership or existing governance.

milestones.name: Existing Business Area-led DD or risk-assessment process completed (as per existing processes)
activities: The Project Sponsor appoints the DD Leader and Accountable Executives, and Accountable Executives appoint suitably skilled Workstream Leaders and fieldwork teams with adequate capacity.

The DD Leader and Corporate Development deliver the existing briefing, coordinate information requests, maintain the policy-gap analysis and Risk Register, and manage the established reporting and sign-off process.

The Business Area Integration Team and relevant functional and country SMEs participate at the appropriate point so DD risks, policy gaps, remediation costs, waivers and integration matters transfer into execution; they do not alter DD ownership, scope or procedures.

milestones.name: Existing final GIC, negotiation and signing process completed (as per existing processes)
activities: The Project Sponsor submits the final GIC application once the Deal Team confirms that DD is complete, commercial terms are defined and required sign-offs are in place.
Group Corporate Legal, Corporate Development and the Business Area jointly lead contract negotiation under their existing mandates, with relevant legal and functional specialists providing inputs.
Before signing, the Deal Team signs off the current Risk Register and confirms that contractual mitigants, integration actions and required announcements are addressed through the existing process.

milestones.name: Integration specialists included in the existing DD process (timing determined by transaction)
activities: Include the Central Hub Integration / Inorganic Growth Team and relevant Technology, Data, Operations, Product, Human Capital, Finance, Risk, Compliance, Procurement and CRES specialists where the transaction scope requires them.
Use existing DD scopes and reports to identify policy-conformance gaps, implementation constraints, synergy dependencies and remediation costs.
Ensure the DD Leader hands the complete set of integration matters, Risk Register items and contractual mitigants to the Integration Leader before execution mobilisation.

milestones.name: Suspensive conditions and legal obligations mobilised (as per existing processes)
activities: Translate each suspensive condition, approval, consent, undertaking and completion deliverable into an obligations log with an accountable owner, due date and evidence requirement.
Coordinate with Compliance, Risk, Finance, country Legal and relevant workstreams on the operational actions required to satisfy legal conditions.
Escalate any condition, consent or obligation that threatens the completion timetable or requires a Deal Team decision, waiver or document amendment.

milestones.name: Programme legal assurance conducted (ongoing)
activities: Ongoing legal assurance provided to the programme, advising on where CPs and SPA conditions impact execution decisions

milestones.name: Mandatory Day 1 readiness and completion supported (as per existing processes)
activities: Confirm that signed transaction terms, suspensive conditions, mandatory pre-Day 1 requirements, policy gaps, waivers and high-risk mitigations are reflected in the readiness evidence.

Support the mandatory Risk-led Day 1 readiness process; Corporate Development and the Integration Leader document minutes and evidence, with Business Area, Corporate Development, Group Corporate Legal and Risk represented in the decision.
Support delivery of closing documents, legal ownership transfer and completion mechanics, then hand signed terms and open obligations to the Central Hub and accountable execution owners.

milestones.name: Integration obligations and post-implementation reporting handed over (as per existing processes)
activities: The Business Area Integration Team owns implementation; Legal and Corporate Development advise on signed terms, approved commercial principles, policy obligations and permitted variations.
Route any change to GIC-approved commercial principles back through GIC and any change to transaction agreements through the Deal Team before agreement or implementation.

Support the Project Sponsor's post-implementation reporting, including performance against the Business Case, material risks, issues and recommendations, with Corporate Development review before GIC submission.

activitySets.heading: Partial Business Acquisition - additional activities

activities: Confirm mandatory pre-Day 1 procedures, policy implementation or approved waivers, high-risk mitigations and legal-entity readiness.

milestones.name: Standalone implementation obligations stabilised (timing determined by transaction)

activities: Translate conditions, buyer and Absa obligations, approvals, consents, notices and closing documents into a controlled obligations log.

activities: Include the Central Hub Separation / Inorganic Growth Team and relevant Technology, Data, Operations, Product, Human Capital, Finance, Risk, Compliance, Procurement and CRES specialists where the transaction scope requires them.
Use existing DD scopes and reports to identify policy-conformance gaps, implementation constraints, synergy dependencies and remediation costs.
Ensure the DD Leader hands the complete set of integration matters, Risk Register items and contractual mitigants to the Separation Leader before execution mobilisation.

milestones.name: Programme legal assurance conducted (ongoing)
activities: Ongoing legal assurance provided to the programme, advising on where CPs and SPA conditions impact execution decisions

milestones.name: Mandatory Day 1 readiness and disposal completion supported (as per existing processes)
activities: Confirm that DD reports, the Risk Register, contractual mitigants, policy requirements and high-risk separation actions support the readiness decision.
Support the mandatory Day 1 readiness process using the existing attendance, voting, evidence and escalation route.
Support purchase-price or consideration transfer, legal ownership change and closing-document delivery, then hand retained obligations into execution governance.

activitySets.heading: Partial Business Sale - additional divestment activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: TSA and separation obligations translated into execution (timing determined by transaction)
activities: Translate signed TSA, access, information, records, customer-transfer, supplier and service-continuity provisions into executable plans.
Confirm service levels, charging, governance, buyer dependencies, dispute routes and exit dates with accountable owners.
Maintain traceability from contractual terms and DD risks to readiness evidence, residual-risk acceptance and TSA exit.

milestones.name: Retained Absa protections and policy obligations controlled (timing determined by transaction)
activities: Track warranties, indemnities, claims support, retained records, data restrictions, legal privilege and policy obligations.
Confirm interim controls, waivers and retained-service arrangements remain effective through completion and transition.
Hand unresolved buyer dependencies and retained obligations to named BAU owners with clear escalation and closure evidence.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Sale A (buyer integrates) - further additional divestment activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Buyer handover and Absa exit obligations controlled (timing determined by transaction)
activities: Define the signed-document requirements for data, records, contracts, licences, customer obligations, assets and operational handover.
Confirm buyer readiness dependencies and Absa retained responsibilities are visible in completion and cutover governance.
Escalate any planned buyer-integration action that conflicts with the transaction agreement, confidentiality restrictions or Absa retained protections.

milestones.name: TSA exit and retained Absa obligations closed (timing determined by transaction)
activities: Track TSA services, claims, disputes, retained commitments and legal variations through the agreed transition period.
Obtain Deal Team approval for agreement amendments and GIC approval for changes to approved commercial principles.
Transfer residual actions to BAU owners and support post-implementation reporting on Absa's remaining exposure.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Sale B (standalone) - complete divestment activity set
activitySets.lead: Standalone:

milestones.name: Existing Absa deal, DD and approval process completed for the standalone sale perimeter (as per existing processes)
activities: Follow the existing origination, governance, confidentiality, GIC, Business Case, DD, negotiation and signing process without adding new pre-signature controls.
Appoint the DD Leader, Accountable Executives, Workstream Leaders and fieldwork teams needed to assess the full business and retained Absa exposure.
Include buyer-standalone, country and functional specialists early enough to identify separation, legal-entity, licence, policy, TSA and readiness implications.

milestones.name: Standalone separation perimeter handed into execution (6 weeks)
activities: Translate signed legal-entity, contract, licence, customer, employee, supplier, data, records and governance provisions into the separation plan.
Hand DD reports, the Risk Register, policy-gap analysis, retained obligations and buyer dependencies to the Separation Leader.
Confirm which obligations transfer, remain with Absa or require TSA or post-completion support.

milestones.name: Standalone conditions and buyer-readiness obligations controlled (timing determined by transaction)
activities: Track suspensive conditions, approvals, consents, buyer evidence, completion documents and Absa retained protections.
Coordinate Group and country Legal, Compliance, Finance, Risk and company-secretarial evidence for completion.
Escalate unmet conditions, buyer-readiness gaps or proposed term changes through the established Deal Team and GIC routes.

milestones.name: Standalone sale Day 1 readiness supported (timing determined by transaction)
activities: Confirm mandatory pre-Day 1 requirements, high-risk mitigations, policy actions, waivers and buyer handover evidence.
Support the mandatory Day 1 readiness meeting while preserving the existing voting, evidence and Chief Risk Officer escalation requirements.
Advise Absa and buyer teams on transaction-document constraints through completion, cutover and early hypercare.

milestones.name: Standalone TSA and retained obligations stabilised (timing determined by transaction)
activities: Monitor TSA performance, retained services, claims, legal variations, information rights and buyer dependencies after completion.
Confirm agreement amendments and changes to GIC-approved principles follow the required Deal Team and GIC approvals.
Transfer unresolved obligations, disputes and legal records to accountable Absa or buyer BAU owners.

milestones.name: Standalone disposal post-implementation reporting supported (timing determined by transaction)
activities: Provide Legal and Corporate Development input on disposal performance, retained cost, risk and delivery against approved commercial principles.
Support the Project Sponsor in preparing Post Implementation Reports and obtain Corporate Development review before GIC submission.
Escalate non-performing commitments or residual exposure through GIC and the applicable risk governance route.

milestoneIntro: The key milestones below are organised as a baseline set, with additional milestones required for more complex deal archetypes split out below as required.

As deal archetypes scale from balance sheet to partial business to full business, each milestone should be assessed against client and transaction volumes, process complexity, channel and platform dependencies, data and record requirements, control change, service continuity, operating capacity and the extent of counterparty or TSA support required.
Service catalogue:
serviceCatalogue: Operational inventory, process mapping and fit-gap analysis
Target operating model, client journey and service model design
Operational procedures, controls and exception management
Client onboarding, account, mandate and channel setup execution
Operational data, document and physical-record migration
Operational testing, dress rehearsals, training and readiness evidence
Cutover, blackout, manual workaround and service-continuity management
LD1 support, hypercare, service stabilisation and BAU handover

activitySets.heading: Balance Sheet Acquisition - baseline activities

milestones.name: Current-state inventory and fit-gap assessment completed (5 weeks)
activities: Inventory client journeys, processes, procedures, controls, channels, applications, reports, vendors, records and service teams in scope.
Map client permissions, account and mandate requirements, process hand-offs, volumes, service levels and exception paths.
Identify gaps, duplicate steps, unsupported activities, capacity constraints and dependencies that require remediation before LD1.

milestones.name: Target service model and operating procedures approved (6 weeks)
activities: Define the LD1 client journey, front-to-back process, operating roles, hand-offs, service standards and control points.
Document procedures for onboarding, servicing, transaction processing, complaints, queries, reporting and operational exceptions.
Agree target and interim arrangements with Product, Technology, Risk, Compliance and regional operations owners.

milestones.name: Cutover, discrepancy and manual-workaround plans approved (4 weeks)
activities: Define blackout periods, cut-off times, transaction handling, data freezes, work allocation and command-centre support.
Create controlled procedures for discrepancies, failed onboarding, unsettled items, suspense balances and unsupported system activity.
Approve temporary manual workarounds, compensating controls, volumes, owners, expiry dates and escalation thresholds.

milestones.name: Operational testing, dress rehearsals and training completed (6 weeks)
activities: Execute process walkthroughs, scenario tests and dress rehearsals covering normal, exception, cutover and rollback activity.
Train front-line, servicing, back-office, control and support teams on approved procedures, channels and escalation routes.
Record defects, close critical gaps and provide readiness evidence against the agreed operational acceptance criteria.

milestones.name: LD1 support and BAU handover accepted (6 weeks)
activities: Confirm client, account, channel, product-linking, data, record, staffing and support readiness before go / no-go.
Operate LD1 and hypercare support with clear triage, service reporting, issue ownership and client-impact escalation.
Transfer residual workarounds, defects, service risks and improvement actions to named BAU owners with closure dates.

activitySets.heading: Partial Business Acquisition - additional activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Transferred, retained and shared operations perimeter separated (5 weeks)
activities: Separate transferring, retained and shared processes, client journeys, teams, records, applications, vendors and control responsibilities.
Identify stranded activities, duplicated hand-offs and service dependencies that cross the transaction perimeter.
Agree operational ownership and escalation routes for every shared or ambiguous activity.

milestones.name: Transitional service and third-party operating model agreed (5 weeks)
activities: Define services provided by the seller, Absa, third parties or shared teams during transition, including service levels and controls.
Agree TSA or interim operating procedures, information flows, issue routes, reporting, access and exit milestones.
Confirm vendor, facility, record and technology dependencies with Procurement, Legal, Technology and Finance.

milestones.name: Onboarding, account, channel and data requirements agreed (5 weeks)
activities: Define operational requirements for client onboarding, account and mandate creation, permissions, product linking and channel access.
Specify the data, digital and physical records, reports and reconciliations required to service clients from LD1.
Confirm operational acceptance criteria and ownership across Data Migration, Technology, KYC / AML, Product and Client Readiness.

milestones.name: Onboarding and Client readiness activities executed (8 weeks)
activities: Execute on client onboarding, outreach, and training previously defined
Link in with the Client Readiness stream to drive proper tracking and evidence
Test that client accounts and profiles are set up properly

milestones.name: Client-cohort onboarding and records transition completed (6 weeks)
activities: Plan onboarding, account, mandate, permission and channel activity by client cohort, product, location and priority.
Coordinate digital and physical record transfer, completeness checks, reconciliation and exception resolution.
Track each cohort to operational readiness and escalate gaps that threaten service continuity or LD1 transactability.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Acquisition A (integrated) - further additional activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Integrated target operating model and process harmonisation approved (8 weeks)
activities: Define the integrated organisation, process, location, channel, vendor and service model across acquired and Absa operations.
Harmonise procedures, controls, service levels, client journeys and exception paths while preserving required local variation.
Approve integration waves, interim states, process retirement and ownership of residual legacy activities.

milestones.name: High-volume onboarding and operational data loading completed (8 weeks)
activities: Execute client, account, mandate, permission, channel and product-linking activity at the required scale.
Load and reconcile operational data, static data, open items, digital documents and physical records.
Operate exception queues, quality controls and daily readiness reporting until priority populations are complete.

milestones.name: Integrated operational capacity and control readiness accepted (6 weeks)
activities: Validate staffing, shifts, skills, facilities, vendors, service desks, contact routes and support capacity for forecast volumes.
Confirm integrated controls, reconciliations, access, maker-checker arrangements and management reporting operate as designed.
Complete integrated rehearsals and obtain Operations acceptance for LD1, hypercare and BAU stabilisation.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Acquisition B (standalone) - new activity set
activitySets.lead: Standalone:

milestones.name: Standalone operations governance and service model established (6 weeks)
activities: Define operational ownership, decision rights, governance forums, service catalogue, locations and regional responsibilities.
Set service standards, operational risk limits, escalation routes, readiness criteria and management information requirements.
Confirm which standards and approvals are standalone, regional, Absa group or externally reserved.

milestones.name: Standalone process, control and client-journey catalogue approved (8 weeks)
activities: Document complete front-to-back processes, client journeys, procedures, controls, reconciliations and exception paths.
Define onboarding, servicing, payments, reporting, complaints, records and operational support procedures.
Validate the catalogue with Product, Risk, Compliance, KYC / AML, Technology and local operations leadership.

milestones.name: Standalone platforms, vendors and records model readied (8 weeks)
activities: Confirm required applications, channels, service desks, facilities, vendors, access and operational reporting are available.
Complete operational data, document and physical-record transfer, storage, retrieval and retention arrangements.
Resolve unsupported services through approved build, vendor, TSA or controlled manual solutions.

milestones.name: Standalone workforce, capacity and training plan completed (6 weeks)
activities: Determine staffing, shift, location, skill, leadership and support requirements for forecast client and transaction volumes.
Recruit, transfer, onboard and train operations staff on systems, processes, controls and client-support expectations.
Test operational capacity under peak, incident and degraded-service scenarios.

milestones.name: Standalone cutover and operational rehearsals completed (6 weeks)
activities: Define cutover, blackout, final data, open-item, transaction, rollback and command-centre procedures.
Run end-to-end rehearsals covering client onboarding, servicing, settlement, reporting, exceptions and incident response.
Close critical defects and approve residual workarounds with named owners, controls and expiry dates.

milestones.name: Standalone LD1 launch and service stabilisation completed (8 weeks)
activities: Execute the operational cutover and confirm clients can transact, be serviced and receive support from LD1.
Operate enhanced service monitoring, issue triage, operational reporting and client-impact escalation through hypercare.
Transfer stable operations, residual defects and improvement actions to standalone BAU owners.

activitySets.heading: Balance Sheet Sale - baseline divestment activities

milestones.name: Operational divestment perimeter and retained-service impact confirmed (5 weeks)
activities: Identify processes, client journeys, teams, records, applications, vendors, assets and controls included in the sale perimeter.
Assess impacts on retained Absa servicing, capacity, hand-offs, controls and operational resilience.
Confirm operational dependencies, obligations and evidence required for separation and completion.

milestones.name: Buyer operational diligence and handover pack completed (5 weeks)
activities: Prepare process, service, volume, staffing, vendor, system, record, control, issue and performance information for buyer review.
Validate operational data and descriptions with Product, Technology, Finance, Risk, Legal and regional teams.
Control disclosure of restricted client, employee, security and operational information through approved clean-room arrangements.

milestones.name: Transfer, run-off and closure service model approved (6 weeks)
activities: Define how in-scope accounts, transactions, mandates, queries, complaints, records and open items transfer, run off or close.
Agree client service routes, hand-offs, service levels, cut-offs and exception ownership before and after completion.
Confirm retained Absa operations can continue without unsupported dependencies or control gaps.

milestones.name: People, vendor and records transition plan approved (5 weeks)
activities: Define transfer or retention of operations staff, knowledge, facilities, vendors, access, procedures and support arrangements.
Plan digital and physical record transfer, retention, retrieval, custody and evidence requirements.
Agree third-party consents, contract changes, service continuity and responsibility for transition costs.

milestones.name: Divestment cutover and controlled-workaround plan approved (4 weeks)
activities: Define blackout, final transaction, open-item, data-freeze, account, settlement, rollback and command-centre arrangements.
Document discrepancy, suspense, rejected-item and client-impact procedures across buyer and Absa teams.
Approve temporary services and manual workarounds with controls, volumes, owners and termination dates.

milestones.name: Completion support and retained BAU handover accepted (6 weeks)
activities: Confirm buyer and Absa operational readiness, outstanding exceptions and residual obligations before go / no-go.
Operate completion and hypercare support with service monitoring, issue triage and client-impact escalation.
Transfer retained services, claims support, records obligations and open actions to named BAU or post-completion owners.

activitySets.heading: Partial Business Sale - additional divestment activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Transferred, retained and shared service model separated (6 weeks)
activities: Separate transferred, retained and shared processes, client populations, teams, channels, records, vendors and control activities.
Identify stranded operations, split hand-offs, duplicated activities and services that cannot be separated by completion.
Agree ownership, service levels and escalation routes for every shared or transitional activity.

milestones.name: Operational TSA model and exit plan approved (6 weeks)
activities: Define each transitional operational service, service level, volume assumption, control, reporting requirement and charging basis.
Document operating procedures, access, information flows, incident management, change control and dispute escalation.
Set TSA exit criteria, migration steps, buyer dependencies, testing requirements and accountable owners.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Sale A (buyer integrates) - further additional divestment activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Buyer integration operations handover completed (6 weeks)
activities: Provide approved process, procedure, control, staffing, vendor, record, service and open-issue handover materials.
Agree the transition from Absa-led servicing to buyer-led processes, channels, support and issue management.
Confirm Absa review and escalation rights where buyer integration affects retained obligations or clients.

milestones.name: Absa operational exit and retained-service continuity completed (6 weeks)
activities: Decommission or transfer operational access, facilities, reports, queues, vendor services and support arrangements.
Confirm retained Absa processes, controls, records, staffing and client-support routes continue after buyer integration.
Track TSA services, residual obligations, exceptions and exit actions to accountable owners.

milestones.name: Completion support and operational issue handover completed (4 weeks)
activities: Support completion-day processing, service triage, reconciliations and resolution of client-impacting issues.
Transfer open items, records requests, disputes, claims support and operational exceptions to buyer, TSA or BAU owners.
Archive operational approvals, evidence, handover packs and lessons for future separations.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Sale B (standalone) - complete divestment activity set
activitySets.lead: Standalone:

milestones.name: Standalone buyer operations capability assessed (6 weeks)
activities: Assess buyer governance, leadership, processes, controls, workforce, locations, systems, vendors and service-management capability.
Evaluate whether the buyer can operate the full business and support required volumes from LD1.
Define remediation, TSA or conditional-completion actions for capability gaps.

milestones.name: Full operational handover pack completed (8 weeks)
activities: Prepare complete process, procedure, client-journey, control, service, volume, staffing, vendor, record and issue documentation.
Transfer operating calendars, service standards, management information, escalation routes and operational knowledge.
Confirm buyer acceptance of the handover pack and ownership of open operational actions.

milestones.name: Standalone infrastructure, vendor and workforce model readied (8 weeks)
activities: Confirm facilities, service desks, channels, applications, access, vendors, support and operational reporting are available to the buyer.
Transfer or establish the required operations workforce, leadership, skills, shifts, training and capacity.
Resolve service gaps through approved build, vendor, TSA or controlled manual arrangements.

milestones.name: Client onboarding, operational data and records transfer completed (8 weeks)
activities: Execute transfer of client, account, mandate, permission, channel, product-linking and open-item information.
Transfer and reconcile operational data, digital documents and physical records with completeness and custody evidence.
Resolve exceptions and confirm priority clients and services are operationally ready.

milestones.name: Standalone cutover, blackout and rehearsals completed (6 weeks)
activities: Agree final transaction, data-freeze, record, settlement, reconciliation, rollback and command-centre procedures.
Run end-to-end rehearsals across buyer, Absa, vendor and TSA teams, including failure and degraded-service scenarios.
Close critical defects and approve residual exceptions with controls, owners and deadlines.

milestones.name: Completion, hypercare and final operational exit completed (8 weeks)
activities: Execute operational completion and confirm the standalone business can transact, service clients and manage exceptions.
Operate joint hypercare, service monitoring, reconciliation, incident response and client-impact escalation.
Complete TSA or separation handover, close Absa access and support obligations, and transfer residual actions to buyer and Absa BAU owners.

procurement.keyRole: Owns procurement execution, supplier continuity and third-party contracting readiness for transferred, retained, replaced or transitional services, with country teams owning local supplier nuance and local contract execution where required.
responsibilities: Build supplier, contract, spend, purchase order, renewal, obligation, criticality and dependency inventories for the in-scope perimeter.
Confirm which supplier contracts transfer, terminate, require replacement, need novation, rely on TSA arrangements or remain with Absa.
Apply SA procurement policy and third-party risk standards, with in-country procurement customising execution for local supplier nuance, regulation and contracting practice.
Coordinate supplier categorisation and decisioning with the programme team, including the split between global framework agreements, central sourcing and local vendor onboarding.
Assess outsourcing, resilience, concentration, data, cyber, financial-crime, cost and regulatory third-party risks.
Manage vendor onboarding, supplier engagement, contract replacement, vendor consolidation and supplier exit activity where required for LD1 or TSA exit.
Confirm purchase-to-pay, approval, payment, supplier-management and supplier-risk processes operate from LD1 and through TSA exit.
Maintain visibility of programme decisions that affect supplier timing, contract scope, regulatory approval, information sharing, resourcing or onboarding lead times.
Escalate late procurement involvement, short-notice deadlines, missing supplier information or underestimated resource requirements before they create LD1 risk.
boundaryItems: Legal owns contract drafting, novation legal advice, formal consents and legal restrictions on sharing existing contract information.
Technology owns technical supplier requirements, systems access, cyber integration and technology-service acceptance.
Operations & Servicing owns operational supplier use, service acceptance and day-one continuity requirements.
Finance & Tax owns spend baselining, payment-route design, cost allocation, stranded-cost analysis, Group Interchange charging, recharges and buy-back mechanics.
The Central Hub owns integrated TSA tracking, decision visibility and dependency escalation; Procurement owns the supplier action plan and evidence.
procurement.centralHubRelationship: Relationship with Central Hub: Procurement owns supplier and third-party readiness decisions and evidence while the Central Hub coordinates cross-workstream dependencies, tracks programme decisions, challenges late escalations and holds owners accountable.
regionalRelationship: Regional Spokes should own local execution as a minimum, with ownership scaling based on maturity, including local supplier data, vendor onboarding, local contracting steps, supplier engagement and local regulatory or market nuance where they have capacity and delegated authority.

Function Authority retains procurement policy, sourcing standards, global framework or group supplier decisions, third-party risk standards and execution ownership where regional maturity, capability or capacity is insufficient or a central supplier relationship must be protected.

As regional maturity increases, local ownership should expand from supplier evidence and execution support into vendor onboarding, local contracting and supplier-management activity, with Function Authority retaining central standards, specialist challenge and reserved approvals.
procurement.externalDependencies: External or counterparty dependencies are managed through the Central Hub governance route where supplier data, regulatory approval timing, contract sharing restrictions, buyer readiness or TSA terms affect LD1.

spokeAuthority: Defines supplier inventory standards, procurement scope, third-party risk requirements and supplier readiness evidence.
mandateRows.hubRole: Coordinates dependency mapping and tracks open supplier decisions in the integrated plan.
mandateRows.governance: Procurement workstream lead, business owner, Legal, Risk, Technology, Operations and Finance & Tax.
mandateRows.escalation: Supplier inventory is incomplete, local contract sharing is restricted, or supplier criticality is disputed.

spokeAuthority: Approves sourcing route, supplier categorisation, replacement procurement, vendor consolidation and use of global framework agreements.
mandateRows.hubRole: Ensures programme decisions are visible and aligned to critical path milestones.
mandateRows.governance: Procurement governance, programme SteerCo where timing affects LD1, Legal for contract route.

milestoneIntro: The key milestones below are organised as a baseline set, with additional milestones required for more complex deal archetypes split out below as required.

As deal archetypes scale up in size / complexity (Balance Sheet Partial Full), each baseline activity should be assessed against the Complexity Factors laid out in the Deal Archetypes documentation, and assessed for whether its size or scope increases as a result of deal specifics.
Service catalogue:
serviceCatalogue: Contract inventories
TSA identification and management
Third party risk assessment
Supplier categorisation

activitySets.heading: Balance Sheet Acquisition - baseline activities

milestones.name: Supplier and contract inventory complete (3 weeks)
activities: Identify all suppliers, contracts, POs, renewals and third-party dependencies in scope
Confirm spend, contract owner, business owner, service criticality and jurisdiction
Map contracts that transfer, terminate, require novation, require replacement or remain outside scope
Build and maintain a central supplier inventory and issue tracker
Escalate gaps in source data or unclear supplier criticality
Critical dependency: incomplete supplier or contract data can hide consent, continuity and payment risks that affect LD1

milestones.name: Third-party risk and outsourcing assessment complete (4 weeks)
activities: Classify suppliers by criticality, outsourcing status, data access, resilience, cyber and regulatory exposure
Identify suppliers requiring enhanced review or approval
Track open risks and obtain approvals
Supplier transfer, novation or replacement route agreed
Bucket suppliers into terminations, existing relationships, and new relationships
Define supplier engagement strategy, communications and consent sequencing
Agree replacement sourcing plan where contracts cannot transfer or service terms are unsuitable
Coordinate supplier dependencies with Technology, Operations & Servicing, Finance & Tax on Group Interchange or recharge implications, and Compliance
Document supplier actions in the integrated programme plan

milestones.name: Purchase-to-pay readiness confirmed (3 weeks)
activities: Confirm setup, master data, purchase order routes, approvals and payments
Validate cost centres, tax, details, payment and reporting
Confirm manual workarounds for any purchase-to-pay gaps at LD1

milestones.name: Supplier cutover and readiness complete (4 weeks)
activities: Prepare supplier cutover communications, access changes, service calls and escalation routes
Rehearse critical supplier service continuity and purchase-to-pay steps
Confirm procurement readiness evidence for go/no-go
Monitor supplier issues, payment failures, residual consents and TSA supplier obligations through hypercare

activitySets.heading: Partial Business Acquisition - additional activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of

milestones.name: Partial supplier perimeter separated (4 weeks)
activities: Separate suppliers, contracts, services, data and purchase routes that transfer from those that stay outside scope
Identify shared suppliers, shared contracts and retained services requiring TSA or replacement support
Confirm interim buying channels, supplier access and approval routes for the transferred perimeter

milestones.name: Supplier replacement and TSA actions agreed (5 weeks)
activities: Define supplier services that Absa must build, replace or support through a TSA before LD1
Confirm supplier onboarding lead times, minimum viable service levels and TSA exit milestones
Track partial-perimeter dependencies, blocker closure and regional supplier evidence

activitySets.heading: Full Business Acquisition A (integrated) - further additional activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of

milestones.name: Supplier integration into Absa procurement framework complete (5 weeks)
activities: Map target suppliers into Absa procurement policies, onboarding rules, approval routes and supplier-management standards
Align vendor master data, purchase-to-pay processes, supplier risk ownership and management information
Confirm critical suppliers are embedded in Absa operational resilience and control routines

milestones.name: Vendor consolidation and supplier exit plan agreed (5 weeks)
activities: Identify duplicate suppliers, non-compliant contracts, unsuitable commercial terms and consolidation opportunities
Plan supplier exits, replacements, novations and contract migrations without disrupting service continuity
Track supplier integration defects, TSA exit actions and BAU handover through hypercare

activitySets.heading: Full Business Acquisition B (standalone) - new activity set
activitySets.lead: Standalone:

milestones.name: Standalone supplier operating model defined (5 weeks)
activities: Confirm the acquired business can operate under Absa ownership with its own supplier governance, controls and reporting
Identify critical suppliers, outsourced services, purchase-to-pay routes and management accountabilities
Define oversight model, escalation path, management information and Absa control touchpoints

milestones.name: Supplier and contract inventory complete (3 weeks)
activities: Build full supplier, contract, purchase order, renewal, obligation and dependency inventory
Classify contracts by transfer, novation, termination, replacement, TSA or retained-service route
Confirm supplier consents, change-of-control requirements, pricing impacts and continuity risks
Third-party risk approvals complete
Assess outsourcing, resilience, cyber, data, concentration and financial-crime exposure
Obtain approvals for critical suppliers and document accepted exceptions

milestones.name: Purchase-to-pay and supplier management ready (3 weeks)
activities: Set vendor master data, approval paths, purchase order flows, payment controls and reporting routines
Test supplier access, payment route, service hand-off, incident route and reporting continuity
LD1 supplier continuity confirmed
Rehearse supplier handover, TSA service calls, access changes, payment steps and escalation routes
Confirm readiness evidence, residual risks, open supplier actions and BAU ownership

activitySets.heading: Balance Sheet Sale - baseline divestment activities

milestones.name: Supplier and contract separation inventory complete (3 weeks)
activities: Identify suppliers, contracts, purchase orders, renewals and critical third-party dependencies linked to the sale perimeter
Confirm which suppliers, services, contracts and obligations transfer, remain with Absa or require TSA support
Capture assignment rights, buyer access restrictions, consent requirements, termination rights and retained liabilities with Group Legal
Maintain supplier separation inventory and issue tracker
Critical dependency: missing supplier separation data can create retained liability, stranded cost or buyer-readiness risk

milestones.name: Buyer access and supplier consent plan agreed (4 weeks)
activities: Define supplier information that can be shared with the buyer and any clean-room restrictions
Agree supplier engagement, consent and communication sequencing
Track buyer dependencies, supplier questions and consent status
Retained-service and TSA supplier model defined
Identify supplier services Absa must continue to provide, separate or charge through TSA arrangements
Confirm service scope, service levels, cost recovery, recharge or buy-back mechanics, supplier permissions and exit milestones
Define retained Absa controls, operational hand-offs and issue escalation routes

milestones.name: Purchase-to-pay and retained supplier readiness confirmed (3 weeks)
activities: Confirm payment route changes, vendor master updates, invoice handling, cost allocation and tax dependencies
Validate supplier access, reporting, approvals and retained-service controls before LD1
Supplier cutover and close-out complete
Rehearse supplier notices, buyer hand-off, TSA activation, payment changes and retained-service checks
Monitor buyer queries, retained obligations, supplier issues, stranded costs and close-out actions through hypercare

activitySets.heading: Partial Business Sale - additional divestment activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Shared supplier and retained-service split agreed (4 weeks)
activities: Separate supplier services that transfer from services retained by Absa or shared through TSA arrangements
Identify supplier dependencies across retained and divested products, customers, systems and operations
Confirm buyer dependencies, retained Absa controls and stranded-cost exposure

milestones.name: Carve-out procurement workplan mobilised (4 weeks)
activities: Track contract separation, supplier communications, buyer hand-offs, TSA readiness and retained-business actions
Confirm regional supplier evidence, fallback paths, issue escalation and BAU ownership

activitySets.heading: Full Business Sale A (buyer integrates) - further additional divestment activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of,

milestones.name: Buyer integration supplier hand-off complete (4 weeks)
activities: Provide supplier inventory, service dependencies, contract status and agreed hand-off evidence to support buyer integration
Coordinate buyer supplier onboarding, consent closure, TSA activation and supplier communication controls
Track buyer-readiness dependencies and retained Absa supplier obligations through governance

milestones.name: Absa supplier exit and retained-service controls complete (5 weeks)
activities: Close or amend Absa supplier arrangements where services no longer support retained operations
Confirm stranded-cost treatment, retained supplier controls, TSA exit milestones and BAU close-out

activitySets.heading: Full Business Sale B (standalone) - complete divestment activity set

milestones.name: Standalone buyer supplier operating model assessed (5 weeks)
activities: Confirm whether the disposed business can operate under buyer ownership with standalone supplier governance and controls
Identify supplier services, contracts, purchase-to-pay routes, people, systems, data and TSA reliance needed for standalone continuity
Define buyer supplier governance, reporting, escalation, approvals and management hand-offs

milestones.name: Supplier transfer and replacement route agreed (5 weeks)
activities: Classify suppliers by transfer, novation, termination, replacement, TSA or retained-service route
Confirm supplier consents, pricing impacts, change-of-control requirements and critical-service risks
Track buyer-side replacement sourcing and supplier onboarding readiness

milestones.name: TSA and retained Absa supplier boundaries defined (4 weeks)
activities: Set service scope, service levels, cost recovery, exit milestones, issue routes and retained Absa control obligations
Confirm supplier permissions to provide services to the buyer or standalone entity during transition

milestones.name: Purchase-to-pay and service continuity tested (3 weeks)
activities: Validate buyer access, payment routes, vendor master changes, supplier reporting and incident escalation
Rehearse supplier handover, TSA service calls, payment changes, retained-service checks and fallback

milestones.name: Standalone completion and hypercare managed (5 weeks)
activities: Operate first-day supplier checks, issue triage, retained-service monitoring and buyer query management
Track supplier service continuity, TSA performance, retained Absa obligations, stranded costs and BAU close-out

product.keyRole:
Owns product proposition decisions and functional requirements for the portfolio, business or retained customer base


Note: For more complex deals, each business area or product may have its own workstream (Markets, Payments, Cards, Wealth, etc.). The roles, responsibilities, capabilities, and broad activities herein still apply.
responsibilities: Analyse the transferring, retained or acquired product set, including terms, pricing, features, eligibility, mandates and controls
Define product build, adaptation, withdrawal, migration, servicing and client-treatment requirements
Own product functional requirements and front-office process design with Operations & Servicing and Technology.
Act as business SMEs to input into testing, client communications inputs and readiness evidence
Lead the business execution of cutover activities to enable client transaction on LD1
Decide product exceptions, remediation or exclusions within delegated authority and escalate product risk
Support Technology in turning product business requirements into actionable technology requirements which support delivery
boundaryItems: Risk / Credit owns risk appetite and credit decisions.
Operations & Servicing owns operational procedures and servicing model
Technology owns system delivery based on business-approved requirements.
product.centralHubRelationship: Relationship with Central Hub: the Functional Spoke owns product proposition and requirements decisions and evidence while the Central Hub sets programme standards, coordinates dependencies and escalates transaction-wide issues.
regionalRelationship: Regional Spokes should own local execution as a minimum, with ownership scaling based on maturity, including product evidence, pricing and terms nuance, customer impact input, local remediation and proposition readiness where they have capacity and delegated authority.

Function Authority retains proposition design, product standards, central product decisions, requirements, exception management and execution ownership where regional maturity, capability or capacity is insufficient.

As regional maturity increases, local ownership should expand from evidence and market input into local product-readiness activity, exception remediation and customer-impact execution, with Function Authority retaining standards, specialist challenge and reserved approvals.

milestoneIntro: The key milestones below are organised as a baseline set, with additional milestones required for more complex deal archetypes split out below as required.

As deal archetypes scale from balance sheet to partial business to full business, each product milestone should be assessed against the transaction perimeter, product complexity, customer impact, regulatory obligations and technology / operational readiness required for LD1.
Service catalogue:
serviceCatalogue: Product inventory, mapping and gap analysis
Product usage, pricing, profitability and terms analysis
Product treatment, exception and client-impact decisioning
Product requirements and acceptance criteria definition
Pricing, billing, reporting and channel readiness inputs
Product SME support for Technology, Operations, Data, Finance, Risk, Legal, Compliance, Communications and Client Readiness
Business SME support for testing, UAT and product-readiness evidence
Product cutover, go-live and hypercare ownership

activitySets.heading: Balance Sheet Acquisition - baseline activities

milestones.name: Product inventory and transaction perimeter confirmed (4 weeks)
activities: Compile all in-scope products, features, accounts, services, channels and customer groups that transfer or require Absa support.
Identify retained, excluded, dormant, unsupported or restricted product variants and the rationale for treatment.
Capture product owners, volumes, usage, revenue, profitability, pricing, operational dependencies and control points.

milestones.name: Product mapping and gap analysis completed (5 weeks)
activities: Map source products to target Absa equivalents or target-state treatments.
Compare product features, terms, pricing, fees, billing, servicing, reporting, channel access, controls and documentation.
Identify gaps, unsupported features, control changes, customer-impact items and dependencies for Risk, Credit, Legal, Compliance, Finance, Operations and Technology.

milestones.name: Product treatment strategy and client impact agreed (4 weeks)
activities: Decide which products migrate unchanged, migrate with changes, require build, require workaround, are grandfathered, are withdrawn or are excluded.
Define customer treatment, pricing / terms changes, client communications inputs, exception principles and approval requirements.
Align treatment decisions with Risk, Legal, Compliance, Finance, Operations, Communications and Relationship teams.

milestones.name: Product requirements and acceptance criteria defined (4 weeks)
activities: Define high-level business requirements for Technology, Operations, Data Migration, Finance, Risk / Credit, KYC / AML and Client Readiness.
Set product acceptance criteria for build, configuration, data, operational process, reporting, client communication and testing.
Prioritise requirements by LD1 criticality, customer impact, regulatory exposure and operational feasibility.

milestones.name: Product build, change and readiness plan mobilised (5 weeks)
activities: Convert product requirements into a tracked delivery plan with owners, dependencies, decisions and evidence expectations, aligned to technology delivery schedules
Track product pricing, billing, reporting, channel, documentation and operational readiness with technology
Agree Product Owner sign-off cadence for design, build, UAT, cutover and residual exceptions.

milestones.name: Product readiness evidenced for LD1 (3 weeks)
activities: Support UAT, friendly client validation or operational readiness checks where product SME input is required.
Confirm that priority product / client cohorts can transact, be serviced, be billed and be reported from LD1.
Sign off residual exceptions, workarounds and hypercare actions with named owners.

activitySets.heading: Partial Business Acquisition - additional activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Product perimeter and shared dependencies separated (4 weeks)
activities: Separate transferring, retained and shared products, client cohorts, product rules, operational processes and channel dependencies.
Identify where products rely on seller services, Absa retained services, shared data, third parties or transition support.
Confirm the boundary between Product, Operations, Technology, Data Migration, Finance and Legal ownership.

milestones.name: Product migration and retained treatment agreed (5 weeks)
activities: Define how each product population will transfer, convert, remain, run off, close, be novated or be serviced under a transitional route.
Agree treatment for in-flight transactions, open commitments, customer instructions, billing, statements, reporting and product documentation.
Document retained-business impacts, customer treatment, exceptions and approvals.

milestones.name: Product and client readiness tracking expanded (4 weeks)
activities: Create a product readiness view by product family, customer group, channel, geography and priority cohort.
Track product decisions, requirements, testing, communications inputs, channel readiness and Operations readiness together.
Escalate product blockers that threaten LD1 client transactability or operational continuity.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Acquisition A (integrated) - further additional activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Product harmonisation blueprint approved (6 weeks)
activities: Define target Absa product set, product hierarchy, proposition changes, pricing approach, client treatment and transition principles.
Agree where acquired products are harmonised, retained temporarily, retired, rebuilt or supported through workaround.
Confirm approvals from Product, Risk, Legal, Compliance, Finance, Operations and Technology governance.

milestones.name: Product rationalisation and post-LD1 roadmap agreed (5 weeks)
activities: Agree which product exceptions, temporary workarounds or retained legacy features remain after LD1.
Define roadmap for product simplification, migration, harmonisation, withdrawal or strategic build after completion.
Hand over residual product actions to BAU product owners and transformation teams.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Acquisition B (standalone) - new activity set
activitySets.lead: Standalone:

milestones.name: Standalone product governance and catalogue established (5 weeks)
activities: Define product ownership, decision rights, governance forums, product hierarchy and approval routes for the standalone business.
Create a complete product catalogue covering terms, pricing, features, customer groups, controls, reporting and support routes.
Confirm which product standards are standalone, Absa-owned, locally owned or reserved for group approval.

milestones.name: Standalone product operating requirements defined (6 weeks)
activities: Define product requirements for servicing, channels, operations, data, technology, controls, documentation, complaints and client support.
Identify product-specific policies, procedures, delegations, mandates, limits and approvals required for the standalone business.
Set acceptance criteria for standalone product readiness and BAU handover.

milestones.name: Product systems, channels and servicing dependencies readied (8 weeks)
activities: Track delivery of product configuration, channel access, operating procedures, reporting, billing, documentation and servicing changes.
Coordinate Product SME input into Technology, Data Migration, Operations, E2E Testing and Client Readiness.
Resolve product blockers, unsupported features and temporary workarounds before LD1.

milestones.name: Standalone LD1 product launch and hypercare executed (4 weeks)
activities: Confirm the standalone product set can transact, be serviced, be controlled and be reported from LD1.
Operate product issue triage and SME support during LD1 and early hypercare.
Transfer residual product actions to standalone BAU product owners.

activitySets.heading: Balance Sheet Sale - baseline divestment activities

milestones.name: Product divestment perimeter and retained business impact confirmed (4 weeks)
activities: Confirm the product set, client cohorts, balances, transactions, rights, obligations and features included in the sale perimeter.
Identify retained products, excluded products, customer-impact items and Absa residual obligations.
Assess impacts on retained business pricing, reporting, servicing, controls and customer journeys.

milestones.name: Product data, terms and client population prepared for buyer process (4 weeks)
activities: Prepare product descriptions, terms, pricing, client population, usage, profitability, reporting and operational evidence for buyer diligence.
Validate product data and business meaning with Data Migration, Finance, Risk, Operations and Legal.
Identify product information that must be excluded, masked or controlled during disclosure.

milestones.name: Product transfer, closure or run-off treatment agreed (5 weeks)
activities: Define whether products transfer, close, run off, remain with Absa, are supported through TSA or require buyer setup.
Agree customer treatment, communications input, notices, documentation, billing, reporting and support implications.
Escalate product exceptions, unsupported features and customer detriment risks.

milestones.name: Retained product servicing and customer treatment protected (4 weeks)
activities: Confirm retained Absa products can continue to be serviced, billed, reported and controlled after divestment.
Agree customer support routes and issue ownership for product queries before and after LD1.
Track retained product dependencies with Operations, Technology, Finance, Risk, Legal and Compliance.

activitySets.heading: Partial Business Sale - additional divestment activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Shared product and client perimeter separated (5 weeks)
activities: Separate transferred, retained and shared product propositions, client cohorts, features, pricing, channels and support requirements.
Identify stranded features, shared servicing, reporting, documentation, billing and customer-impact dependencies.
Agree decision rights for product exceptions and customer treatment across buyer, seller and Absa teams.

milestones.name: TSA and retained product support route defined (5 weeks)
activities: Define product services that Absa continues, stops, transfers or supports through a TSA.
Set product service standards, exit milestones, dependency owners, reporting and escalation routes.
Confirm product terms and customer treatment remain consistent with legal documents and operational capability.

milestones.name: Product carve-out exceptions and client treatment governed (4 weeks)
activities: Maintain a log of product exceptions, unsupported features, customer-treatment decisions and residual obligations.
Escalate exceptions that affect customer outcomes, legal commitments, regulatory obligations or buyer readiness.
Hand over open product carve-out actions to TSA, BAU or post-completion owners.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Sale A (buyer integrates) - further additional divestment activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Absa retained product obligations and exit controls managed (4 weeks)
activities: Track Absa retained product obligations, TSA product services, claims support, data access, reporting and product-control evidence.
Confirm buyer integration does not create unsupported Absa product obligations or customer-impact risk.
Define approval route for product waivers, changes, exceptions and post-completion disputes.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Sale B (standalone) - complete divestment activity set
activitySets.lead: Standalone:

milestones.name: Full product separation and buyer handover pack completed (6 weeks)
activities: Prepare complete product handover pack covering catalogue, terms, features, pricing, client cohorts, data, reporting, controls and open issues.
Define product obligations that transfer, remain with Absa, are supported through TSA or require post-completion governance.
Confirm local and regulatory product requirements with Legal, Compliance, Risk and regional teams.

milestones.name: Product TSA and retained Absa obligations controlled (5 weeks)
activities: Define any product-related TSA services, information rights, reporting, support routes, service standards and exit milestones.
Track retained Absa product obligations, customer support exposure, buyer dependencies and issue resolution through governance.
Confirm product arrangements support customer continuity without creating unsupported Absa obligations.

milestones.name: Product exit readiness and final handover completed (4 weeks)
activities: Confirm buyer readiness, Absa exit actions, product evidence, completion deliverables and support handover before go / no-go.
Advise on product questions during LD1, cutover and early hypercare within agreed obligations.
Archive product decisions, exception logs, handover packs and residual actions for BAU or post-transaction owners.
