risk.keyRole: Owns independent 2LOD risk oversight, risk appetite challenge and programme risk assurance, while business and functional owners remain accountable for 1LOD execution and control operation.
responsibilities: Confirm the 1LOD / 2LOD accountability model at mobilisation: business owns execution and controls; Risk owns independent oversight, challenge and escalation.
Define the role of in-country risk for country-based activity, including 2LOD oversight, local evidence, local governance input and support to central Risk.
Assess risk appetite for the deal, portfolio, product, client, country, sector and transaction route, and present material risk appetite items to board or exco where required.
Establish risk governance, principal risk type coverage, committee routes, evidence standards, risk acceptance process and escalation thresholds.
Challenge due diligence, control mapping, credit exposure analysis, data completeness, data accuracy, remediation actions and readiness evidence from 1LOD teams.
Coordinate risk input to assurance planning, including early scoping of Internal Audit, PwC, Deloitte, KPMG or other external assurers
Maintain independent risk views for signing, CP fulfilment, regulatory submissions, completion, LD1 go/no-go, hypercare and BAU transition.
boundaryItems: 1LOD business, functional and in-country owners own control design, remediation and local execution; Risk reviews, challenges, approves or escalates the residual risk position.
Compliance owns compliance interpretation and regulatory-condition tracking; Legal & CorpDev owns legal drafting and CP tracking; Risk owns the independent risk judgement and risk appetite route.
Independent Assurance and 3LOD Internal Audit provide assurance opinions; Risk should coordinate the overall assurance plan
Data Migration owns migration execution and reconciliation; Risk challenges whether the programme can evidence data completeness, accuracy and control operation.
E2E Testing and Client readiness own test execution and go-live orchestration; Risk challenges success criteria, evidence sufficiency and residual risk acceptability.
risk.centralHubRelationship: Relationship with Central Hub: Risk owns independent risk decisions, risk acceptances, appetite positions and readiness evidence while the Central Hub coordinates governance, issue tracking, integrated reporting and counterparty PMO escalation.
regionalRelationship: Regional Spokes should own local execution as a minimum, with ownership scaling based on maturity, including local 2LOD evidence, local governance input, control-owner challenge, MI and risk issue escalation where they have capacity and delegated authority.

Function Authority retains risk appetite, group risk standards, material risk acceptances, independent challenge, assurance coordination and execution ownership where regional maturity, capability or capacity is insufficient.

As regional maturity increases, local ownership should expand from evidence provision into local oversight, local committee input, readiness challenge and remediation tracking, with Function Authority retaining group standards, specialist challenge and reserved approvals.
risk.externalDependencies: External or counterparty dependencies are managed through the Central Hub governance route where data, buyer readiness, regulator communication, external assurance, audit timing or risk evidence affects signing, completion or LD1.

spokeAuthority: Defines risk governance, risk acceptance route, principal risk type coverage and the 2LOD challenge model.
mandateRows.hubRole: Embeds risk cadence into programme governance and tracks actions to closure.
mandateRows.governance: Risk governance, accountable executive, programme SteerCo, board or exco where appetite requires.
mandateRows.escalation: Ownership between business, country Risk and central Risk is unclear or risk items are bypassing governance.

spokeAuthority: Approves or escalates risk appetite, policy exceptions, waivers and residual risk positions.
mandateRows.hubRole: Maintains plan visibility and tests timing against signing, CP and LD1 milestones.
mandateRows.governance: Enterprise Risk, principal risk type owners, board or exco where required.
mandateRows.escalation: Risk appetite is outside tolerance, data is incomplete, board/exco evidence is not ready or business case risk changes.

spokeAuthority: Owns the risk view of assurance requirements and coordinates the appointment and sequencing conversation with IA, Compliance and external assurers.
mandateRows.hubRole: Maintains the integrated assurance calendar, evidence dependencies and escalation route. Inputs into assurance requirements based on SME knowledge
mandateRows.governance: Risk, Independent Assurance, Internal Audit, Compliance, Legal, Procurement where third-party assurance is relevant.
mandateRows.escalation: regulator-appointed assurance scope overlaps, arrives late

spokeAuthority: Provides the independent risk opinion on mock runs, dress rehearsals, data completeness, digital readiness, cards readiness, controls and residual risk.
mandateRows.hubRole: Coordinates readiness pack, decision forum and open issue escalation.
mandateRows.governance: Client Readiness, E2E Testing, Data Migration, Operations, Technology, Compliance and programme SteerCo.
mandateRows.escalation: Success criteria are undefined, data comfort is not evidenced, or digital/cards readiness creates unmanaged LD1 risk.

mandateRows.area: Risk issue escalation and post-LD1 monitoring
spokeAuthority: Escalates material risks, monitors accepted risks and validates closure through cutover, hypercare and BAU transition.
mandateRows.hubRole: Tracks action owners, reporting cadence and accountable executive intervention.
mandateRows.governance: Risk committees, accountable executive, programme SteerCo, board/exco as needed.
mandateRows.escalation: SteerCos are cancelled, PMO issues are not front-run, residual risk rises, or risk acceptance pressure increases without evidence.

capabilityRows.category: Specific Project Manager required?
capabilityRows.content: Unlikely - simple balance sheet transactions can be coordinated through the Risk lead, and 2LOD risk oversight does not require significant technical coordination. Dedicated programme Risk coordinator or PM could be added as deal complexity increases, governance timelines tighten

capabilityRows.category: Baseline capabilities
capabilityRows.content: 2LOD independent challenge; enterprise risk governance; risk appetite assessment; credit risk assessment; risk acceptance drafting; controls mapping; policy and process gap analysis; data-control review; readiness and go/no-go assurance.

capabilityRows.category: Incremental capabilities by deal archetype / complexity
capabilityRows.content: Principal risk type triage; acquired or sold policy mapping; local 1LOD execution assurance; integration, separation and standalone risk assessment; culture and maturity review; key-person dependency challenge; TSA and retained-service risk assessment.

capabilityRows.category: Specialist capabilities triggered by deal characteristics
capabilityRows.content: Banking credit risk, insurance risk, operational resilience, conduct risk, regulatory risk, financial crime risk, cyber and technology risk, model risk, market and liquidity risk, reputational risk and country risk input where relevant.

milestoneIntro: The key milestones below are organised as a baseline set, with additional milestones required for more complex deal archetypes split out below as required.

As deal archetypes scale from balance sheet to partial business to full business, each baseline activity should be assessed against the complexity factors laid out in the deal archetypes documentation, and assessed for whether its size or scope increases as a result of deal specifics.
Service catalogue:
serviceCatalogue: Risk appetite assessment and monitoring
Controls mapping and remediation
Programme risk assurance
Risk governance set-up and execution
Credit risk assessment and decisioning
Principal risk type SME coordination
Policy, process and data-control waiver management
Risk readiness and go/no-go opinion

activitySets.heading: Balance Sheet Acquisition - baseline activities

milestones.name: Risk appetite and due diligence assessment completed (4 weeks)
activities: Confirm initial risk appetite fit for the portfolio, product, client, country, sector and transaction structure
Request due diligence inputs covering risk policies, control issues and incidents
Assess integration risk into the Absa environment, including risk policies, credit standards, data controls, processes, delegations and required waivers.

milestones.name: Risk governance and rules of engagement established (3 weeks)
activities: Mobilise the Risk workstream with a named 2LOD lead, Enterprise Risk contact and principal risk type specialists as required
Define the risk accountability map, governance cadence, committee route and rules of engagement based on counterparty size, deal complexity and transaction perimeter.
Set evidence standards, committee lead times and escalation thresholds early so governance timelines are not underestimated

milestones.name: Principal risk type and control assessment completed (5 weeks)
activities: Identify the principal risk types triggered by the transaction and engage relevant specialists early enough for formal review
Assess operational resilience, conduct, regulatory, financial crime, cyber, model, reputation, market and liquidity risks where the perimeter or product set requires it
Complete a culture and maturity risk assessment, including key-person dependency and operational capability risks that could affect readiness
Challenge business 1LOD workstream plans for governance requirements, data controls, control evidence, remediation actions and policy or process exceptions

milestones.name: Risk approvals and programme assurance kicked off (3 weeks)
activities: Draft risk acceptances and waivers with clear owners, mitigations, expiry dates, monitoring requirements and escalation thresholds
Secure delegated Enterprise Risk approvals in time for signing, completion and LD1
Validate Central Hub SteerCo risk reporting and challenge understated severity, governance timing or readiness implications
Provide the Risk readiness view for testing exit, completion, LD1 go/no-go and BAU transition evidence packs.
Monitor residual risk through cutover and hypercare, with explicit control over late-stage pressure to accept risk without evidence

activitySets.heading: Partial Business Acquisition - additional activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Partial risk perimeter and dependencies confirmed (3 weeks)
activities: Define the split between transferring and retained risk perimeter across clients, products, controls, policies, systems, services and people.
Assess TSA, shared-service, Group Interchange and retained-service risks created by dependencies between Absa, the seller and the acquired business
Confirm residual risk owners for retained dependencies, Absa interim controls and post-LD1 actions.

milestones.name: Policy, process and control gaps mapped (4 weeks)
activities: Map acquired policies, procedures, delegations and control standards against Absa requirements.
Ensure business has Reviewed 1LOD data-control, access, record-keeping and reporting arrangements for the partial perimeter and any retained seller dependency
Set approval routes for policy gaps, process waivers, control weaknesses and interim operating model exceptions.

milestones.name: Regional and business 1LOD execution model agreed (3 weeks)
activities: Confirm which activities must be executed by in-country teams because local regulation, data access or control ownership requires local execution.
Establish a risk issue cadence with the Central Hub, and businesss 1LOD owners for unresolved partial-integration risks
Confirm KYC / AML, Compliance and credit-control hand-offs for clients, products, records and unresolved cases.

milestones.name: People, conduct and change risks challenged (3 weeks)
activities: Assess culture, maturity, ways of working and key-person dependency risks with HR and Change Management for the transferring population
Challenge customer, conduct, reputational and communications risks where rumours, regulator activity or stakeholder disclosure could affect the market

activitySets.heading: Full Business Acquisition A (integrated) - further additional activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Integrated risk and control framework approved (5 weeks)
activities: Expand principal risk type coverage for the integrated business, including insurance risk where the perimeter includes insurance activity or products
Approve the integrated risk and control framework that will apply after migration into Absa policies, processes, committees and reporting.
Review readiness of each business 1LOD workstream against agreed risk controls, policy requirements and remediation commitments.

milestones.name: External assurance requirements mapped (3 weeks)
activities: Based on programme requirements and regulator stipulations, map required external assurance partners
Engage external assurance partners early to provide consistent advice to programme
Define key focus areas for external assurance, as well as measures of success and links into risk and programme governance

milestones.name: Portfolio risk migration controls agreed (5 weeks)
activities: Map credit policies, rating approaches, delegated authorities, limits, collateral processes, arrears handling and impairment routines into the Absa model
Define migrated portfolio monitoring, risk MI, committee reporting and escalation thresholds for the integrated business.
Approve or escalate the plan for deferred remediation, temporary controls and post-LD1 waiver closure.

milestones.name: Cutover and integration risk tested (4 weeks)
activities: Challenge technology, data migration and operational workstream plans for control design, data quality, resilience, fallback and evidence sufficiency
Assess culture, maturity, management capability and key-person retention risks that could affect the integrated control environment
Conduct cutover and rehearsal risk reviews that test controls, accountabilities, fallback routes and issue escalation.

milestones.name: BAU risk governance and hypercare established (3 weeks)
activities: Align enterprise risk MI, committee cadence, issue escalation and risk ownership with BAU Absa governance.
Recommend the Risk go/no-go position for integration completion based on evidence, residual risk and committee approvals.
Monitor post-LD1 risk remediation, control stability, culture adoption and first risk reporting cycles until BAU ownership is stable.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Acquisition B (standalone) - new activity set
activitySets.lead: Standalone:

milestones.name: Standalone risk operating model established (5 weeks)
activities: Establish the standalone Risk oversight model under Absa ownership, including accountabilities, committees, delegated authorities and escalation routes
Appoint the standalone Risk lead, Enterprise Risk lead and principal risk type specialists required for the business profile.
Confirm whether local regulation or greenfield operations require a full in-country risk and control team to be hired, retained or stood up before LD1.

milestones.name: Enterprise risk and culture assessment completed (5 weeks)
activities: Assess target governance maturity, risk culture, risk appetite framework, policy framework, committee effectiveness and evidence standards.
Complete an enterprise risk assessment covering strategy, conduct, operations, resilience, cyber, financial crime, model, insurance, market, liquidity, reputational and country risks as relevant
Coordinate compliance, legal, customer, regulator, reputation and market-disclosure risks where rumours or regulator communication could create transaction risk

milestones.name: Policy control model ready (4 weeks)
activities: Determine which risk policies and processes can remain local and which require Absa group overlay, waiver, remediation or approval
Define all risk acceptances, waivers with owners, due dates, monitoring evidence and committee approval route.

milestones.name: Standalone reporting and resilience controls tested (4 weeks)
activities: Define control, reporting, access arrangements between the standalone business, Absa group oversight and retained services
Set risk MI, risk appetite monitoring, escalation, issue and reporting for LD1
Assess OpRes, business continuity, cyber, outsourcing and third-party controls supporting standalone state

milestones.name: Standalone LD1 readiness and hypercare governed (4 weeks)
activities: Secure Enterprise Risk and relevant principal risk type committee approvals before completion and LD1
Provide a standalone LD1 risk readiness opinion covering governance, people, controls, reporting and residual risk
Monitor reporting cycle, hypercare issues, risk acceptances and BAU handover

activitySets.heading: Balance Sheet Sale - baseline divestment activities

milestones.name: Divestment risk governance and appetite view established (3 weeks)
activities: Mobilise Risk workstream with a named 2LOD lead, Enterprise Risk contact and required risk specialists
Define the divestment risk accountability map, governance cadence, committee route and rules of engagement based on buyer profile, counterparty size, sale perimeter
Confirm risk appetite implications for the transferred portfolio and the retained Absa business

milestones.name: Buyer readiness and Absa residual risk assessed (4 weeks)
activities: Assess buyer or counterparty readiness from a risk, control, credit, operational resilience and conduct perspective using evidence agreed through the Central Hub.
Identify Absa residual risk across customer outcomes, complaints, regulatory exposure, reputation, data access, records, controls and retained services.
Validate the Central Hub go/no-go risk pack and challenge understated timing, evidence or residual risk implications.

milestones.name: Data, control handover and retained services risk defined (5 weeks)
activities: Review clean-room, data-sharing, record transfer and control-handover arrangements with Compliance, KYC / AML, Data Migration and Legal & CorpDev
Challenge 1LOD separation plans for continuity, controls, remediation actions and policy exceptions
Define TSA, retained-service and Group Interchange risk controls, including monitoring, issue escalation, exit criteria and residual ownership
Confirm which divestment activities must be executed in country because regulation, data access or local control ownership requires local delivery.

milestones.name: Residual risk approvals and hypercare monitoring maintained (3 weeks)
activities: Draft residual risk acceptances and waivers with clear Absa owners, mitigations, expiry dates and monitoring requirements.
Monitor transferred portfolio issues, buyer questions, retained obligations and Absa residual risk through cutover, hypercare and BAU close-out
Escalate any late-stage acceptance pressure where evidence, owner or mitigation is incomplete.

activitySets.heading: Partial Business Sale - additional divestment activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Retained and transferred risk ownership separated (3 weeks)
activities: Separate retained and transferred risk ownership across clients, products, policies, controls, systems, records, services and people
Assess dependencies between retained Absa operations and the divested perimeter, including shared controls, shared services and unresolved incident ownership
Define risk ownership for shared clients, shared products, historical records, complaints, incidents, litigation support and regulatory commitments.

milestones.name: In-country and buyer standalone capability assessed (4 weeks)
activities: Confirm that the in-country team, buyer team or transitional model can facilitate the standalone business where local execution is needed
Validate buyer or separated 1LOD control evidence before Absa accepts residual risk
Confirm retained-business risk MI, monitoring, reporting and issue escalation after LD1

milestones.name: TSA and retained-service risk boundaries agreed (4 weeks)
activities: Map TSA, Group Interchange and retained-service risk boundaries, including monitoring, escalation routes and exit criteria
Track policy waivers, process exceptions and deferred remediation through enterprise risk committees where residual risk remains with Absa
Route material separation risks to enterprise risk governance before they impact completion or TSA exit

milestones.name: People, reputation and BAU handover risks controlled (3 weeks)
activities: Review reputational, communications and rumour-management risks with Communications, Compliance and the Central Hub
Assess key-person loss, capability gaps and operational people risk
Prepare BAU handover of retained risks, risk acceptances, evidence packs, lessons learned

activitySets.heading: Full Business Sale A (buyer integrates) - further additional divestment activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Buyer integration risk hand-off controlled (4 weeks)
activities: Provide agreed risk information, policy extracts, control evidence and credit portfolio data within approved limits / controls as per SPA/BSA
Challenge the buyer integration hand-off plan for continuity, conduct, controls, complaints, regulatory commitments and customer outcomes
Validate that buyer integration activity does not create unresolved Absa operational, reputational, regulatory or customer risk.

milestones.name: Transferred credit evidence and residual obligations confirmed (5 weeks)
activities: Confirm transferred credit files, collateral records, open risk issues, waivers, impairments and exclusion decisions are complete or clearly retained.
Review Absa residual obligations for TSA services, data access, complaints, historical records, incidents, regulatory queries and litigation support.
Secure Absa risk committee approval for residual risks, retained obligations and any deferred actions before completion.

milestones.name: Late-stage acceptance pressure controlled (5 weeks)
activities: Control late-stage risk acceptance pressure by requiring evidence-based decisions, named owners and agreed expiry dates.
Monitor transition risks, risk acceptances, buyer dependencies and TSA exit conditions through integration hypercare.
Capture risk lessons learned, policy mapping outputs, approval routes and evidence templates for reuse on future divestments.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Sale B (standalone) - complete divestment activity set

milestones.name: Standalone divestment risk governance established (3 weeks)
activities: Establish the standalone risk governance model, including buyer, Absa and in-country 1LOD and 2LOD accountabilities
Identify the target standalone risk function, committees, delegated authorities, policies, risk appetite, MI and reporting capability required for LD1.
Define Absa, buyer responsibilities for policy waivers, controls, incidents and risk reporting

milestones.name: Buyer and in-country capability assessed (4 weeks)
activities: Assess buyer ability to operate standalone business from a risk, control, credit, conduct and resilience perspective
Assess culture, maturity, management capability, key-person dependency and people-risk in standalone business
Confirm OpRes, cyber, outsourcing, business continuity and third-party risk controls supporting the standalone business

milestones.name: Portfolio, policy, data and records transfer controlled (4 weeks)
activities: Map Absa policies, procedures, controls, registers and evidence standards to the standalone risk operating model
Identify regulatory, compliance, conduct, customer, reputation, market-disclosure and country risks that could remain with Absa

milestones.name: TSA, waiver controls agreed (4 weeks)
activities: Define TSA, retained-service and Group Interchange controls, including monitoring, escalation, failures, exit criteria and evidence
Set all risk acceptances, waivers, temporary controls with accountable owners, due dates and approval routes
Secure Enterprise Risk, relevant principal risk approvals for signing, completion, LD1 and any retained Absa obligations

milestones.name: Standalone LD1, hypercare and BAU handover completed (4 weeks)
activities: Verify LD1 evidence for risk governance, local execution capability, reporting, committee operation, controls, people and unresolved residual risk.
Monitor the first risk reporting cycle, hypercare issues, buyer dependencies, retained Absa obligations and TSA exit
Hand over residual risks, records, open actions, risk acceptances, templates and policy mapping outputs to BAU or post-transaction owners.

risk.sizingFactors: Risk sizing should also reflect the number of principal risk types triggered, credit exposure complexity, in-country 2LOD requirements, board or exco appetite route, data completeness and accuracy concerns, external assurance scope, regulator-appointed audit requirements, mock / dress rehearsal complexity, digital readiness and high-volume operational testing such as cards.
sizingDrivers: Complex deal scope requiring extensive risk oversight (multiple entities, geographies, etc.)
High-value or high-visibility deal which must be managed carefully
Deal scope impacts Absa’s fundamental regulatory processes (e.g., funding, capital adequacy, sanctions, AML reporting, etc.)
Multiple regulators involved with significant levels of scrutiny

technology.keyRole: Owns technology delivery required to support the transaction perimeter and target operating model, including environment readiness, architecture, solution design, build, testing, contingency planning, war-room escalation and service transition. Technology also supports capability mapping during due diligence, while business and Product Owners should own the target capability decisions in the future state.
responsibilities: Map current and required capabilities across digital channels, branch channels, core systems, integration points and operational platforms.
Translate business, product, operational, data and control requirements into technology scope, architecture decisions and solution design.
Deliver environments, build, configuration, interfaces, access, non-functional testing, release management and deployment plans.
Coordinate with Data Migration on source and target systems, data feeds, ETL environment needs, extract routines and cutover technical runbooks.
Define technology contingency, fallback, resilience, cyber, access and war-room escalation requirements for testing, cutover and hypercare
Maintain central visibility of resourcing contracts and technology delivery assumptions, including country-owned contract items such as travel, local support and implementation dependencies
Own technology service transition assessment, remediation, post-LD1 stabilisation and handover into BAU technology operations.
boundaryItems: Business and Product Owners own business capability requirements, target capability decisions and acceptance criteria; Technology performs capability mapping and feasibility assessment where Product Owner capability is not yet mature.
Data Migration owns migration logic, data quality, reconciliation and data cutover; Technology owns platforms, environments, interfaces, access and technical cutover.

Procurement owns supplier sourcing and third-party contract actions; Technology owns technical vendor requirements and must input to resourcing, travel and implementation contract terms before commitments are made.
Regional technology teams execute local activity where agreed, but central Technology owns or approves decisions affecting SA-hosted core systems and central accountability.
E2E Testing owns integrated journey coverage and evidence; Technology owns technical testing, environments, defect remediation and release readiness.
technology.centralHubRelationship: Relationship with Central Hub: the SA Functional Spoke owns technology delivery decisions, technical readiness evidence and technology budget or resourcing assumptions where it is accountable, while the Central Hub coordinates dependencies, governance cadence, scope control and escalation.
regionalRelationship: Regional Spokes should own local execution as a minimum, with ownership scaling based on maturity, including local system and infrastructure evidence, access coordination, local suppliers, testing support, deployment prerequisites and country implementation activity where they have capacity and delegated authority.

Function Authority retains architecture, SA-hosted core systems, cyber and access standards, central platforms, budget or resourcing accountability, and execution ownership where regional maturity, capability or capacity is insufficient.

As regional maturity increases, local ownership should expand from evidence and support into local delivery, test execution and deployment activity, with Function Authority retaining standards, specialist challenge and reserved approvals.
technology.externalDependencies: External or counterparty dependencies are managed through the Central Hub governance route where technology data, environments, supplier contracts, access, approvals, buyer readiness or joint testing affect LD1.

mandateRows.area: Capability mapping and target technology scope
spokeAuthority: Maps current and required channel, core-system and platform capabilities where business or Product Owners do not have requisite capabilities
mandateRows.hubRole: Ensures capability decisions are captured in scope, plan, budget and dependency governance.
mandateRows.governance: Business owner, Product Owners, Architecture, Technology, Operations and programme governance.
mandateRows.escalation: Business capability ownership is weak, Product Owner capacity is unclear, or technology scope is being inferred without evidence.

mandateRows.area: Technology solution architecture and delivery route
spokeAuthority: Owns solution design, architecture decisions, lift-and-shift versus build recommendation, environment approach and non-functional requirements.
mandateRows.hubRole: Challenges critical path, dependency impact, scope control and readiness evidence.
mandateRows.governance: Architecture, Cyber, Risk, Compliance, Technology governance and programme SteerCo.
mandateRows.escalation: Architecture exception, cyber risk, target-state conflict, environment gap or local maturity issue threatens delivery.

spokeAuthority: Owns technology delivery resourcing assumptions and should control or approve the technology budget where held accountable for outcomes.
mandateRows.hubRole: Tracks budget, procurement and dependency impacts across the integrated plan.
mandateRows.governance: Technology leadership, Finance & Tax, Procurement, HR where people capacity is required, and programme governance.
mandateRows.escalation: Country-owned contracts omit delivery needs, central Technology is accountable without decision rights, or run-cost uplift is not funded.

spokeAuthority: Approves build scope, release sequencing, environment readiness, test support and defect remediation for technology deliverables.
mandateRows.hubRole: Coordinates cross-workstream readiness, E2E dependency and issue escalation.
mandateRows.governance: Technology governance, change advisory controls, E2E Testing, Data Migration and Risk.
mandateRows.escalation: Testing fails without agreed learning path, change freeze applies, capacity is short or release evidence is incomplete.

spokeAuthority: Defines technical cutover, contingency, fallback, resilience, war-room entry criteria and issue escalation route.
mandateRows.hubRole: Integrates technology cutover into the LD1 command centre and programme go/no-go pack.
mandateRows.governance: Client Readiness, Risk, Cyber, Operations, Data Migration and programme governance.
mandateRows.escalation: Fallback is not viable, technology incident affects wider Absa operations, or local teams make decisions outside agreed mandate.

spokeAuthority: Recommends technology readiness status, accepted exceptions, residual risk and BAU service transition approach.
mandateRows.hubRole: Integrates readiness and exceptions into completion, LD1 and hypercare governance.
mandateRows.governance: Technology operations, service management, Cyber, Risk, accountable business owner and BAU control owners.
mandateRows.escalation: Critical readiness evidence, service support, licensing, support staffing or residual exception remains unresolved at go/no-go.

milestoneIntro: The key milestones below are organised as a baseline set, with additional milestones required for more complex deal archetypes split out below as required.

As deal archetypes scale from balance sheet to partial business to full business, each baseline activity should be assessed against the complexity factors laid out in the deal archetype documentation.
serviceCatalogue: Environment readiness
Architecture decision making and solution design
Technology contingency planning
War room planning and escalation
Technology build based on business or migration requirements
Technology testing coordination and execution
Technology service transition assessment and remediation

activitySets.heading: Balance Sheet Acquisition - baseline activities

milestones.name: Product mapping and capability assessment (7 weeks)
activities: Assess current and required capabilities across digital, branch, core-system and operational channels during due diligence.
Recommend lift-and-shift, build, enhance, procure or decommission options based on target operating model and delivery feasibility.
Confirm that business or Product Owners make capability decisions, with Technology documenting feasibility and implications.

milestones.name: Technology build based on business or migration requirements (8 weeks)
activities: Deliver build, configuration, interfaces, access, reporting, infrastructure and integration changes needed for the deal perimeter, based on capability gaps identified
Coordinate build with Data Migration requirements, supplier inputs, security controls and business acceptance criteria
Track scope changes, budget impact, licensing uplift and support-staff implications from build decisions.

milestones.name: Environment set up & maintenance (7 weeks)
activities: Confirm environments, access, connectivity, test data, release windows and non-production controls required for the transaction.
Identify environment gaps affecting Data Migration, E2E Testing, Operations, Risk, Compliance and Client Readiness
Evidence environment stability, access readiness and support ownership before formal testing starts

milestones.name: Contingency planning & failover readiness (4 weeks)
activities: Define resilience, fallback, rollback, manual workaround and incident paths for technology failure scenarios
Align contingency plans with Data Migration, Operations, Risk, E2E Testing and Client Readiness.
Confirm contingency owners, decision points and evidence before dress rehearsals and go-live.

milestones.name: War room protocol definition and testing (6 weeks)
activities: Define war-room entry criteria, issue severity, escalation route, decision authority and command-centre participation.
Confirm central and country technology contacts, supplier contacts and out-of-hours support arrangements.
Agree which issues enter the war room and which move into backlog or BAU remediation.

milestones.name: Technology testing coordination and execution (6 weeks)
activities: Run technical testing, SIT support, non-functional testing, defect remediation and release readiness checks.
Support E2E Testing with environments, data feeds, technical defect resolution and evidence for go/no-go.

milestones.name: Technology service transition assessment and remediation (3 weeks)
activities: Assess BAU support model, service desk, monitoring, access support, incident management, capacity and run-cost requirements.
Remediate service-transition gaps before LD1 or agree accepted exceptions with accountable owners.
Transfer open technology issues to hypercare or BAU technology operations with clear ownership.

activitySets.heading: Partial Business Acquisition - additional activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Partial technology perimeter and capability mapping completed (4 weeks)
activities: Map capabilities, systems, channels, interfaces and infrastructure split between transferring, retained and shared activity.
Confirm Product Owner or business decisions for capabilities that Technology has mapped
Identify platform enhancements, take-over needs, procurement needs and TSA technology dependencies

milestones.name: Country, contract and resourcing dependencies mobilised (7 weeks)
activities: Review country-owned technology contracts, supplier support and local implementation dependencies
Confirm central visibility of technology resourcing contracts where central teams are accountable for delivery.
Escalate gaps in local maturity, culture or decision discipline to central or joint governance.

milestones.name: Shared platform build, test and cutover route agreed (8 weeks)
activities: Define build and release path for shared systems, retained systems, transferred platforms and integration points.
Test partial cutover, retained service continuity, access controls and data feed readiness.
Agree post-LD1 support and defect ownership across

activitySets.heading: Full Business Acquisition A (integrated) - further additional activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Integrated technology capability model approved (8 weeks)
activities: Confirm required enhancements to existing Absa channels, including digital, branch, core-system and operational capabilities.
Resolve whether required capabilities will be built by Technology, owned by Product Owners or delivered through business-unit digital teams.
Align integrated capability decisions to the target operating model and budget.

milestones.name: Integrated build, licensing impacts delivered (8 weeks)
activities: Deliver build and configuration across applications, interfaces, identity, channels, environments and reporting platforms.
Coordinate procurement and vendor inputs for technology build or support expansion.

milestones.name: Integrated testing, cutover and service transition completed (6 weeks)
activities: Support E2E and dress rehearsal cycles with stable environments, defect remediation and release evidence.
Confirm cutover, fallback, war-room and technology readiness evidence for LD1 go/no-go.
Transition integrated services into BAU support, monitoring and incident management.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Acquisition B (standalone) - new activity set

milestones.name: Standalone technology operating model and architecture designed (6 weeks)
activities: Define standalone systems, channels, infrastructure, integration, support model, security and governance required for the acquired business.
Assess whether to take over existing technology, procure new platforms, build Absa-hosted capability or run interim TSA-backed services.
Confirm decision rights and budget ownership for central and country technology teams.

milestones.name: Core systems, channels and environments stood up (8 weeks)
activities: Build or procure core systems, digital channels, branch channels, access, identity, infrastructure and operational platforms, as required, or assess suitability of existing
Set up environments, monitoring, release processes, service management and cyber controls.
Confirm local infrastructure, contracts, suppliers, resourcing are funded and executable.

milestones.name: Standalone integration and data enablement delivered (8 weeks)
activities: Build interfaces, reporting flows, data feeds and integration patterns required for standalone operation.
Coordinate with Data Migration on ETL environment needs, target-system readiness and technical cutover runbooks.
Validate resilience, access, capacity and performance for standalone volumes.

milestones.name: Standalone test, contingency and cutover rehearsed (6 weeks)
activities: Run technical, non-functional, E2E support, contingency and command-centre rehearsals.
Confirm market-specific testing approach, defect response and readiness evidence.
Update cutover and fallback plans based on rehearsal findings.

milestones.name: Standalone service transition completed (3 weeks)
activities: Stand up BAU technology operations, support staffing, incident management, monitoring and vendor support.
Confirm licensing, support cost and run-cost uplift are reflected in Finance and operating budgets.
Transfer open technology actions to hypercare or standalone BAU owners.

activitySets.heading: Balance Sheet Sale - baseline divestment activities

milestones.name: Technology sale perimeter and exit requirements defined (4 weeks)
activities: Identify systems, channels, access, interfaces, data feeds, infrastructure and services affected by sale
Confirm Absa retained systems, buyer hand-off and technology exit obligations
Assess whether buyer support requires lift-and-shift, extract-only support, TSA services or temporary access.

milestones.name: Buyer-facing technology support and data enablement prepared (8 weeks)
activities: Provide technical input needed for buyer source-to-target mapping, data extraction, access setup and interface understanding.
Confirm confidentiality, security and access controls for buyer-facing technology support.

milestones.name: Absa technology controls and cutover route agreed (6 weeks)
activities: Plan access removal, interface shutdown, retained service continuity, release windows and technical fallback.
Run technical testing and cutover rehearsal for seller-side technology steps.
Confirm readiness evidence for completion, LD1 and post-LD1 support.

milestones.name: Service transition and residual support handed over (3 weeks)
activities: Define post-LD1 support model, defect ownership, service levels and escalation route.
Transfer buyer, Absa BAU or TSA technology issues to the right owner.
Close Absa technology exit actions once retained controls and support obligations are stable.

activitySets.heading: Partial Business Sale - additional divestment activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Shared technology and TSA dependencies mapped (4 weeks)
activities: Separate technology services, systems, access, interfaces and support between buyer, retained Absa and TSA-backed activity.
Confirm local country systems, contracts and support dependencies needed for the carve-out.
Map technology dependencies to Procurement, Data Migration, Operations, Risk and Legal obligations.

milestones.name: Partial separation build, test and access controls completed (8 weeks)
activities: Deliver access changes, interface changes, retained-system controls and buyer hand-off technology changes.
Test shared-service and TSA-supported journeys with E2E Testing and Client Readiness.
Validate that retained Absa systems remain stable and secure after separation.

milestones.name: TSA exit technology path launched (4 weeks)
activities: Define technology actions needed to exit TSAs, remove shared access and close temporary support.
Track buyer readiness and Absa residual technology risks through governance.
Confirm BAU or buyer ownership for post-LD1 defects and residual support.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Sale A (buyer integrates) - further additional divestment activities
activitySets.lead: The above, with the addition of:

milestones.name: Buyer integration technology dependencies aligned (8 weeks)
activities: Agree buyer and Absa responsibilities for integration, access, data, interfaces, environments and support.
Confirm Absa technology support needed for buyer integration without compromising retained controls.
Escalate buyer technology readiness gaps through joint governance.

milestones.name: Absa exit controls and retained service readiness completed (4 weeks)
activities: Execute access removal, interface changes, monitoring updates, retained platform controls and service continuity checks.
Support buyer integration testing where Absa systems or data are in scope.
Confirm technology readiness evidence for TSA entry, TSA exit and Absa retained obligations.

activitySets.heading: Full Business Sale B (standalone) - complete divestment activity set

milestones.name: Buyer standalone technology readiness requirements agreed (4 weeks)
activities: Define the buyer standalone technology capabilities, systems, channels, support, access and data enablement Absa must support.
Agree evidence Absa requires before service exit or obligation closure.
Confirm local country, supplier, security and regulatory technology dependencies.

milestones.name: Full Absa technology separation executed (8 weeks)
activities: Remove access, close interfaces, separate environments, transfer agreed data enablement and shut down temporary services.
Validate Absa retained systems, monitoring, reporting and controls after separation.
Track buyer standalone defects that delay Absa support exit.

milestones.name: Technology TSA exit and obligation closure completed (4 weeks)
activities: Complete transition-service exit actions, service desk handover, vendor handover and residual issue transfer.
Confirm Absa has no unsupported technology obligations, access exposure or run-cost leakage.
Archive technology decisions, designs, test evidence, cutover evidence and service transition records.

sizingDrivers: Net-new technology build required
Cross-collaborative build required across buyer and seller
New environments or configurations required to support the build
Significant in-house tech build required, rather than sitting with a vendor

partnerServices.keyService: Environment readiness
Architecture decision making and solution design
Technology contingency planning
War room planning and escalation
Technology build based on business or migration requirements
Technology testing coordination and execution
Technology service transition assessment and remediation

responsibilities.centralHub: Leads programme control, dependency management and local escalation. Provides more hands-on coordination.
responsibilities.functionalSpoke: Leads functional design, planning, evidence standards and key execution tasks.
responsibilities.regionalSpoke: Provides local data, stakeholder access, market insight and execution support.

responsibilities.centralHub: Maintains central governance, plan control, readiness integration and escalation.
responsibilities.functionalSpoke: Sets standards, reviews local outputs and co-delivers complex tasks.
responsibilities.regionalSpoke: Leads defined local activities and produces evidence for central review.

responsibilities.centralHub: Maintains transaction-wide control, reserved authority and executive reporting.
responsibilities.functionalSpoke: Provides standards, challenge, specialist input and escalation support.
responsibilities.regionalSpoke: Leads local execution, local decision papers and readiness evidence within delegated authority.

mandate.low: SA Functional Spoke directs; Regional Spoke recommends.
mandate.high: Regional Spoke decides within agreed standards.
mandate.reserved: Material customer, risk or regulatory impacts escalate.

mandate.low: SA Functional Spoke decides with local consultation.
mandate.medium: SA Functional Spoke remains accountable; Regional Spoke may recommend.
mandate.high: Regional Spoke may decide locally delegated matters.
mandate.reserved: Group policy, product, risk, legal and finance standards remain reserved.
Scope, budget, timing, LD1, TSA, go/no-go and executive reporting remain central.

mandate.low: Control function decides with local input.
mandate.medium: Control function decides; local team evidences controls.
mandate.high: Local control owners can approve delegated items.
mandate.reserved: Material risk acceptance, legal advice, compliance interpretation and accounting policy remain reserved.

centralisationPrinciples.remainCentralIntro: What should remain central regardless of country maturity:
remainCentral: Group-wide transaction governance, methodology, programme standards, issue escalation and executive reporting.
Material risk acceptance, group policy interpretation, group technology architecture and enterprise-level regulatory decisions.
Cross-border dependencies, transaction-wide readiness, cutover command centre, independent assurance and lessons learned.
SPA execution implications, TSA governance, completion-critical dependencies and cross-workstream dependency management.
centralisationPrinciples.delegatedLocallyIntro: What can increasingly be delegated locally as maturity increases:
delegatedLocally: Local process design, local stakeholder engagement, country-specific regulatory inputs and local execution planning.
Local readiness evidence, local testing participation, client or employee engagement execution and country issue resolution.
Routine operational decisions within delegated authority and within group standards.

crossCuttingMinimum: A named accountable executive and named lead for each activated workstream.
Sufficient protected capacity, with BAU backfill where transaction activity is material.
Basic project-management capability: planning, dependencies, status reporting, issue escalation and evidence management.
Clear delegated authority and an understood escalation route to the central Function Authority.
Local legal, regulatory, cultural and market knowledge.
Documented decisions, handovers, readiness evidence and residual-risk ownership

comms.name: Communications / Marketing
items: Local communications lead with reputation, leak and crisis-management capability.
Stakeholder mapping across regulators, clients, employees, media and other local stakeholders.
Local drafting and adaptation across language, culture, product and communication channels.
Defined approval route and authority for client, employee and public communications.
Client-facing employee briefing and coordination with contact centres and digital channels.
Local brand, campaign and channel-activation capability, including post-LD1 content management.

finance-tax.name: Finance & Tax
items: Country finance lead with transaction and project-management capability.
Local statutory, regulatory-reporting and tax expertise.
Finance data, ledger, reconciliation and process SMEs.
Ability to map local ledgers and policies into Group structures and test migrated finance data.
Integration-cost estimation, budget management and materiality assessment.
Local liquidity, FX, funds-flow, close and cutover capability.
Ability to operate and evidence local recharge, buy-back and TSA charging arrangements.

change-management.name: Change Management
items: Named local change lead with protected delivery capacity.
Local stakeholder, cultural, leadership and workforce-impact assessment capability.
Ability to develop and execute local change, engagement, training and adoption plans.
Coordination across Human Capital, Communications, CRES and business leadership.
Understanding of local unions, employee sentiment and consultation constraints.

compliance.name: Compliance & Regulatory Approvals
items: Established relationship with the local regulator.
Ability to interpret local frameworks and draft and submit notifications or applications.
Knowledge of likely regulatory conditions, evidence requirements and approval timescales.
Capability to track conditions and execute regulatory commitments after approval.
Capacity to respond quickly to regulator questions and escalate central dependencies.

procurement.name: Procurement
items: Named local procurement lead with sufficient capacity.
Complete local supplier and contract inventory capability.
Vendor categorisation, onboarding, screening, third-party risk and dispensation capability.
Local contract-execution and supplier-relationship management.
Knowledge of local tax, recharge and legal-entity contracting implications.
Ability to execute central sourcing decisions and adapt Group policies to local requirements.

ops-servicing.name: Operations & Servicing
items: Accountable local operations lead and relevant process SMEs.
Ability to map local processes, controls, customer journeys and service dependencies.
Workforce, capacity and BAU-continuity planning.
Branch, ATM and other local service-point readiness capability.

product.name: Product / Business
items: Capability to support mapping across products, channels, features and customer propositions.
Understanding of local customer needs, market practices and regulatory constraints.
Ability to translate business requirements into technology and operational requirements with support from central function.
Product acceptance, pricing, profitability and customer-impact assessment capability with support from central function.
Ownership of local product readiness, training and post-LD1 performance.

risk.name: Risk
items: Independent country second-line Risk lead.
Access to the relevant principal-risk specialists, including credit, operational, conduct, resilience and people risk.
Ability to interpret local risk appetite and present material risks to country governance.
Local policy mapping, waiver, exception and risk-acceptance capability.
Readiness challenge and sign-off capability supported by reliable evidence.

data-migration.name: Data Migration
items: Named local data owner and accountable source-system SMEs.
Data inventory, ownership, lineage and source-to-target mapping capability with support from central function
Data-quality profiling, cleansing and remediation.
Extraction, reconciliation and completeness and accuracy validation.
Input into defined success criteria for mock migrations and dress rehearsals.
Cutover support, post-migration reconciliation and data hypercare.

technology.name: Technology
items: Named country technology lead with clear authority and escalation routes.
Local application, infrastructure, channel, interface and technology-contract knowledge.
Local budget, resource, travel and supplier-contract planning.
Environment, connectivity, access and workplace-technology delivery capability.
Test, defect, cutover, contingency, war-room and service-transition capability.

independent-assurance.name: Independent Assurance / External Audit
items: Input into external assurance scope based on deal parameters and local nuance.
Tracking of assurance provider scope to ensure minimal overlap

kyc-aml.name: KYC / AML
items: Country MLRO or empowered financial-crime lead.
Knowledge of local KYC, AML, sanctions and regulatory requirements.
Customer-risk, KYC-file and remediation SMEs.
Screening, PEP, sanctions and transaction-monitoring readiness capability.
Local approval and exception-management authority.
Evidence-based LD1 financial-crime readiness sign-off.

hr.name: Human Capital
items: Named country HC lead and dedicated people-workstream project manager for material deals.
Local employment law, union and consultation expertise.
Organisational design, role levelling, talent, retention and workforce-planning capability.
Reward, benefits, pension and terms-and-conditions harmonisation expertise.
Payroll, HR systems, employee-data and onboarding capability.
Cultural integration and senior employee-engagement capability.
Close coordination with Communications, Change, Legal and regulatory stakeholders.

e2e-testing.name: E2E Testing
items: Named country test lead with authority across local workstreams.
Local business and operational SMEs capable of defining realistic scenarios.
Coverage of local customer journeys, cards, digital channels, branches and regulatory processes.
Test-data and environment readiness.
Agreed success criteria for testing, mock runs and dress rehearsals.
Defect triage, remediation, retesting and evidence management.
Capacity to support repeated rehearsals without undermining BAU.

ld1-readiness.name: Client Readiness
items: Named country client-readiness lead with cross-functional authority.
Client segmentation and end-to-end local customer-journey mapping.
Engaged and trained relationship managers and other client-facing employees.
Local onboarding, servicing, contact-centre and digital-channel readiness.
Readiness metrics, client-impact escalation and complaint-management capability.
LD1 client support and hypercare.

legal.name: Legal & CorpDev
items: Country Legal lead with strong local-law and transaction support capability.
Local due-diligence, drafting-review and legal-risk assessment.
Conditions-precedent and local-obligation tracking.
Traceability from due-diligence findings into transaction documents and execution plans.
Regular collaboration with Group Legal, Compliance, Finance and programme governance.
Local business or commercial SMEs capable of supporting business-owned diligence and business-case assumptions
CorpDev transaction leadership can remain central; the minimum country requirement is informed commercial input and strong local Legal execution.

cres.name: CRES
items: Named country CRES lead responsible for day-to-day estate delivery.
Property, lease, occupancy, facilities and critical-site assessment capability.
Local project management for construction, fit-out, moves and vendor delivery.
Local landlord, supplier, certification and statutory-approval management.
Budget, procurement and investment-governance capability.
Workplace readiness covering access, parking, security, branding and employee experience.
Joint inspection and asset-verification capability for branches, ATMs and transferred premises.
Early mobilisation, ideally allowing approximately six months for material premises changes.

internal-audit.name: Internal Audit
items: Independent country Internal Audit lead or delegated audit resource.
Programme-governance, control and transaction-risk assurance capability.
Ability to review conditions precedent, readiness governance and management evidence.
Sufficient understanding of data migration, testing and cutover to challenge programme conclusions.
Independent reporting and escalation to appropriate audit and country governance.
Findings tracking and independent closure validation.
Early coordination with Risk and external assurers while preserving third-line independence.

maturityDimensions.low: Limited transaction or specialist capability; local team relies on SA SMEs.
maturityDimensions.medium: Competent BAU specialists with targeted transaction support.
maturityDimensions.high: Experienced functional leads able to lead local transaction delivery.

maturityDimensions.low: Limited or no comparable execution experience.
maturityDimensions.high: Repeated M&A, migration, integration or separation experience.

maturityDimensions.low: Low delegated authority and frequent SA approval needs.
maturityDimensions.medium: Delegated authority for routine operational decisions.
maturityDimensions.high: Authority for local functional decisions within group policy.

maturityDimensions.medium: Named leads with some ring-fenced capacity.
maturityDimensions.high: Dedicated local leads and support capacity for transaction delivery.

maturityDimensions.low: Processes poorly documented or inconsistently evidenced.
maturityDimensions.medium: Processes documented with some evidence gaps.
maturityDimensions.high: Stable controls, clear governance and transaction-ready evidence.

maturityDimensions.medium: Understands local requirements and needs central support for complex positions.
maturityDimensions.high: Can lead local regulatory inputs and defend local readiness evidence.

maturityDimensions.low: Data quality issues and manual MI.
maturityDimensions.medium: Usable MI with defined remediation needs.
maturityDimensions.high: Reliable MI, clear ownership and strong reconciliation discipline.

maturityDimensions.low: Requires templates and hands-on drafting support.
maturityDimensions.medium: Can produce drafts for central challenge.
maturityDimensions.high: Can independently produce local plans, evidence and decision papers.

forums.name: Workstream Sessions
forums.objective: Align on key RAIDs within the workstream, and items for escalation to the Transaction Working Group
forums.attendees: Workstream AE, Workstream Lead, Workstream PM (as applicable)
forums.inputs: Workstream L2 Plan, Workstream level RAID log
agenda: Overview of L2 plan, and progress against activities
Review of workstream RAID log, assessment of each item
Agreement on items for escalation and key dependencies
Agreement on where workstream needs support, and items for AE to take away
success: Continuously updated workstream-level RAID Log
Detailed L2 plan tracked consistently
alignment of which RIAD items must be escalated
clear mitigation plans for critical items and escalation paths
remedial: Rebuild or rebaseline the L2 plan where activities, dependencies, milestones or ownership are incomplete or no longer credible
Review overdue and off-track activities individually, agreeing recovery actions and revised delivery dates
Define clear thresholds for which RAID items should be managed within the workstream and which require escalation
Assign a named owner, target date and escalation route to every critical RAID item
Hold targeted working sessions for critical issues that cannot be resolved within the regular workstream meeting
Increase the frequency of progress reviews temporarily where the workstream is materially behind plan or carrying significant unresolved risk

forums.name: Absa Transaction Working Group
forums.objective: To provide visibility of workstream progress, elevating any risks, issues and dependencies to the PMO
agenda: Overview of progress to date and feedback from SteerCo
success: Workstreams arrive at the meeting prepared, with filled out status updates
Cross-workstream discussion happens in the session where dependencies exist
Workstreams ask questions of each other, with minimal central hub input
remedial: Ask for workstream lead / PM contact details to be included on the status reports, and call them directly if not up to standard
Escalate to AEs where traction is not being seen
Request status reports are signed off by AEs before submission to drive accountability

forums.name: Absa Internal PMO
forums.objective: Identify programme-level risks or issues or decisions which must be escalated
forums.inputs: Key RAIDs from Transaction Working Group
outputs: Key RAIDs for escalation to Internal SteerCo or Joint PMO
success: Clear view of key RAIDs established ahead of the meeting
Alignment within the PMO on what the critical issues are
Clear view of next steps for remediation of issues
Minimal ambiguity around RAID impact
remedial: Require every material RAID to state its impact, owner, proposed remediation, target date and decision or support required
Use a pre-meeting PMO alignment session to resolve differences in the assessment or prioritisation of critical issues
Escalate overdue or repeatedly unresolved RAIDs to the Programme Manager and relevant workstream lead
Assign a named owner and deadline to every remedial action before the meeting closes

forums.name: Joint PMO
forums.objective: To provide day to day management of programme planning, execution, and issue resolution between Counterparty and Absa
forums.chair: Absa Transaction Director, Counterparty Transaction Director
forums.attendees: Counterparty PMO / Absa Central Hub PMO
forums.inputs: Key RAIDs identified in Absa Internal PMO meeting
outputs: Key joint RAIDs for escalation to Joint SteerCo
success: Close collaboration across parties
Willingness across both parties to be flexible to suit the transaction
Problems solved in the session, rather than ‘taken away’
remedial: Reinforce shared transaction outcomes, roles and expected behaviours where collaboration becomes fragmented or entity-led
Require issues raised at the meeting to include a recommended resolution, accountable owner and deadline
Review whether meeting membership, delegated authority or ways of working are preventing decisions from being made in the session
Arrange targeted working sessions for recurring issues requiring deeper cross-party resolution

forums.name: Absa Internal SteerCo
forums.objective: To provide the executive leadership with a programme update, ExCo leads to speak to risks and issues where required
forums.decisionType: Make decisions on transaction critical items, even if not usually in their remit under BAU (e.g., budget, resourcing)
forums.attendees: Absa Workstream Executives, TD, Prog. Manager, AE
forums.inputs: Joint SteerCo Pack + Ad Hoc Materials
agenda: Progress against the plan and budget
outputs: Items to focus on at Joint SteerCo
success: Decisions made in the room, based on materials provided
Deep engagement, questioning, and challenge from members
Cross-functional collaboration of executives to support decision making
Prioritised in busy diaries
remedial: Contact members who are not engaging or attending to reconfirm expectations and understand any barriers to participation
Escalate persistent non-attendance or delegation to the Executive Sponsor
Request explicit views from relevant executives during the meeting where sufficient challenge or cross-functional input is absent
Assign named executive sponsors to decisions requiring coordination across multiple functions
Introduce delegated decision-makers where diary constraints repeatedly prevent the correct representation
Escalate decisions that remain unresolved beyond the agreed deadline, with the resulting impact on the transaction clearly stated

forums.name: Joint SteerCo
forums.objective: To provide oversight of joint migration plan, assess readiness to progress to the next stage during programme tollgates, and resolve issues that have been escalated by the Joint Programme Management Office.
forums.attendees: Absa / Counterparty Executive Teams, TDs, Prog. Managers
agenda: Programme progress and unresolved joint programme issues
Change in overall implementation programme strategy if any
success: Decisions jointly debated and made in the room
Robust but respectful debate - not anger or silence
Overall focus on the success of the transaction, rather than personal or entity-specific issues
remedial: Hold pre-alignment discussions between the two executive sponsors where contentious decisions are likely to prevent productive debate
Restate the shared transaction objectives and agreed decision principles where discussion becomes entity-specific or positional
Escalate unresolved decisions through the agreed transaction governance route, with clear options, risks and consequences of delay
Record the rationale for each joint decision to prevent previously resolved issues from being reopened without new evidence
Address persistent unconstructive behaviour directly with the relevant executive outside the forum and agree expectations for future meetings

roles.title: Executive Sponsor (Accountable Exec, AE)
roles.oneLiner: Provide overall strategic direction and drive decision making at the highest levels
roles.responsibilities: Ultimately responsible for the strategic and commercial success of the transaction
roles.mandate: Makes Absa-wide, transaction-level decisions which may materially impact the shape or success of the transaction
prerequisites: Must be empowered to convene top decision makers at short notice
Must be empowered to make decisions which impact the strategic direction of the transaction as a whole

roles.title: Transaction Director (TD)
roles.oneLiner: Senior leader accountable for the successful execution of the transaction. Translates the strategic intent and contractual requirements into an executable programme, establishes the organisation and governance to deliver it, and drives towards successful Legal Day 1
roles.responsibilities: Translating the deal into an executable transaction programme, mobilising the transaction, owning the integrated execution plan, and leading programme governance and decision-making
roles.mandate: Makes transaction-level decisions which are vital for execution, assesses intra-transaction trade-offs, and provides execution-level strategic direction
prerequisites: Must be empowered to make transaction-level decisions related to execution
Must own the budget, to ensure the programme is staffed correctly
Must own the maintenance of the business case, to ensure the programme is tracking effectively
Must be empowered to escalate to executives at short notice on urgent matters
boundaries: Accountable but not responsible for driving execution (Prog. Manager)
Escalates to AE where decisions have a broader strategic impact
Functional decisions on execution-specifics (design decisions, etc.) are made by Workstream Execs

roles.title: Programme Manager / Director
roles.oneLiner: Drives the day-to-day management and control of the M&A programme. Acts as the central point of coordination across the transaction, ensuring that plans, dependencies, risks, decisions and readiness are managed consistently across the organisation.
roles.responsibilities: Establishes and operates the programme management framework, owns and maintains the integrated programme plan, drives cross-workstream coordination and dependency management, runs governance, reporting and decision support, leads the PMO and maintain delivery discipline
roles.mandate: Makes programme-management related decisions, regarding the governance and execution of the plan (e.g. governance cadence, reporting structures, etc)
prerequisites: Must be empowered to define the programme structure and governance
Must be empowered to hold execution teams accountable, regardless of seniority
Must drive plan creation, to ensure plan tracking is achievable and realistic
Must be empowered to escalate to the Transaction Director at short notice on urgent matters
boundaries: Responsible for driving execution, but not the execution itself
Escalates to TD where decisions have a broader programme impact

roles.title: PMO Support
roles.oneLiner: Provides the programme management coordination, administration and control required to support delivery of an M&A deal
roles.responsibilities: Maintains programme plans and milestone tracking, coordinates workstream reporting, maintains RAID logs, coordinates governance and programme forums, supports dependency and cross-workstream coordination, maintains programme documentation and controls
roles.mandate: Limited decision mandate, may make decisions on escalations if execution is lacking
prerequisites: Must be empowered to build relationships with Workstream Leads and hold them accountable, regardless of seniority
boundaries: Responsible for coordinating execution, but not the execution itself
Escalates to Programme Manager where decisions must be made

roles.title: Workstream Exec
roles.oneLiner: Owns the success of the workstream outcomes and is ultimately accountable for their execution
roles.responsibilities: Unblock workstream execution by providing SME input and decision making, support WSL with escalations and senior-level coordination, assure workstream trade-offs and major prioritisation decisions
roles.mandate: Makes workstream-level prioritisation and trade-off decisions, signs off on key design decisions and workstream execution plan
prerequisites: Must be empowered to define the strategic direction of the workstream, aligned to deal objectives
boundaries: Accountable for workstream execution, not responsible
Escalates to AE / TD where trade-off decisions are programme-wide

roles.title: Workstream Lead (WSL)
roles.oneLiner: Defines and manages the backlog of work within their workstream, ensuring alignment with deal objectives
roles.responsibilities: Own workstream scope, detailed plan, outcomes and deliverables. Develop and maintain the detailed workstream plan, mobilise and coordinate functional resources and SMEs, manage workstream risks, issues, assumptions and dependencies
roles.mandate: Can determine workstream-level requirements, and make prioritisation decisions which do not impact overall delivery scope
prerequisites: Must be empowered to define the detailed activities which sit underneath high-level milestones
Must be able to define resource requirements, and prioritise resource capacity
boundaries: Responsible for driving workstream execution, and some of the execution itself
Escalate to Workstream Exec where trade-off decisions must be made

roles.title: Workstream Project Manager
roles.oneLiner: Supports the Workstream Lead by providing project management discipline, including tracking progress, managing timelines, reporting risks and issues, and coordinating across teams
roles.responsibilities: Act as facilitator between the Workstream Lead and technical or operational teams to ensure smooth execution, own the coordination of the L2 plan, own workstream-level governance activities, and preparing WSL to report into Central Hub
boundaries: Responsible for coordinating workstream execution, and some of the execution itself
Escalates to Workstream Lead where any decisions must be made

roles.title: Workstream Team Member
roles.oneLiner: Completes execution tasks within a workstream, and flags RAID items for escalation
roles.responsibilities: Leverage function-specific SME knowledge to execute an plan and milestones, input into requirements and planning, escalate into workstream governance where needed
boundaries: Responsible for actual execution, not decision making

buckets.title: Mobilisation Roadmap Overview
buckets.purpose: Understand the end-to-end mobilisation journey and what needs to be achieved at each stage.
buckets.short: The end-to-end journey, stage by stage.

blocks.title: Tailored, not a timetable
blocks.body: Indicative timing flexes with deal archetype, complexity and transaction context. Use the stages and exit gates as the control, not the calendar.

buckets.title: Mobilisation Principles
buckets.purpose: Understand the core principles that should govern mobilisation on every transaction.
buckets.short: Six principles that govern every mobilisation.

items.title: Prepare before signing
items.body: Mobilisation readiness is built ahead of signature, so day one is a start rather than a scramble.

items.title: Plan from outcomes and readiness
items.body: Plans are built backwards from the outcomes and readiness required, not forwards from available activity.

items.title: Time-box planning
items.body: Planning is bounded, so mobilisation converges on a credible plan rather than expanding indefinitely.

items.title: Make accountability explicit
items.body: Every workstream, output and decision carries a named accountable owner.

items.title: Facilitate the work
items.body: Mobilisation is facilitated with the teams doing the work, rather than written on their behalf.

items.title: Build challenge into mobilisation
items.body: Structured challenge is part of the process, so weak plans are surfaced before execution begins.

buckets.title: Detailed Activities
buckets.purpose: Provide the detailed actions required to move from transaction preparation through to an approved mobilisation plan.
buckets.short: Actions from preparation to an approved plan.

blocks.title: Expandable by design
blocks.body: Each stage above will hold the detailed activity table. Additional activities can be added within these groups without changing the page structure.

buckets.title: Workstream Mobilisation
buckets.purpose: Determine which workstreams need to be mobilised and what each workstream should focus on.
buckets.short: Which workstreams to stand up, and their focus.

dayDetails.title: Establish mobilisation authority
outcomes: Mobilise core transaction leadership, and identify broader leadership requirements
activities: Print this page off as a plan and fill in the key activity owner names.
Confirm the transaction archetype, perimeter, effort size and complexity.

Confirm critical transaction dates to confirm the planning window (Days 11 – 20), including the date of regulatory approval submissions (and whether a migration plan must be attached to these), the LD1 date as envisioned in the SPA or agreed alongside Counterparty, and other critical dates impacting planning (change freezes, legal constraints, long-stop dates, etc).
Name the Executive Sponsor, Transaction Director, and Programme Manager.
Across each of these roles agree on core responsibilities in mobilisation, decision rights and escalation triggers, and the mobilisation phase reporting cadence.

Accountable Executive responsible for contacting & mobilising broader programme leadership, communicating the strategic intent of the deal, as well as interfacing with Absa leadership committees (Board, StratCo, etc).

Transaction Director responsible for onboarding and selecting programme leadership (Workstream Execs) alongside AE based on SME knowledge, defining required governance structures, and leading reporting.
Programme Manager responsible for standing up chosen governance, defining planning requirements, organising logistics, and supporting WS Execs in onboarding broader team members.
Work with the legal team to draft or amend an NDA which can be used to onboard people into the insider list.

Based on deal archetype, perimeter, complexity, and those involved in DD, TD and AE draft a list of required Workstreams, and socialise with CorpDev and Business stakeholders involved in DD for validation.
Structure onboarding materials for these stakeholders, as well as broader team members to be onboarded in future.
Contact the counterparty to understand their programme leadership structure, and set up regular touchpoints.
Create an information request and assumptions log to track key information and inform planning.

dayDetails.title: Stand up the mobilisation team and secure capacity
outcomes: Convert the Day 1 appointments into a functioning core mobilisation team with accepted roles, protected capacity and owned coverage gaps.
activities: Print this page off as a plan and fill in the key activity owner names.

Define the minimum core-team roles needed to run mobilisation, including PMO coordination, Legal or Compliance, technology access administration, people or resourcing support and communications support.
Nominate a named individual for each core-team role, using interim cover where a permanent resource is not yet available.
Issue a concise role card to each core-team member covering mobilisation responsibilities, authority, required availability, escalation route and immediate deliverables.
Obtain explicit acceptance from each core-team member and record any conditions, start-date constraints or delegated responsibilities.
Check availability across Days 2 to 10 against BAU deadlines, leave, regulatory commitments and other change activity.
Agree release, backfill or reprioritisation actions with the relevant line managers where committed capacity is insufficient.
Allocate ownership and response dates for the information requests and assumptions opened on Day 1 without assessing or resolving their substantive content.
Place the agreed mobilisation reporting cadence into calendars and confirm who prepares, reviews and circulates each update.
